GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 34.01 PROPERTY TAX PAYMENTS.
   (A)   Title and authority. This section may be cited as the “Luna County
Single Payment Property Tax Ordinance” or “this section,” and is adopted
pursuant to NMSA § 4-37-1 (being Laws of 1975, Chapter 312) and NMSA § 7-38-38
(being Laws of 1983, Chapter 216).
   (B)   Declaration of purpose. NMSA § 7-37-38 authorizes a Board of County
Commissioners to provide by ordinance that property taxes under $10 are due and
payable in a single payment on November 5 of the year in which the tax bill was
prepared and mailed. It is therefore the purpose of this section to establish
for 1983 and subsequent tax years that property taxes under $10 shall be due
and payable in such single payment.
   (C)   Payment of property taxes. For the 1983 property tax year and all
subsequent property tax years, until changes are required by law or amendment
of this section, property taxes under $10 are due and payable in a single
payment on November 5 of the year in which the tax bill was prepared and
mailed.
(Ord. 7, passed 7-14-1983)
TAX OBLIGATION FOR LAND TRANSFERS
§ 34.15 SHORT TITLE.
   This subchapter shall be known and be cited as the “Luna County Tax
Obligation for Land Divisions and/or Combinations” or “this subchapter.”
(Ord. 76, passed 7-13-2023)
§ 34.16 PURPOSE.
   (A)   The County Assessor is charged with the responsibility of maintaining
current records of property tax assessments. The division of land and
combination of land within the county impedes the Assessor’s ability to
maintain current records of property tax assessments when map code numbers are
assigned to parcels prior to the payment of past due and prepaid property
taxes.
   (B)   Therefore, it is deemed that any lot split, combination, or any other
division or combination of land within the county will only be made on the
Assessor’s records through or by the assignment of the County Assessor’s map
code identification numbers, after the applicant or developer shall have first
obtained a certificate of taxes paid issued by the County Treasurer’s office
establishing that any existing property tax obligations on the land to be
divided or combined are currently paid.
   (C)   Upon request for a certificate of taxes paid, during the current tax
year and when tax rates have not been set or tax bills mailed, payment of taxes
shall be based on the prior tax year’s tax rate and will constitute full
payment of the taxes for the year during which the certificate is issued.
(Ord. 76, passed 7-13-2023)
§ 34.17 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COMBINATIONS OF LAND.
      (1)   Two or more assessments (notices of value) combined for the
convenience of the property owner or the Assessor’s office.
      (2)   Example: same property owner owns two subdivision lots adjacent to
each other and wishes to receive only one assessment from the Assessor’s
office.
   DIVISION OF LAND.
      (1)   Real property broken down into one or more smaller parcels.
      (2)   These divisions of land can be in smaller parcels than defined in
Chapter 156, but cannot be developed or improved on unless Chapter 156 and the
building permit code requirements have been met.
(Ord. 76, passed 7-13-2023)
§ 34.18 ISSUANCE OF CERTIFICATE.
   (A)   In order for a certificate of taxes paid to be issued, all property
taxes due or to become due on the land to be divided or combined, for the
current tax year or any past tax years, must be paid in full to the County
Treasurer.
   (B)   If certificates are requested pursuant to this section for the paid
tax year and tax rates have not yet been set or tax bill have not yet been
mailed, the Assessor shall determine taxes due on the basis of the prior year’s
tax rates. This will constitute full payment of the taxes on the real property
for the current tax year.
   (C)   The Assessor’s office will require a five-business day processing
period prior to the issuance of the certificate of taxes paid.
   (D)   In addition, any property owner transferring ownership during the tax
year has the option of pre-paying property taxes for the current year.
(Ord. 76, passed 7-13-2023)
TAX SALE PROPERTY EMANCIPATION
§ 34.30 GENERAL.
   The county shall consider bidding real property from the State Taxation and
Revenue, Delinquent Property Tax Bureau, tax auction if it can be held for
future sale or if the property is located in an area where the real properly
may be used to meet the operational needs of the county government (including
to be held for possible bundling with other properties for future sales).
(Ord. 103, passed 4-8-2021)
§ 34.31 PROCEDURE FOR PURCHASING AT TAX SALE.
   (A)   Controls.
      (1)   Establishing county interest. The process of establishing the
county interest is the development of an account of interested properties sent
to the State Taxation and Revenue, Delinquent Tax Bureau:
         (a)   The account will be developed by a panel consisting of, but not
limited to, a representative from the County Assessor’s office and the County
Planning Department;
         (b)   A greater number of parcels within the account should be
localized within one to two sections, townships, and ranges. Properties outside
the selected section, township, and range may be purchased; however, it should
be minimized for administrative and planning purposes;
         (c)   A general description of the property, including the exact
location, any structures (above- and below ground), past uses of the property,
location characteristics;
         (d)   Copies of current property tax bills and special assessment
bills; and
         (e)   Properties that have been inventoried by Taxation and Revenue,
Delinquent Tax Bureau for auction may be purchased by the county by using the
controls set forth.
      (2)   Approval by County Manager. The account in Control 1 must be
approved by the County Manager and the Budget and Procurement Director of the
county.
      (3)   Setting a standard bid amount. The county is establishing a
standard bid amount of 4% of taxable valuation set by the Assessor.
   (B)   Request for sale. The account, along with a request for sale, will be
forwarded to the State Taxation and Revenue, Delinquent Property Tax Bureau for
future sale.
   (C)   Non-competition clause. The spirit of this policy is to emancipate
properties within the financial means of the county. No other valid bids must
be made on the property to validate the purchase made by the county.
(Ord. 103, passed 4-8-2021)

NAMING OF COUNTY-OWNED PROPERTY
§ 35.001 PURPOSE.
   (A)   This subchapter shall apply to the consideration of conferring a
specific name to any county owned or operated building, facility, or property,
excluding streets and roads.
   (B)   This subchapter shall also apply when preparing an official comment or
recommendation of the county to other entities, public or private. This
includes contemplating the naming or dedication of buildings, facilities, or
property owned or operated by an entity other than the county.
   (C)   COUNTY OWNED PROPERTY, included within the scope of this subchapter,
includes:
      (1)   Buildings and structures, including overpasses and bridges; and
      (2)   Real property, including open spaces, parks, and undeveloped or raw
land.
   (D)   This subchapter shall not apply to historically registered properties
for which a name has been indicated on a nomination form or accepted for use on
any historic register.
   (E)   This subchapter shall not apply to public art installations that have
been commissioned and/or accessioned with a title that serves as the name of
the artwork.
(Ord. 111, passed 4-27-2022)
§ 35.002 INITIAL PROCEDURE FOR NAMING REQUESTS.
   (A)   Requests to name or rename county owned property must be in writing
and submitted to the County Clerk for consideration by the Board of County
Commissioners.
   (B)   Any county resident, property owner, business operator, or elected
official representing any part of the county may submit a request to name or
rename county owned property.
   (C)   Requests shall include:
      (1)   Map illustrating the property that is the subject of the request;
      (2)   The name of any existing place, street, facility, or property
affected by the request or similar in name;
      (3)   Any common usage names, nicknames for the subject property, as well
as any nearby topographical, geological, or archaeological landmarks;
      (4)   An overview of any public outreach or support for the request;
      (5)   A statement explaining the reason or basis for the request, and
historic, cultural, community, or other significance of the request;
      (6)   Statements of support or endorsement of the request;
      (7)   An overview of any opposition or criticism of the request; and
      (8)   A description of any plans, promotions, advertising, signage,
markers, plaques, and the like anticipated or planned by the sponsor of the
request.
   (D)   Upon receipt, the County Clerk will deliver the request to the Board
of County Commissioners at the County Manager’s office.
   (E)   (1)   Within 30 days of delivery, the County Manager, or designee,
will review the request for completeness and notify the sponsor:
         (a)   The request is complete and has been accepted;
         (b)   The request is not complete, listing the deficiencies, and has
been rejected and returned to the sponsor; or
         (c)   Additional information is requested regarding the request or its
sponsor.
      (2)   Deficiencies or requests for additional information must be
resolved within 30 days or the request will be deemed denied.
   (F)   Accepted requests will be forwarded to the County Historical Society
for review and comment on the historical, cultural, or community significance
and propriety of the request. The analysis and review shall be submitted to the
Board of County Commissioners within 60 days as a non-binding recommendation
regarding disposition of the request.
(Ord. 111, passed 4-27-2022)
§ 35.003 ACTION ON REQUESTS.
   (A)   After expiration of 60 days from submission to or upon receipt of the
non-binding recommendation from the County Historical Society, a public hearing
for consideration of the request shall be scheduled before the Board of County
Commissioners.
   (B)   Notice and hearing shall be in substantially the same manner as the
approval of ordinances.
(NMSA §§ 4-37-6 and 4-37-7)
   (C)   Prior to or at the public hearing on the request, any county resident,
property owner, business operator, or elected official representing any part of
the county may submit a public comment in writing at the County Manager’s
office or at the public hearing.
   (D)   All public comments shall be compiled and made part of the record of
the public hearing prior to the vote of the Board of County Commissioners.
   (E)   After due consideration of the request, recommendation from the County
Historical Society and all public comments, the Board of County Commissioners,
in its discretion, may vote to accept, reject, modify, or remand the
recommendation for additional information, comments, or other requested action.
   (F)   Once approved, changes to the name or dedication of any county owned
property is strongly discouraged and may only be granted when a material and
substantial change in circumstances since the approval of the initial request
or the discovery of previously unknown adverse information that materially and
substantially affects the previously granted approval.
(Ord. 111, passed 4-27-2022)
§ 35.004 FACTORS FOR CONSIDERATION OF REQUESTS.
   When considering the merits of a request to name or rename county owned
property, the Board of County Commissioners shall consider the following:
   (A)   Whether the proposed name is a duplication or creates a confusing
similarity to existing buildings, facilities, cities, or other named landmarks;
   (B)   For requests to rename or remove an existing name, the existence of a
material and substantial change in circumstances since the approval of the
initial request or the discovery of previously unknown adverse information that
materially and substantially affects the previously granted approval;
   (C)   For names of individuals, the honoree must have been deceased at least
one year prior to the request and contributed outstanding civic service to the
county resulting in the well-being and betterment of the county and its
citizens;
   (D)   Whether the proposed named is offensive, vulgar, inappropriate, or
culturally insensitive;
   (E)   The recommendation of the County Historical Society;
   (F)   The direct relation or contextual connection of the proposed name to
the county;
   (G)   Whether the proposed name is one of common usage or colloquial names
attached to the county owned property;
   (H)   Whether the proposed name is based on or related to a distinctive,
predominant, or defining natural or geological feature of the county;
   (I)   Absent a significant historical basis, proposed names must be secular
and/or non-partisan;
   (K)   Whether the proposed name is associated with a historically
significant event in the county;
   (L)   Whether the proposed name reflects broad historical patterns in the
county history;
   (M)   Whether the name is associated with the life or lives of persons of
historical significance in the county, past or present;
   (N)   Whether the name reflects a distinctive achievement in or connected to
the county;
   (O)   Whether the proposed name is connected to an individual or
organization significantly whom facilitated, donated, or bought the county
owned property to be named;
   (P)   If a portion, room, or something less than the entirety of a named
property is the subject of the request, whether the proposed name is consistent
with the overall name of the property;
   (Q)   Whether the proposed name is part of a larger coordinated and planned
effort supported by the community or another political subdivision;
   (R)   Whether the proposed name is consistent with use or purpose of the
subject property;
   (S)   Whether the proposed name engenders a positive public image and is not
unduly divisive or controversial; and
   (T)   Whether the proposed name is free of religious symbols or
connotations, partisan political symbols or connotations, and racist or
discriminatory symbols or connotations.
(Ord. 111, passed 4-27-2022)
COUNTY FACILITY USAGE
§ 35.015 PURPOSE.
   (A)   The purpose of this subchapter is to address non-governmental and
public utilization and scheduling of space owned by the citizens of the county
which is controlled and operated by the Board of County Commissioners of the
county (“BOCC”). Certain county spaces designated by the BOCC as available for
public use may be used by members of the public or organizations as provided by
this rule and other applicable public safety rules.
   (B)   The county is a political subdivision of the state formed for the
purpose of governing the territory and inhabitants therein, and public usage of
the county space is subordinate to that purpose and all costs related to public
usage of the county space shall be paid by the user.
(Ord. 104, passed 7-8-2021)
§ 35.016 POLICY.
   (A)   Applicability. This subchapter does not apply to the county, its
elected officials, employees, agents, or contractors within the regular course
and scope of their duties.
   (B)   Separate agreements. Users who have separate agreements, such as
leases, for county facilities shall be permitted to operate under said
agreements notwithstanding any provision in this subchapter to the contrary.
   (C)   Fees. Usage fees shall be established separately by the BOCC and shall
be calculated to cover the county’s costs associated with the public use of the
facility as well as appropriate security or cleaning deposits.
(Ord. 104, passed 7-8-2021)
§ 35.017 CONFLICTS.
   In the event of conflict with other county ordinances or resolutions, the
provisions of this subchapter shall supersede other previously enacted
ordinances and resolutions unless otherwise stated herein.
(Ord. 104, passed 7-8-2021)
§ 35.018 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   APPLICATION FEE. The non-refundable fee set by the BOCC that must be
submitted along with the facility use application for consideration and
approval of a public and/or non-governmental use of space.
   FACILITY USE APPLICATION. The document that must be completed and submitted,
along with the application fee, requesting permission and scheduling the use of
space.
   INDEMNITY COST. Any additional costs incurred by the county to insure
against or obtain indemnification by users, when necessary.
   LIABILITY COST. The cost of obtaining insurance coverage to cover approved
users and their use of space incurred by the BOCC, and which is paid by the
user.
   NON-GOVERNMENTAL USAGE. The use of space by anyone for a purpose not related
to the governance of the county, as determined by the BOCC, but does not
include exclusive rental or lease agreements between the BOCC and any third
party.
   PUBLIC EVENT. Any planned, organized, promoted, or encouraged gathering or
activity for a specific purpose held on, in, or at the county space by any user
or persons, or entities, not affiliated with the BOCC.
   PUBLIC SPACE or COUNTY PUBLIC SPACE. A specific type of space owned,
operated, or controlled by the BOCC and generally open for public use, such as
Courthouse Park and the County Skate Park.
   PUBLIC USAGE. Use of space by members of the public, external entities, and
other usage not by the county, its elected officials, employees, and agents,
but does not include exclusive rental or lease agreements between the BOCC and
any third party.
   PUBLIC USE PERMIT. A permit issued by or on behalf of the BOCC for the
exclusive use of the county space for a specified date and time.
   REFUNDABLE DEPOSIT. The amount paid by an approved user to ensure compliance
with applicable terms and conditions of use, including post-use cleaning, and
which is subject to forfeiture for material non-compliance with and terms or
condition of use.
   SITE FEE. The cost assessed and paid in advance by an approved user of
space.
   SPACE or COUNTY SPACE. Areas, both inside and out, property, buildings, and
structures owned, operated, or controlled by the Board of County Commissioners.
   TULIP. The Tenant Users Liability Insurance Coverage offered by the county’s
insurer to users covering their usage of space.
   USAGE FEE. All fees assessed for the approved use of space, and may include
an application fee, site fee, refundable deposit, liability cost, and
indemnification cost.
   USER. The person or entity approved for use of space.
(Ord. 104, passed 7-8-2021)
§ 35.019 COUNTY SPACE DESIGNATED FOR PUBLIC, NON-GOVERNMENTAL USAGES.
   Subject to use by the county for governance purposes and BOCC approved
governmental uses, the following space is designated for public usage and non-
governmental usage:
   (A)   Mimbres Valley Special Events Center, with or without kitchen access;
   (B)   The County Courthouse Park:
      (1)   Pavilion;
      (2)   Gazebo;
      (3)   Outdoor restrooms; and
      (4)   Duck downs (south-east park area).
   (C)   Old train depot;
   (D)   Statmax Family Entertainment Center;
   (E)   MVLC Columbus;
   (F)   Courthouse office space;
   (G)   Park Plaza office space;
   (H)   VFD (substations):
      (1)   Florida Mountain;
      (2)   Sunshine; and
      (3)   Cooke’s Peak.
   (I)   County skate park; and
   (J)   Other facilities designated by the BOCC from time to time.
(Ord. 104, passed 7-8-2021)
§ 35.020 PERMITTING PROCESS.
   (A)   Public use permits may vary greatly from facility to facility and will
be issued by the County Planning Department Monday through Friday during
regular business hours.
   (B)   In order to obtain a public use permit, users must first complete and
submit a facility use application along with any fees and supporting
documentation. The application is available from the County Planning Office.
   (C)   Public use permits are issued on a first come/first served basis, but
are subject to priority county use and will be issued no later than two working
days after receipt of a complete public use application.
   (D)   Prior to issuance of the public use permit, the user will be required
to perform a walkthrough of the facility to be used and an inventory and damage
notice signed by the user upon completion.
(Ord. 104, passed 7-8-2021)
§ 35.021 TERMS, CONDITIONS.
   (A)   No space or county property may be used for any public event or
exclusive use without advance issuance of a public use permit by or on behalf
of the BOCC.
   (B)   All usage of space must comply with applicable laws, rules,
regulations, ordinances, and standards, including all those imposed by the
BOCC, and must be permitted as required by any agency or entity with
jurisdiction.
   (C)   Users, as identified on the public use application, will be
responsible for any damage to county facilities, equipment, or property
occurring during the use of the facility.
   (D)   Public events or other large-scale events on, in, or at the county
space will be subject to additional requirements, as determined by the BOCC, or
its designee, which may include security personnel, liability insurance, dram
shop liability coverage, set-up fees, cleaning fees, trash/disposal services,
and other considerations for the protection of public health, safety, and
welfare while on county property and for the protection of county personnel and
property.
   (E)   Public events will require security measures, as dictated by the BOCC,
which may include law enforcement presence, private security personnel,
controlled access, and secure or restricted areas.
   (F)   Public usage may also require additional measures, such as waste
disposal and parking plan/arrangements.
   (G)   (1)   In addition to compliance with all applicable statutes,
regulations, and the rules of the State Alcohol and Gaming Commission, public
events where licensed alcohol service or sales are allowed will require
controlled access to each alcohol sales/dispensing locations, and designated
security personnel at each sales/dispensing locations and each access point.
      (2)   Public events that may be attended by 50 or more persons, based on
venue size, ticketing, or reservations, will require the presence of at least
one security officer.
      (3)   Public events that may be attended by 100 or more persons, based on
venue size, ticketing or reservations, may require fenced enclosures for
outdoor events, security guards manned access control/entry points, pre-entry
screening, bag searches, medical personnel, traffic control, and parking lot
patrol.
   (H)   Additional relevant factors concerning the use of county property are
as follows:
      (1)   Venue location and proximity to sensitive locations, such as
residences, schools, churches, daycares, and the like;
      (2)   Venue amenities in use, such as kitchen, restrooms, multiple rooms,
and the like;
      (3)   Number and location of access points to the venue;
      (4)   Ticketed admission, open to the public admission and reserved
seating;
      (5)   Time of day/night of the public event;
      (6)   Length of public event;
      (7)   Presence of food or beverages, whether sold, served, or allowed in;
      (8)   Set-up and take-down time necessary;
      (9)   Presence of unattended minors or children;
      (10)   Necessity for traffic control and parking management;
      (11)   Affiliated or related events such as a parade, carnival, race, or
rally; and
      (12)   Anticipated presence of dangerous materials or weapons as part of
the event, such as firearms, cannons, explosives, fireworks, hazardous
chemicals, and livestock or other animals.
   (I)   Insurance shall be generally required for all facility users and
alcohol dispensers, but may be waived on a case-by-case basis based on a
determination that potential risks do not warrant requiring insurance.
(Ord. 104, passed 7-8-2021)
§ 35.022 PROHIBITIONS ON USES.
   (A)   County public spaces, namely Courthouse Park and Duck Downs, and the
county skate park, are closed from 10:30 p.m. until 6:00 a.m. daily and, absent
a public use permit issued pursuant to this subchapter, it shall be illegal
(trespassing) for any person to enter or remain on these properties during
closed hours.
   (B)   No space, including, but not limited to, Courthouse Park, may be used
as a residence, a shelter for camping, overnight parking, or other occupancy at
any time and water, electricity, trash receptacles, and other amenities are
provided for users during permit hours and general public use during regular
county business hours.
   (C)   Loitering is also prohibited.
   (D)   All refuse must be placed in trash receptacles or packed out,
including animal feces.
   (E)   (1)   Use of county spaces without a public use permit is non-
exclusive and on a first come, first serve basis.
      (2)   Except for public use permit holders or users, no person or entity
may claim or assert exclusive use or possession of any county space, and any
attempt to exclude others from use or enjoyment of any county space, except
with a valid public use permit, will be deemed a violation of this subchapter
and results in the automatic revocation of the right or privilege to be on, in,
or at that county space for a period of 24 hours, and subjects such violators
to prosecution for trespass.
   (F)   Disorderly conduct, inappropriate behavior, illegal conduct, abuse of
the facility, or damage to property may result in the immediate termination of
the public use permit, and the activity or event occurring thereunder, without
refund and with loss of any deposits.
   (G)   The BOCC, or its designee, namely the County Manager, and his or her
staff, have the unilateral discretion regarding interpretation and enforcement
of the terms and conditions of public use permits, and in the violation of this
subchapter and propriety or necessity of terminating a public use permit and
the activity or event occurring thereunder.
   (H)   (1)   County buildings and facilities are not generally available for
commercial purposes to avoid unfairly undercutting existing private businesses
in the county.
      (2)   However, commercial use may be permitted when such use is limited
in duration and provides sufficient community benefit. Examples of such
allowable commercial use are the Deming Duck Races, Salsa Fest, and Klobase
Barbeque.
   (I)   Golf, archery, and shooting are not allowed at county facilities.
   (J)   Pets must be under the physical control of the person bringing the pet
into the park, and aggressive or menacing pets must be immediately removed from
the county facility.
   (K)   Tobacco, cannabis, unlicensed liquor, and illegal or illicit drugs are
prohibited at county facilities.
   (L)   All persons present at any public event or other activity at a county
facility must be appropriately attired at all times.
(Ord. 104, passed 7-8-2021)

INDIGENT HEALTH CARE PROGRAM POLICY AND PROCEDURES
§ 35.080 INTRODUCTION.
   (A)   Mission statement. The County Indigent Health Care Program’s mission
is to promote the health and well being of residents of the county through
programs which improve access and availability of health care services in the
community.
   (B)   Vision statement. The vision of the County Indigent Health Care
Program is to improve the quality of life in the county by identifying and
addressing the health care needs of the residents of the county through
collaboration with community partners.
   (C)   Introduction. The County Indigent Health Care Program (“IHC”) is a
program administered by the Board of County Commissioners, in its capacity as
the Indigent Hospital and County Health Care Board (“Board”). The IHC program
was established in accordance with the Indigent Hospital and County Health Care
Act, NMSA Chapter 27, Article 5 (1978) (“Indigent Act”).
      (1)   (a)   The program provides assistance to medically indigent
patients (“patients”) who are residents of the county for authorized costs of
ambulance and health care services (“services”) provided by IHC designated
health care providers (“providers”)
         (b)   Providers eligible for IHC funding include in-state ambulance
services and in-state hospitals licensed by the State Department of Health.
Services may include in-patient and/or out-patient hospital services. Out-
patient hospital service may include diagnostics, such as labs and radiology,
limited to Mimbres Valley Medical Center.
      (2)   The Program shall also be utilized for primary care services,
physicians and for other services as deemed necessary by the IHC Administrator
for individuals held at the County Detention Center. This includes providing
for payment of medical claims by individuals committed to the custody of the
County Detention Center.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.081 APPLICANT AND APPLICATION.
   (A)   The applicant must be the patient. If the patient is a minor, a parent
or legal guardian having legal custody must file the application. In the event
of the death of the patient, the applicant shall be either the surviving spouse
or the executor or administrator of the estate. If the patient is
incapacitated, the applicant shall be the guardian, conservator, or other
legally responsible party.
   (B)   The application process and income verification for patients who have
received services by any provider within the county will be processed and
submitted by those institutions in cooperation with the County IHC Coordinator
(s). In some cases, patients may apply directly to the IHC program office, but
in either case, reimbursement is always made to the provider directly.
   (C)   The provider staff shall provide application materials, schedule an
interview with each patient, and provide assistance in completing the
application and verification process. The provider staff shall ensure that the
application is complete and all necessary verification documents to prove
eligibility are attached. The provider staff shall attach a claim statement and
itemized bill to each application and submit the claim to the IHC staff at 700
South Silver Avenue, Deming, NM, 88030. A separate application and claim must
be filed for each patient. No application will be accepted by the provider
staff prior to the patient receiving services. Failure to properly complete the
application or to provide eligibility documentation may result in denial of the
claim. Applications for services by providers outside of the county must be
submitted by the patient directly to the IHC staff for processing.
   (D)   The patient must sign a verified statement of qualification which
shall constitute an oath of the person signing it, and any false statements in
the verified statement made knowingly constitute a felony. All claims and
applications and any information contained therein shall be subject to
verification by the IHC staff.
   (E)   Applications are valid for one year from application date, except in
certain cases where the IHC staff finds that information must be updated with
each claim.
   (F)   Where services have been rendered to a person incarcerated in the
County Detention Center, or to a patient who is unable to provide traditional
documentation to verify eligibility, the program/facility administrator or
representative may attest to the patient’s indigency and residency, provided
that the means of determining eligibility shall be part of his or her record at
that facility and shall be available for auditors upon request.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.082 INDIGENT PATIENT.
   (A)   In order to be eligible for IHC program assistance, a patient must be
medically indigent as defined by NMSA § 27-5-4(G), must be a resident of the
county, and must not be eligible for Medicaid.
   (B)   Individuals committed to the custody of the County Detention Center
shall be considered medically indigent for the purposes of this policy.
   (C)   (1)   A patient who has received services from an IHC designated
provider, and who can normally support himself or herself and dependents on
present income and available liquid assets, but, taking into consideration this
income and those assets and the requirement for other necessities of life for
himself or herself and dependents, is unable to pay the costs of ambulance
transportation or medical services, or both, is defined as MEDICALLY INDIGENT.
      (2)   As provided by the Board of County Commissioners, “It shall not
include any person whose annual income together with his spouse’s annual income
totals an amount which is 50% greater than the per capita personal income,” for
the state as shown for the most recent year available in the survey of current
business published by the U.S. Department of Commerce. See Attachment A of the
original Resolution 25-82 from which this subchapter is derived for the income
limits.
   (D)   The term PATIENT includes a minor who has been denied Medicaid, and
has received services from a provider, and whose parent or the person having
legal custody of that minor would qualify as a patient if they received
services from a provider.
   (E)   NECESSITIES OF LIFE is defined to include the costs of food, shelter,
clothing, utilities, and vehicle/transportation expenses.
   (F)   The County IHC Board has set financial guidelines dealing with income
and assets, in addition to residency requirements, in order to determine if a
patient is eligible for IHC assistance.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.083 THIRD-PARTY LIABILITY.
   (A)   (1)   If there is a liability claim pending such workman’s
compensation, a lawsuit due to bodily injury, or another third party claim, IHC
claims will be processed and held by IHC staff until information detailing the
outcome of such liability claims is provided.
      (2)   The patient must demonstrate that no other source of payment
exists. If the patient has or plans to file a personal injury lawsuit, the
application must agree to subrogation.
   (B)   Failure of the patient to have available health care insurance through
their employer or private source shall not be considered by the County Health
Care Board to determine eligibility.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.084 OTHER ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS.
   (A)   The IHC program is the payer of last resort. The provider staff shall
make all reasonable efforts to determine whether or not the patient is eligible
under any other public or private assistance program, such as Medicaid,
Medicare, or Indian Health Services.
   (B)   The provider staff shall require the patient to apply for medical
assistance through all agencies available. The patient shall provide a letter
from such agencies determining the approval or denial and this shall be part of
the verification process. Failure to cooperate in seeking assistance through
other government agencies will be grounds for denial of the IHC claim.
   (C)   A provider shall not be paid by the IHC funds for any costs when the
patient has been determined by the Human Services Department to be eligible for
Medicaid or any other assistance form HSD.
   (D)   If a patient has applied for assistance under the State Crime Victims
Reparation Commission, the state requires that all collateral sources such as
health insurance and programs such as the IHC program be exhausted before
assistance may be granted. In these cases, the Crime Victims Reparation
Commission is the payer of last resort.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.085 RESIDENCY.
   (A)   The patient must be domiciled in the county continuously and without
interruption for at least three months (90 days) prior to the date of service.
U.S. Citizenship is not required. Patients who reside out of the county for
periods of time on a temporary basis, including temporary employment, job
training, and full-time students with intent to return to the county of
residence, may be considered for IHC assistance based on the weight of the
evidence presented to the County Health Care Board. Under certain
circumstances, the patient may be asked to show intent to remain in the county.
   (B)   Residents of the county who are full time students attending school in
the state but out of the conty may qualify for IHC assistance. Such patients
will be taken into consideration on a case-by-case basis.
   (C)   A minor child is eligible for IHC assistance only if his or her
custodial parent resides in the county and only if the custodial parent would
qualify to receive IHC assistance. If only one of the parents of a minor child
of separated or divorced parents resides in the county, the applicant must
produce any separation agreement or divorce decree which pertains to the
custody of the minor child and to the responsibility for payment of medical
expenses.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.086 ASSETS.
   (A)   LIQUID ASSETS are defined to include cash and all other funds in
checking accounts, savings accounts, certificates of deposit, credit union
accounts, stocks, bonds, equity in real estate (other than the patient’s
primary home), and trusts.
   (B)   The asset limit for a household of one is $10,000; for a household of
two is $20,000; and for a household of three or more is $30,000. The asset
limit for widow/widowers is $20,000.
   (C)   Exempt are all liquid assets if the medical bill(s) exceed the amount
of savings of the household.
   (D)   Exempt are all or part of allowable asset limit if a patient has high
medical costs due to a catastrophic illness or injury. The patient is required
to provide a doctor’s report stating the nature of the illness or injury, and
the patient’s prognosis.
   (E)   Life insurance shall be exempted.
   (F)   Assets may be spent down to allowable limits by paying doctor bills,
other medical expenses or burial expenses not covered under the IHC program.
Documentation must be provided.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.087 INCOME VERIFICATION/COMPUTATION.
   (A)   General income.
      (1)   The gross income based on the number of individuals in the
household unit size cannot exceed 150% of the per capita income for the state.
      (2)   If the income level is equal to or greater than the personal per
capita income for state residents, as set forth in NMSA 1978 § 27-5-4(G), then
the patient is not designated as an “indigent patient.”
      (3)   For the purpose of determining household unit size, household
members to be included are the patient, the patient’s spouse, and the patient’s
legal dependents. All patients may be required to provide tax returns, check
stubs, award letters, profit/loss statements, trust documents, and the like to
the provider or IHC staff as part of the income verification process. All
sources of income earned or unearned by the household may be considered.
      (4)   Current income will be considered as income received 12 months
prior to the date of service, the twelfth month will be the month of the date
of service. The income of a deceased patient will not be included.
      (5)   Additional relevant information may be required by the IHC staff
and may be requested by telephone and/or by letter allowing up to 30 days for
the applicant to respond to such a request. Failure to comply will result in
the claim being administratively deleted or submitted by the IHC staff to the
County Health Care Board with a recommendation of denial.
   (B)   Special circumstances.
      (1)   If the applicant is an unwed mother, the annual income of the
father of the baby is included as the spouse’s annual income when calculating
the combined annual income.
      (2)   Unwed couples who are living together are treated the same as
married couples. Their annual incomes are combined.
      (3)   Couples who have been separated or divorced for less than 12 months
count all income for twelve months prior to hospitalization as combined annual
income.
   (C)   Extenuating circumstances. Approval may be granted in cases where the
patient’s household experiences a loss of income or has high medical debt due
to extenuating circumstances such as, but not limited to, a catastrophic
illness or injury of a household member. The patient may be required to provide
a doctor’s report stating the nature of the illness or injury, and the
patient’s prognosis. IHC staff may recommend approval for the full period of
eligibility, or for a one-time payment for the submitted claim or episode,
based on the weight of evidence received and documentation provided by the
patient.
   (D)   Income computation. The tax return for the prior year is the basis for
determining income in most situations. Whatever is stated to the IRS will apply
to dependency and income, unless status has changed. No deductions will be made
for number of dependents in the household.
      (1)   If the applicant has been steadily employed, use the prior year’s
tax return, and/or payroll check stubs for 12 months prior to hospitalization.
Employers’ letter of income verification may be needed.
      (2)   If the applicant has had variable employment, use the three prior
year’s tax returns, payroll check stubs for 12 months prior to hospitalization
and verification of income by letters from employers.
      (3)   If the applicant is self-employed, income is the net profit or loss
shown on Line 33, Form 1040 of Schedule C, plus any other income available from
other sources.
      (4)   If the applicant is a farm-laborer or occasional part-time
employee, use the prior year’s income tax return unless the applicant can
provide proof of income for each of the 12 months prior to hospitalization.
      (5)   If the patient is a dependent (at any age) and the dependent has
income, then the dependent’s income may be included with the income
calculation.
      (6)   If the patient is a dependent (at any age), the parent’s or
guardian’s income is considered in the income calculation.
      (7)   Depreciation is not an allowable deduction to income.
      (8)   Unearned income shall be verified by income tax returns, award
letters or viewing checks. Worker’s compensation and unemployment compensation
shall be counted as unearned income.
      (9)   Two or more households may be living under one roof but are not one
economic unit. This can best be established by their income tax returns which
will determine if the income(s) will be considered one household.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.088 SMALL CLAIMS.
   IHC claims from any provider in the amount of $100 or less will not be
considered for payment by the IHC program.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.089 LIMITATIONS ON IHC PAYMENTS.
   (A)   An eligible applicant may receive up to $25,000 total for all
hospitalization and emergency transport services per fiscal year (July 1
through June 30). The fiscal year shall be determined by the date of service.
Claims are accepted for the current fiscal year and the previous two fiscal
years. Claims for services provided prior to the previous two fiscal years will
not be accepted.
   (B)   Services are reimbursed at the following rates.
      (1)   Hospitalization:
         (a)   Mimbres Valley Medical Center: Up to $10,000 annually, with the
single visit minimum of $100 or greater. Room rates must be semi-private.
Reimbursement is paid at Medicaid eligible rates.
         (b)   Any state hospital and hospitals in El Paso, Texas: Up to
$10,000 annually, with a single visit minimum of $100 or greater. Payments for
services provided outside of the county is limited to medically necessary
inpatient hospital claims reimbursed at the Medicaid rate, but not to exceed
the limitations set forth herein.
         (c)   Any non-state hospital and hospitals outside El Paso, Texas: No
reimbursement.
         (d)   Hospitalization direct services: Up to $5,000 annually for any
fees directly incurred during a hospital or emergency room visit. Direct
services include physicians’ fees, pathology fees, and lab fees, which are
billed separately from the hospital facility. Reimbursement is paid directly to
providers at Medicaid eligible rates.
      (2)   Ambulance/emergency transport services:
         (a)   Emergency transport services (ground or air) may be reimbursed
at a maximum of $1,500 per claim. The transport of a patient must be by an
approved state-certified ambulance provider. The expense incurred includes the
care and transport of a patient to the “nearest” hospital; and
         (b)   The IHC fund is not intended to serve as reimbursement to the
patient/guarantor for payments previously made to the provider by the patient/
guarantor.
      (3)   Payments from the IHC fund shall not be considered for:
         (a)   Elective services, or services not considered a medical
necessity;
         (b)   Treatment which includes a more expensive procedure or product
when a less expensive procedure or product is available;
         (c)   Work-related injuries that are covered by the State Workers’
Compensation Act;
         (d)   Services that have been determined by the State Human Services
Department to be eligible for Medicaid reimbursement; or
         (e)   Medicare and other third-party insurance deductibles and co-
pays, except for services rendered at Mimbres Valley Medical Center.
      (4)   Primary care services; County Detention Center Detainees.
         (a)   Primary care services are provided for individuals committed to
the custody of the County Detention Center for the basic or general health care
needs of the detainees. Services may be provided by a licensed medical doctor,
certified registered nurse anesthetist, certified nurse practitioner,
osteopathic physician, dentist, optometrist, or expanded practice nurse when
providing emergency services, as determined by the IHC Administrator, in a
hospital to an indigent patient; or a licensed medical doctor or osteopathic
physician, dentist, optometrist, or expanded practice nurse when providing
services in an outpatient setting, as determined by the IHC Administrator.
         (b)   The IHC Administrator may allow other services which will
benefit individuals committed to the custody of the County Detention Center as
deemed necessary.
         (c)   For individuals committed to the custody of the County Detention
Center, approvals or reimbursements of IHC Funds by the county shall be made to
eligible medical providers based on the entirety of the actual billed charges
or 100% of the Medicaid rate, whichever is the lessor thereof, for eligible
treatment. Charges shall be submitted on itemized bills with the treatment
diagnosis from the medical provider. The charges for such services shall not
exceed the normal charges to other patients.
      (5)   Other services will be prioritized and reimbursed as allowed by
NMSA §27-5-7.1 and as approved and reviewed by the County Health Care Board on
a case-by-case basis.
   (C)   Charges that do not have Medicare rates assigned to them will be
reimbursed io the medical providers at a rate of 50% of the lowest contracted
rate available. Approvals or reimbursements will be made to medical providers
after obtaining authorization from the IHC Board.
   (D)   All payments for any services are limited to funding availability. A
claim made to the County Health Care Board for payment for the care of an
indigent patient shall not expire or become invalid because of a lack of money
in the fund during any fiscal year but shall be carried over into the ensuing
fiscal year.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.090 PATIENT/APPLICANT RESPONSIBILITIES.
   Proof of financial eligibility and residency is the responsibility of the
patient. Failure to provide the required information may lead to denial of the
application by the IHC staff. It is also the responsibility of the patient to
provide proof of all means of support from all sources.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.091 RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF PROVIDERS.
   (A)   Providers shall comply with the standards of the federal Health
Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (“HIPPA”).
   (B)   Required filings. Prior to filing any claim with the County Health
Care Board every provider shall place on file the following information per
NMSA § 27-5:
      (1)   Written financial assistance policies that are publicized;
      (2)   Proof that the provider is licensed under the laws of this state or
any state or other governmental entity in which the health care provider
operates; and
      (3)   Any other information or data that may be deemed necessary by the
County Health Care Board.
   (C)   A qualifying hospital requesting or receiving safety net care pool
provider hospital payments shall:
      (1)   Accept every indigent patient and request reimbursement for those
patients through the appropriate county indigent fund. The responsible county
shall approve requests meeting its eligibility standards and notify the
hospital of such approval(s);
      (2)   Confirm the amount of payment authorized by each county for
indigent patients, to that county for the previous fiscal year, by September 30
of each calendar year;
      (3)   Negotiate with each county the amount of indigent hospital payments
anticipated for the following fiscal year by December 31 of each year; and
      (4)   Provide to the department prior to January 15 of each year the
amount of the authorized indigent hospital payments anticipated for the
following fiscal year after an agreement has been reached on the amount with
each responsible county and such other related information as the department
may request.
   (D)   The provider staff shall provide the patient with a list stating the
documents that are needed to provide the information necessary to complete the
verification process.
   (E)   The provider staff is responsible to specify the date by which
documentation must be provided. Care will be exercised to allow a reasonable
length of time, not to exceed 90 days, for the applicant to gather all
necessary documentation. If the patient requests additional time, the request
may be honored, but the patient must specify a reasonable date which may not
exceed 15 days of the date of the request. If the information is not provided,
the claim may be submitted to the IHC staff with a request for a denial.
   (F)   To verify applications:
      (1)   The provider staff will verify the applications by gathering
documentation for the information given on the application form. All claims
will be submitted to the IHC staff for presentation to the IHC Board for
review; and
      (2)   The amount approved for payment from the IHC Funds shall be
accepted and deemed by the provider as payment in full. Any collection action
against the patient for any portion of the bill not covered by IHC Funds is
prohibited.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.092 IHC STAFF RESPONSIBILITIES.
   (A)   The IHC staff will retain computerized case records for a period of
not less than five years. Case records will be periodically purged when it is
evident that the information is no longer valid or necessary and the time limit
for retention of records has expired.
   (B)   The IHC staff will request from the Finance Department a check (f/k/
a warrant) for payment of approved claims on a monthly basis.
   (C)   The County Treasurer’s Office and Business Office shall maintain all
IHC records of payment.
   (D)   Confidentiality:
      (1)   The IHC staff shall comply with the standards of the federal Health
Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (“HIPPA”).
      (2)   All records dealing with physical or mental examinations or medical
treatment of patients are not public records and shall remain confidential
unless otherwise provided by law.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.093 AUTHORITY OF THE BOARD.
   (A)   The IHC Board has complete authority to authorize payment from the IHC
Fund.
   (B)   The Board shall state in writing the reason for rejecting or
disapproving any claim to the applicant via the IHC staff and provide a copy of
that determination to the provider.
   (C)   The IHC Board may, under extenuating circumstances deemed appropriate,
increase or decrease any payment on behalf of an indigent patient.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.094 OPEN MEETINGS LAW.
   The meeting of a County Health Care Board quorum which is held for the
purpose of approving, denying, hearing appeals of patients’, or to discuss
other business within its authority shall be held in compliance with the Open
Meetings Law. The County Health Care Board may use a numbering or lettering
system to keep confidential the identity of the individual whose claim is being
discussed.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)
§ 35.095 APPEALS.
   (A)   If denied a claim, an applicant may appeal the decision in writing to
the Indigent Funds Claims Board within 30 days of notification of denial. A
written appeal should be addressed to:
Indigent Funds Claims Board
PO Drawer 551
Deming, NM 88031-0551
   (B)   The Claims Administrator will inform the applicant in writing of the
time and place of the applicant’s hearing with the Indigent Funds Claims Board.
The Claims Administrator may also request additional information at that time.
   (C)   A meeting of the Indigent Funds Claims Board is held for the purpose
of hearing the appeals of applicants. The Board may use a numbering or
lettering system to keep confidential the identity of the individual whose
claim is being discussed, unless the appealing applicant wishes to address the
Board.
   (D)   All decisions of the Board are final.
   (E)   The patient will be notified in writing within ten days of the Board’s
decision. If the Board upholds the eligibility denial, the patient has the
right to file an appeal with District Court.
(Res. 25-82, passed 11-13-2025)

SOLID WASTE SYSTEM
§ 50.01 PURPOSE.
   (A)   This subchapter is enacted pursuant to the authority granted to the
Board of County Commissioners, hereinafter “the Board,” under the laws of the
state, including, but not limited to, NMSA §§ 4-37-1, 3-48-1 et seq., and 4-56-
1 et seq.
   (B)   This subchapter is enacted to protect and promote the health, safety,
and general welfare of the inhabitants of the county, hereinafter “the county,”
by establishing a system for collection and disposal of solid waste throughout
the unincorporated areas of the county.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.02 DEFINITIONS.
   The words, terms, and phrases used in this subchapter shall generally be
interpreted consistent with NMSA §§ 4-37-1 et seq. and 4-56-1 et seq., and
applicable solid waste management regulations, promulgated by the state, its
departments, and agencies.
   COMMERCIAL USER. Any person generating solid waste from any use other than a
single-family dwelling unit.
   CONVENIENCE STATION. A small solid waste transfer station operated by the
county for disposal of solid waste produced incidental to the normal
residential use of a single-family dwelling unit.
   DISPOSAL FACILITY. A permitted sanitary landfill or other acceptable method
of solid waste disposal, including a convenience or transfer station, which
operates in compliance with all state or other applicable waste management
regulation owned and operated by the City of Deming and/or the county.
   HAZARDOUS WASTE. Substances defined as hazardous or toxic by the United
States Environmental Protection Agency, the United States Resource Conservation
and Recovery Act, being 42 U.S.C. §§ 6901 et seq., the Federal Toxic Substances
Control Act, being 42 U.S.C. §§ 2601 et seq., the State Hazardous Waste Act,
being NMSA §§ 74-4-1 et seq., other state or local law, and specifically
includes radioactive, volatile, highly flammable, explosive, biomedical,
infectious, and liquid waste, sludge waste, residue from industrial processes
or pollution control processes, contaminated soil, anything contaminated with
polychlorinated biphenyls (PBCs) or asbestos, outdated or contaminated, or
banned, chemicals or commercial products, animal waste or body parts, grease
trap residues, closed cartridge filters from dry cleaning establishments, and
other similar wastes.
   MULTIPLE-FAMILY DWELLING UNIT. Any structure designed for residential use by
two or more families.
   PERSON. Every person, firm, partnership, public or private corporation,
association, trust, estate, or any other legal entity subject to the county’s
jurisdiction.
   PREMISES. Any real property, whether public, private, or commercial,
including vacant lots or lots with any type of structure, and includes realty
and personal property on the property and within structures on the property.
   PRIVATE SANITATION COMPANY. Any business registered with the State
Environment Department as a “commercial hauler” and operates in compliance with
all state, county, or other applicable solid waste management regulations, and
which is also registered to do business in the county and not accepting out-of-
county trash in the county.
   SINGLE-FAMILY DWELLING UNIT. A dwelling unit for one family.
   SOLID WASTE. Any garbage, rubbish, or refuse, rejected or waste food, offal,
swill, carrion, ashes, dirt, slop, wastewater, trash, weeds, briars, brush,
junk automobiles or automobile parts, waste or unwholesome material of any
kind, except sewage, and including residential, commercial, institutional,
industrial, and recreational waste.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.03 ACCUMULATION, DISPOSITION OF SOLID WASTE.
   (A)   Prohibited accumulations. No person shall allow any solid waste to
accumulate upon premises which that person owns, rents, leases, or otherwise
occupies or controls, except in the manner provided by this subchapter.
   (B)   Acceptable accumulations. Building materials, pipes, lumber, or boxes
may be stored on the premises if the accumulation is evenly piled and stacked,
and is for business purposes or for a construction project for which a valid
and current building permit has been issued, or for a construction or
improvement project for which a permit is not legally required; any otherwise
permissible accumulation shall not be allowed to become a feeding or breeding
place for flies, insects, or rodents, or to otherwise become unsanitary,
unsafe, or similarly injurious to public health and safety.
   (C)   Prohibited acts.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to scatter or distribute solid
waste or to disturb the contents of any solid waste receptacles other than to
dispose of it in conformity with this subchapter.
      (2)   It shall be unlawful for any person to sweep, place, throw, or
deposit solid waste upon any street, alley, sidewalk, gutter, storm sewer,
parkway, river, stream, lake, pond, arroyo, or other premises within the
county, except in receptacles or containers consistent with the provisions of
the subchapter. It shall be unlawful to transport solid waste in such a manner
as to cause it or allow it to be distributed onto such premises.
   (D)   Disposal facilities. All solid waste other than hazardous waste shall
be conveyed to a disposal facility though a method authorized by and consistent
with all provisions of this subchapter. The authorized use of transfer and
convenience stations will be governed by administrative procedures authorized
by the City of Deming and the county.
   (E)   Hazardous waste. Hazardous solid waste shall be disposed of at a
facility, which has been issued a permit by the State Environment Department
(or comparable agency with jurisdiction in the location of the facility) for
the disposal of hazardous waste.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.04 COLLECTION, DISPOSAL OF SOLID WASTE.
   (A)   Disposal facilities. The county shall provide at least one disposal
facility in order to allow county residents and property owners to comply with
the provisions of this subchapter.
   (B)   Convenience disposal stations. As needed to adequately accommodate
storage and orderly collection of solid waste, the county may develop
convenience stations as a temporary and intermediate disposal of waste. Only
residential solid waste or refuse will be accepted at convenience stations. Any
persons who pays the disposal facility assessment may utilize any convenience
station provided by the county for the disposal of small amounts of solid waste
produced incidental to the normal residential use of a single-family dwelling
unit. Private sanitation companies and commercial users may not use the
convenience stations.
   (C)   Transfer station.
      (1)   A solid waste transfer station will be provided by the City of
Deming and the county for the disposal of solid waste refuse. All residents of
the county will be allowed access and use of the transfer station. Commercial
users and/or large residential items, such as furniture and appliances, may be
disposed of at the transfer station or may be directed to the landfill.
      (2)   Any person paying the disposal assessment fee may use the transfer
station without charge, except for tires and dead animals where a charge is
applicable.
      (3)   Persons who do not pay the disposal fee assessment may use the
transfer stations and pay the appropriate tipping fees. Private sanitation
companies licensed by the county may use transfer stations or landfill as
directed by the county.
   (D)   Tipping fees. Private sanitation companies, except for commercial
users, construction, and demolition companies shall pay any and all tipping
fees that may be required for use of a particular disposal facility.
   (E)   Location. Location of convenience stations is to be determined by the
county.
   (F)   Private sanitation pick-up service.
      (1)   All private sanitation companies doing business with the county
must have a franchise agreement with the county must register with the County
Planning Department, and pay an annual licensing fee.
      (2)   The fee will be set annually by resolution by the Board of County
Commissioners. Private haulers must comply with all State Environmental
Department regulations, provisions of the franchise agreement, and the
provisions of this subchapter.
      (3)   Private haulers may set their own rates and may use the county
transfer station only for waste originating in and picked up in the county.
   (G)   Containers. Containers utilized for storage of solid waste on the
premises, and for transportation of solid waste to a disposal facility, must be
designed and secured so as to fully enclose and contain the solid waste and
must be leak-proof for storage or transport. All containers (brands and types)
must be approved by the county.
   (H)   Multi-family dwelling units. Multi-family dwelling units shall be
considered a commercial user; any owner of a multi-family dwelling unit who
fails to or refuses to comply with the commercial user requirements of this
subchapter shall be subject to the full disposal facility assessment for each
dwelling unit, and shall also be subject to prosecution for violation of the
subchapter, and to all other penalties allowed by law.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.05 DISPOSAL FACILITY ASSESSMENT.
   The owner of any residential and commercial property or premises (or which
could be used for residential or commercial purposes) within the county shall
be assessed an annual fee of $12 for each tax bill assessed by the County
Treasurer. The assessed amount shall be included in the tax bill mailing, and
shall be due and payable concurrently with all assessed taxes. In the event the
fee is not timely paid, a fixed penalty of $5 shall be added to the annual fee.
In addition to the penalty, an interest charge of 1% per month shall accrue.
Collection of delinquent fees provided above be as allowed by law.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.06 REGULATIONS FOR PRIVATE COLLECTION, CONTAINERS.
   (A)   Frequency of service. Solid waste collection services by private
sanitation companies must be provided on at least a weekly basis, or more
frequently if necessary, to keep the premises free of solid waste consistent
with the provisions of this subchapter.
   (B)   Containers. Containers utilized for storage of solid waste on the
premises between collections must be designed so as to fully enclose and
contain the solid waste, and must be leak-proof for storage of any liquid solid
waste. The county must approve all containers used by private sanitation
companies.
   (C)   Vehicle requirement. Private sanitation company vehicles shall be
covered and meet all state and federal vehicle safety requirements, and all
county requirements that may be developed subsequent to this subchapter.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.07 COUNTY COLLECTIONS.
   The county may provide pick-up and disposal services as needed to ensure
competition, affordability, and compliance with this subchapter. The fees for
county pick-up services shall be based on the costs of operations,
depreciation, capital improvements, and administrative, and all other necessary
business costs.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.08 BILLING, COLLECTION OF ASSESSMENTS.
   The county shall bill disposal facility assessments in the tax bill mailings
issued by the County Treasurer. Non-payment of any assessment will be subject
to collection as allowed by law, including, but not limited to, the provisions
NMSA §§ 3-48-4 et seq. allowing for a lien on the property subject to the
assessment.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.09 CONSTRUCTION, DEMOLITION DEBRIS, SOLID WASTE.
   (A)   Construction and demolition debris, solid waste disposal. Commercial
users in construction and demolition industries shall not be required to meet
the requirements applicable for other commercial users for construction and
demolition debris, or solid waste produced incidental to construction and
demolition operations, but shall instead comply with the provisions of §
50.04. Construction and demolition debris, or other forms of solid waste
produced by a commercial user incidental to construction and demolition
operations, shall not be disposed of at convenience stations.
   (B)   Construction and demolition debris, solid waste provisions.
      (1)   Solid waste containment required. At all sites where streets,
sidewalks, buildings, or structures are being constructed, remodeled, repaired,
demolished, or maintained, the construction site shall be kept free from
uncontained accumulations of solid waste debris, including, but not limited to,
scrap or discarded pieces of concrete, cinderblock, asphalt, concrete, and
other building or construction products. Accumulations shall be deemed
contained when placed in solid waste or debris containers. Any accumulation
otherwise permissible under this section shall not be allowed to become a
feeding or breeding place for flies, insects, or rodents, or to otherwise
become unsanitary, unsafe, or similarly injurious to the public health and
safety. The following types of solid waste accumulations shall not be required
to be placed in approved storage containers if the specified conditions are
met.
         (a)   Major building demolition waste. Solid waste produced by a major
building demolition which is so large in scope or scale that it cannot
reasonably be placed in approved containers shall be an exception to this
section, provided all loose, readily wind-borne matter is contained and the
remainder is either not an immediate hazard to the public because of its nature
or because of security measures on site. Immediately following completion of
the demolition project, all solid waste on the site must be removed to an
approved disposal facility.
         (b)   Major street construction and maintenance project waste. Solid
waste from street construction, reconstruction, or maintenance projects, and
street-pavement cuts which are so large in scope or scale that they cannot
reasonably be placed in approved containers, shall be an exception to this
section, provided all loose, readily wind-borne matter is contained and the
remainder is not an immediate hazard to the public. Immediately following
completion of the demolition project, all solid waste on the site must be
removed to an approved disposal facility.
         (c)   Masonry solid waste. Rock, concrete, mortar, brick, and
cinderblock solid waste does not have to be placed in an approved container and
may be collected into a pile on the ground, but must be removed to a permitted
disposal site immediately upon completion of the construction from which the
waste was generated, or within 30 days after the work is abandoned. Extra
concrete from cleaning delivery trucks must be placed on site and not on
developed roads or sidewalks. This concrete must subsequently be removed to a
permitted disposal site.
         (d)   Roofing materials solid waste. Shingles, tarpaper, and other
solid waste from roofing jobs that are capable of readily becoming wind-borne
do not have to be placed into an approved container, provided such waste is
placed directly into a dump truck or similar truck for hauling to an approved
disposal facility and is removed on a daily basis.
         (e)   Wind-borne solid waste. Solid waste capable of being wind-borne
shall be contained daily, except on windy days when it shall be contained
immediately. Windy days shall be those days when solid waste is observed
becoming wind-borne.
      (2)   Storage containers. Unless granted a specific exception within this
division (B), solid waste materials from construction shall be deposited and
stored within approved waste containers as follows:
         (a)   The following mechanically transported containers may be used
for construction waste:
            1.   Open-top containers, commonly referred to as roll-off
containers, to be used for construction waste not capable of readily becoming
wind-borne and acceptable for limited amounts of heavy items, such as earth,
bricks, concrete, and shingles;
            2.   Overhead-dump containers, having lids and at least three cubic
yards capacity, to be used for lightweight construction waste only, including
that which is capable of readily becoming wind-borne, and for earth, bricks,
concrete, shingles, and other heavy materials; and
            3.   Other containers, including, but not limited to, dump trucks
and fenced enclosures, may be used for waste control, provided a request is
submitted and approved with the building permit.
         (b)   Containers having lids shall be kept closed at all times, except
when containers are being filled or emptied.
         (c)   The number of containers at a construction site shall be
sufficient to ensure compliance with this subchapter.
         (d)   Required containers shall be located not more than 200 feet from
the construction site, and may be shared by more than one construction site.
      (3)   Disposal. Construction and demolition debris, or other forms of
solid waste produced by a commercial user incidental to construction and
demolition operations, shall be disposed at a facility or as directed.
      (4)   Responsibility. It shall be the duty of any person holding a
building permit to provide acceptable containers and to have all solid waste
placed therein, and to have such containers emptied often enough to prevent
their overflow. It shall further be the duty of the person holding a building
permit and the property owner whether to remove or cause to be removed all
construction solid waste from the site to a disposal facility, or to contract
for the services of a private sanitation company to transport such waste to a
disposal facility or approved fill site.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.10 ENFORCEMENT PROVISIONS.
   (A)   Construction and demolition debris, or other forms of solid waste
produced by a commercial user incidental to construction and demolition
operations, shall be disposed of at a disposal facility or as directed.
   (B)   This subchapter shall be enforced by the County Sheriff’s Department
and/or the County Code Enforcement Unit, or other authorized county personnel.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.11 ADMINISTRATION.
   Under the supervision of the County Manager, county staff is authorized to
implement, manage, and enforce this subchapter. Policies and procedures to be
developed and implemented pursuant to this authority may include determination
of the frequency and method of billing for disposal facilities assessments,
imposition of late fees for non-payment, offering discounts for advance
payments, establishing documentation requirements, and any other matters
necessary to administer the subchapter.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.12 EXEMPTION.
   Agriculture waste is exempt from the provisions of this subchapter.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
§ 50.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   In addition to any other penalty or remedy, including injunctive
relief, any person who violates any provision of §§
50.01 through
50.12 shall be subject to prosecution consistent with state and local law,
including, but not limited to, NMSA § 40-37-03. Each violation of §§
50.01 through
50.12 shall be subject to a fine of up to $300, up to 90 days imprisonment, or
both, except that:
      (1)   A fine of up to $1,000 may be assessed against any person who
discards private property in any manner other than by disposing of it in an
authorized landfill or other disposal facility; and
      (2)   A fine of up to $5,000 may be assessed against any person for the
improper or illegal disposal of hazardous materials or waste in any manner
other than as provided for in the Hazardous Waste Act, NMSA §§ 74-4-1 et seq.
(Ord. 50, passed 10-21-2002)
CHAPTER 51: SEWAGE
Section
