51.99   Penalty
DISPOSAL OF UNTREATED WASTE
§ 51.01 SCOPE.
   (A)   This subchapter is adopted pursuant to the authority granted the
county by the state, including NMSA §§ 4-37-1 et seq.
   (B)   This subchapter shall apply to the disposal of waste in the county by
all persons.
(Ord. 63, passed 12-6-2005)
§ 51.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   PERSON. Any person, individual, firm, partnership, corporation, company,
society, association, or cooperative, and every officer, agent, or employee
thereof.
   PREMISES. Any real property in the county, improved or unimproved, located
outside the municipal boundaries of the City of Deming and the Village of
Columbus, New Mexico.
   WASTE.
      (1)   LIQUID WASTE. All liquid waste from any industrial, manufacturing,
or mechanical process, including motor oil and lubricants, wastewater,
including sewerage from septic tanks or other sources, and any contaminated or
hazardous liquids as defined by state and deferral law, specifically including
the State Hazardous Waste Act, being NMSA §§ 74-4-1 et seq., Federal Toxic
Substances Control Act, being U.S.C. §§ 2601 et seq., and substances defined as
hazardous by the United States Environmental Protection Agency.
      (2)   SEPTAGE. The residual wastes including human waste, water, or
grease removed from septic tanks, from a holding tank, or other on-site
wastewater treatment system.
      (3)   SLUDGE. Solid, semi-solid or liquid waste generated from a
municipal, commercial, or industrial wastewater treatment plant, water supply
treatment plant or air pollution control facility that is associated with the
treatment of these wastes.
(Ord. 63, passed 12-6-2005)
§ 51.03 DISPOSAL OF WASTE.
   (A)   No person shall dispose of any waste, as defined in §
51.02, on any premises located in the county. This includes the discharge (land
application) of septage by any collector or other disposal entity.
   (B)   This subchapter shall apply to all liquid waste, including the waste
approved by the State Environment Department, which may not be discharged on
county premises.
   (C)   This subchapter shall not apply to disposal of waste into a municipal
sewer system or treatment facility operated by the City of Deming or the
Village of Columbus.
(Ord. 63, passed 12-6-2005) Penalty, see §
51.99
§ 51.04 ENFORCEMENT.
   Pursuant to NMSA §§ 4-37-3 and 4-37-4, §§
51.01 through
51.03 may be enforced by the County Sheriff and deputies or County Code
Enforcement Officers.
(Ord. 63, passed 12-6-2005)
§ 51.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   Any failure to comply with a requirement or regulation of §§
51.01 through
51.03 shall constitute a violation of §§
51.01 through
51.03.
      (2)   Pursuant to NMSA § 4-37-3, violation of §§
51.01 through
51.03 may be prosecuted in any court of competent jurisdiction within the
county, and shall be punishable by a fine of $300 or imprisonment for 90 days,
or both, except that where the violation involves the disposal or discarding of
refuse, litter, or garbage on public or private property in any manner, other
than by disposing of it in an authorized landfill, the fine may be no more that
$1,000, and except that where the violation involves the improper or illegal
disposal of hazardous materials or waste in any manner, other than that as
provided for in the Hazardous Waste Act, being NMSA §§ 74-4-1 et seq., the fine
may be more than $5,000.
      (3)   In addition to the penalties set forth in division (B)(2) above,
the county may seek injunctive relief against a violator requiring tho violator
to perform, or prohibiting the violator from performing, certain conduct
related to §§
51.01 through
51.03.
(Ord. 63, passed 12-6-2005)
TITLE VII: TRAFFIC CODE
   Chapter
      
70.   RECREATIONAL VEHICLES
CHAPTER 70: RECREATIONAL VEHICLES
Section
Off-Highway Vehicles
   
70.01   Purpose
   
70.02   Definitions
   
70.03   OHV operation on county roadway
   
70.04   Restrictions and prohibitions on OHV operation
   
70.05   Miscellaneous
OFF-HIGHWAY VEHICLES
§ 70.01 PURPOSE.
   (A)   This subchapter shall apply to the operation of off-highway vehicles
on county-owned and controlled roadways consistent with the provisions of the
Off-Highway Vehicle Act, NMSA §§ 66-3-1001 et seq.
   (B)   This subchapter is only applicable to those areas in the county
outside the incorporated municipalities of the City of Deming and Village of
Columbus.
   (C)   Nothing contained in this subchapter applies to or affects operation
of off-highway vehicles on private property, nor does it authorize operation on
roads or highways owned or controlled by the state or federal government, or
agencies thereof.
(Ord. 112, passed 7-13-2023)
§ 70.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COUNTY-OWNED or CONTROLLED ROADWAY. Within the scope of this subchapter,
includes all designated county roads, both maintained and not maintained by the
county, rights-of-way, and easements that were constructed, signed, and
maintained for regular passenger-car use by the general public.
   OFF-HIGHWAY MOTOR VEHICLE (OHV). A motorized vehicle designed by the
manufacturer
for operation off the highway or road, and includes:
      (1)   ALL-TERRAIN VEHICLE (ATV), which is a motorized vehicle, 50 inches
or less in width, having an unladen dry weight of 1,000 pounds or less,
traveling on three or more low-pressure tires and having at least one seat
designed to be straddled by the operator and handle-bar type steering control;
      (2)   OFF-HIGHWAY MOTORCYCLE (OHM), which is a motorized vehicle
traveling on not
more than two tires and having a seat designed to be straddled by the operator
with handle-bar type steering control;
      (3)   RECREATIONAL OFF-HIGHWAY VEHICLE (UTV), which is a motorized
vehicle designed for travel on four or more non-highway tires, for use by one
or more persons, and being 80 or less inches in overall width, exclusive of
accessories, a gross vehicle weight rating not greater that 1,750 pounds, an
engine displacement of less than 1,000 cubic centimeters, maximum speed
capability in excess of 35 mph, and having one or more non-straddle seating, a
steering wheel for steering control, and identification by means of a 17-
character vehicle identification number; and
      (4)   Any other vehicle identified or described by the State Department
of Game and Fish or the Off-Highway Motor Vehicle Advisory Board fitting the
general profile of a vehicle operated off the highway for recreational
purposes.
   OFF-HIGHWAY MOTOR VEHICLE ACT. Refers to NMSA §§ 66-3-1001 through 66-3-
1021, and may be referred to herein as THE ACT or OHMVA.
(Ord. 112, passed 7-13-2023)
§ 70.03 OHV OPERATION ON COUNTY ROADWAY.
   (A)   An OHV, excluding OHM (motorcycles) and snowmobiles, may be operated
on a county-owned or operated roadway if:
      (1)   The vehicle has one or more headlights and one or more taillights
that comply with the OHMVA, being NMSA §§ 66-3-1001 et seq.;
      (2)   The vehicle has brakes, mirrors, and mufflers;
      (3)   The operator has a valid driver’s license or permit as required
under the Motor Vehicle Code and off-highway motor vehicle safety permits as
required under the OHMVA;
      (4)   The operator is insured in compliance with the provisions of the
Mandatory Financial Responsibility Act, being NMSA §§ 66-5-201 et seq.;
      (5)   The operator of the vehicle is using eye protection that complies
with the OHMVA;
      (6)   The vehicle complies with the registration, license plate,
validation stickers, and display requirements of the OHMVA; and
      (7)   The vehicle is equipped by a spark arrester approved by the United
States Forest Service.
   (B)   Operators of OHVs under the age of 18 years must also comply with the
following:
      (1)   Must be at least 13 years of age and have a valid motorcycle
license and off-highway vehicle safety permit, or be at least 15 years of age
and have a valid driver’s license, instruction permit, or provisional license
and off-highway vehicle safety permit;
      (2)   Must be accompanied by or under the direct supervision of a parent,
guardian, or custodian of a certified safety/OHV instructor;
      (3)   May not operate while carrying a passenger under the age of 18
years; and
      (4)   Must wear a safety helmet that complies with the OHMVA.
   (C)   All operators shall be subject to the applicable requirements and
penalties for moving and parked vehicles of the Motor Vehicle Code, being NMSA
§§ 66-1-1 et seq., except for those provisions in conflict with the OHMVA,
including provisions relating to driving while under the influence of
intoxicating liquor or drugs, and to the penalty provisions of the OHMVA.
(NMSA § 66-3-1020)
(Ord. 112, passed 7-13-2023) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 70.04 RESTRICTIONS AND PROHIBITIONS ON OHV OPERATION.
   (A)   No person may operate an OHV on any limited-access highway, freeway,
or interstate except to cross after coming to a complete stop prior to crossing
and yielding the right-of-way to all oncoming traffic.
   (B)   ATVs operated pursuant to this subchapter shall be subject to a speed
limit of 35 mph or the posted speed limit, whichever is less, and only on the
right-hand side of the roadways.
   (C)   UTVs operated pursuant to this subchapter shall be subject to a speed
limit of 45 mph or the posted speed limit, not to exceed 55 mph.
   (D)   Operators of OHVs shall ride only on the permanent and regular seat
attached thereto, and shall not carry any passenger unless such vehicle is
designed to carry more than one person on permanent and regular seating
attached to the OHV.
   (E)   Operators of OHVs may not carry any person, package, bundle, or other
items which prevent the operator from keeping both hands on the steering
mechanism, or which interferes with the operation of the OHV or obstructs the
operator’s view.
   (F)   OHVs may not be used on county-owned or controlled roadways in the
pursuit of and/or with the intent to hunt or take a game animal, except as
allowed by the State Game Commission.
   (G)   No operator shall use any OHV in the pursuit of, or harassment of,
livestock belonging to another person or entity, except in the course of valid
agricultural operations, nor in any manner that has a direct negative effect on
or interferes with persons engaged in agricultural practices.
   (H)   OHVs may not be operated on land owned, controlled, or administered by
the State Game Commission or the State Parks Division, except as specifically
authorized bylaw.
(Ord. 112, passed 7-13-2023) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 70.05 MISCELLANEOUS.
   (A)   The provisions of this subchapter shall not apply to persons who
operate OHVs on privately held land or to OHVs that are:
      (1)   Owned and operated by an agency or department of the United States,
the state, or a political subdivision of this state;
      (2)   Owned by non-residents and used in this state only for organized
competition purposes, provided that the use is not on a rental basis, unless
holding a valid non-resident permit;
      (3)   Brought into this state by manufacturers or distributors for
wholesale purposes and not used for demonstrations;
      (4)   In the possession of dealers as stock-in-trade and not used for
demonstration purposes;
      (5)   Farm tractors, as defined by NMSA § 66-1-4.6, special mobile
equipment, as defined by NMSA § 66-1-4.16, or OHVs being used for agricultural
operations; or
      (6)   Used exclusively on private closed courses.
   (B)   This subchapter does not authorize OHV use anywhere other than county-
owned or controlled roadways, and specifically does not authorize operation on
private lands or roads without the express permission of the landowner or
leaseholder of such lands.
(Ord. 112, passed 7-13-2023)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 90.01 SHORT TITLE.
   This chapter shall be known as the “Nuisance Ordinance,” and shall be
referred to herein as “this ordinance” or “this chapter.”
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 90.02 JURISDICTION.
   This chapter shall provide for the regulation of littering; nuisances;
dangerous buildings; salvage yards; towing operations; dealers, wreckers, and
dismantlers; burial and disposal of human remains; and waste tires within the
county, but not within the boundaries of municipalities.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 90.03 MEANING OF TERMS.
   Wherever the terms COUNTY PLANNING DIRECTOR or COUNTY PLANNER appear in this
chapter, they shall be read and understood as including any other person or
position authorized by the County Manager or the Board of County Commissioners
to administer or otherwise carryout the requirements of the chapter.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 90.04 PURPOSE.
   (A)   Every owner of property in the county is entitled to the peaceful
enjoyment of his or her property free from any interference caused by the
unlawful act or failure to perform a duty by any other persons in the county,
or by any other person suffering or permitting any condition or thing to be or
exist; which act, omission, condition, or thing either:
      (1)   Injures or endangers the comfort, repose, health, or safety of
others;
      (2)   Offends decency;
      (3)   Is offensive to the senses;
      (4)   Unlawfully interferes with, obstructs or tends to obstruct, or
renders dangerous for passage any public road, highway, sidewalk, stream,
ditch, or drainage;
      (5)   In any way renders other persons insecure in life to the use of
property; or
      (6)   Essentially interferes with the comfortable enjoyment of life and
property, or tends to depreciate the value of the property of others.
   (B)   This chapter establishes certain duties that owners of property owe to
the community.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 90.05 ILLUSTRATIVE ENUMERATION.
   The maintaining, using, placing, depositing, leaving, or permitting to be or
remain on any public or private property of any of the following items,
conditions, or actions are declared to be and constitute a nuisance; provided,
however, this enumeration shall not be deemed or construed to be conclusive,
limiting, or restrictive:
   (A)   Accumulation of rubbish, trash, refuse, junk, and other abandoned
materials, metals, lumber, or other things;
   (B)   Any condition that provides harborage for rats, mice, snakes, flies,
mosquitoes, injurious insects, termites, and other vermin;
   (C)   The carcasses of animals or fowl not disposed of within a reasonable
time after death;
   (D)   The pollution of any public or private well or cistern, stream, lake,
arroyo, canal, or body of water by sewage, dead animals, industrial wastes, or
other substances;
   (E)   Discarding, discharging, releasing, scattering, throwing, sweeping, or
dumping, either intentionally or unintentionally, of litter, paper, cans,
bottles, packaging, refuse, trash, construction waste, building materials, or
garbage into the public right-of-way, onto the private property of other
persons, or into the environment;
   (F)   Junked, inoperative, wrecked, dismantled, partially dismantled,
discarded, unused, or unlicensed mobile homes, recreational vehicles, or
trailers, except in an authorized, permitted salvage yards;
   (G)   Discarded or unused machinery or appliances, or parts thereof, or the
accumulation of materials that creates an unsafe, unsightly condition, or a
harborage for disease vectors or other vermin, except for such items located in
an authorized, permitted salvage yard; and
   (H)   Any building, structure, or other place or location where any
activity, which is in violation of local, state, or federal law, is conducted,
performed, or maintained.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 90.06 DEFINITIONS.
   (A)   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   (B)   Any word or term not defined in this chapter shall have the meaning
ascribed to it in the county subdivision ordinance or the county zoning
ordinance, or the Deming/Luna County extra-territorial zoning regulations, or
they shall have their ordinary accepted meaning within the context with which
they are used.
      ACCEPTABLE.
         (a)   Accepted by the County Building Official, or the State Building
Official, with respect to matters set out in this chapter;
         (b)   Accepted by the County Fire Marshal, or other authority
designated by the County Manager, with respect to matters under the NFPA Fire
Protection Code; and
         (c)   Accepted by the County Code Compliance Officer with respect to
the standards set out in this chapter.
      AGRICULTURE. An agricultural use or activity requires a tract containing
five or more contiguous acres in active, current use for the production of farm
crops for sale and profit, including vegetables, fruit, cotton, grain, and
other crops, and the processing of crops to the generally recognizable minimum
level of marketability and storage thereof on the premises; the open range
grazing of livestock or irrigated pasture for grazing livestock; animal and
poultry husbandry, dairy operations, floriculture, and horticulture; and
accessory uses customarily incidental to agricultural activities; provided
further, that AGRICULTURE does not include commercial slaughter houses,
meatpacking plants, fertilizer yards, or other similar animal-related uses.
      AGRICULTURAL BUILDING. A structure designed and constructed to house farm
implements, hay, grain, poultry, livestock, or other horticultural products.
This structure shall not be a place of human habitation or a place of
employment, where agricultural products are processed, treated, or packaged,
nor shall it be a place used by the public.
      BALED TIRE or TIRE BALE. A method of volume reduction of waste tires,
whereby whole or cut tires are compacted into a bundle and then banded together
to form a tire bale. BALED TIRES shall not be considered processed tires and
shall be defined as solid waste, unless they are incorporated into some
beneficial use project.
      BUILDING OFFICIAL. The officer, or official or inspector, or other
designated authority, charged with the administration and enforcement of any
code, or the BUILDING OFFICIAL’S duly authorized representative.
      BURIAL. The process of interring human remains.
      CEMETERY. A place dedicated to, and used and intended to be used for, the
permanent interment of human remains.
      CERTIFICATE OF COMPLIANCE. A certificate issued to the property owner by
the County Code Compliance Officer, or other designated county official, or a
State Building Official evidencing the fact that the requirements of this
chapter, as set forth in this chapter, have been met.
      CODE. A standard that is an extensive compilation of provisions covering
broad subject matter or that is suitable for adoption into law, or any adopted
uniform code pertaining to construction activities.
      CODE COMPLIANCE OFFICER. The person designated by the county to enforce
various county codes or ordinances.
      COUNTY. Luna County, New Mexico.
      COUNTY BOARD. The Board of County Commissioners.
      CUT TIRE. A waste tire from which the tire face, tread, or sidewall has
been cut or removed for beneficial use. A CUT TIRE shall consist of pieces
greater than 18 inches on any one side.
      GRAVE. A lot, plot, or burial space, and means a space of ground used
for, or intended to be used for, the permanent interment of human remains.
      HUMAN REMAINS or REMAINS. The body of a deceased person, regardless of
its stage of decomposition, and cremated remains.
      INSPECTOR. The County Building Inspector or the Code Compliance Officer,
or a person duly delegated by the County Building Inspector or the Code
Compliance Officer, or a person instructed or requested by the County Building
Inspector or the Code Compliance Officer, to provide a written report with
respect to any matter set out in this chapter.
      INTERMENT. The disposition of human remains by entombment, inurnment, or
burial.
      JUNKED MOBILE HOME. Any abandoned, disassembled, dismantled,
uninhabitable, severely damaged, or wrecked mobile home.
      LITTER, TO LITTER, or LITTERING. The act of placing, discarding,
broadcasting, throwing, tossing, or allowing the spreading or broadcasting of
refuse or debris onto any property or location, or site not officially
designated as a solid waste or refuse disposal facility, and shall include all
such acts by a person occupying a motor vehicle.
      LCBO. The County Building Official; see also INSPECTOR and BUILDING
OFFICIAL.
      MAINTAINED. To carry out any repairs, reconstruction, refinishing, or
replacement of any part or parts of a building, or structure or property, and
MAINTAINED shall also mean the upkeep, attention, and care of grounds.
      MANUFACTURED HOME. A movable or portable housing structure over 32 feet
in length or over eight feet in width constructed to be towed on its own
chassis and designed to be installed with or without a permanent foundation for
human occupancy as a residence, and which may include one or more components
that can be retracted for towing purposes and subsequently expanded for
additional capacity, or may be two or more units separately towable but
designed to be joined into one integral unit, as well as a single unit.
MANUFACTURED HOME does not include recreational vehicles or modular or pre-
manufactured homes built to IBC standards, designed to be permanently affixed
to real property. MANUFACTURED HOME includes any movable or portable housing
structure over 12 feet in width and 40 feet in length, which is used for non-
residential purposes.
      MOBILE HOME. A moveable or portable housing structure larger than 40 feet
in body length, eight feet in width, or 11 feet in overall height, designed for
and occupied by no more than one family for living and sleeping purposes that
is not constructed to the standards of the United States Department of Housing
and Urban Development, the National Manufactured Housing Construction and
Safety Standards Act of 1974, being 42 U.S.C. §§ 5401 et seq., and the Housing
and Urban Development Zone Code 2, or the International Building Code, as
amended, to the date of the unit’s construction or built to the standards of
any municipal building code.
      NOTICE OF NUISANCE. The notice issued by any authorized County Employee
directed to the owner, occupant, or tenant of property in the county setting
out the violations and the time limits for abatement of the violations under
this chapter.
      NUISANCE. Knowingly creating, performing, or maintaining anything
affecting any number of citizens without lawful authority, or failure to
perform a duty which creates any of the outcomes identified in §
90.04.
      OCCUPANCY. The purpose that a building, or part thereof, is used or
intended to be used.
      OFFICER. The Code Compliance Officer, the person designated by the county
to administer and enforce various codes and ordinances.
      OWNER. Any person, agent, firm, or corporation having a legal or
equitable interest in the property.
      PARCEL. A unit of land capable of being described by location and
boundaries, and not dedicated for public or common use.
      PERMIT. An official document or certificate issued by the Building
Official, the County Planner, or other authorized authority, as appropriate,
authorizing performance of a specified activity.
      PERSON. A natural person, including any individual, partnership, company,
corporation, firm, association, trust, estate, foundation, and state and
federal agency, institution, county, city, town, village, or municipality, or
other legal entity however organized.
      PROCESSED TIRE. A tire that bas been processed through grinding,
shredding, or other means, thereby producing a material that is readily
suitable for marketing into product manufacturing, energy recovery, or other
beneficial reuse markets. Waste tires that have been compacted, baled, cut, or
shredded, without a suitable market, shall not be considered PROCESSED TIRES
and shall be regulated as solid waste.
      PROPERTY. Any area, plot, or parcel of land in the county, which is under
a common ownership or is separately identified for assessment by the County
Assessor’s office. PROPERTY shall include land under the ownership of the
United States, the state, or any local government or school district entity.
This definition is intended to be inclusive and not limiting, and shall
therefore include all land within the boundaries of the county, except that the
definition of property, and therefore this chapter, shall exclude PROPERTY
within the boundaries of the City of Deming and the Village of Columbus, and
any hereafter incorporated municipality.
      PROPERTY OCCUPANT. Any person who is occupying any property, whether by
legal right or without legal right.
      PROPERTY OWNER. The person who is the recorded owner of any property
according to the records contained in the County Clerk’s office.
      RECREATIONAL VEHICLE. A self-contained driven or towed portable unit not
designed to be installed on a temporary or permanent foundation, nor used for
human occupancy as a residence, which includes: pickup campers, chassis mounted
motor homes, mini motor homes, park trailers, recreational vans, pop-up tent/
hard-top trailers, converted busses, or other converted and chopped vehicles.
      REFUSE.
         (a)   Any organic or inorganic waste or debris, including, but not
limited to, garbage, household waste, wastepaper, waste containers, empty
packaging, empty or used plastic bags or other plastic containers, empty drink
containers, empty or used styrofoam containers, empty metal cans or containers
of any kind, any material that is discarded after residential or commercial
use, scraps of building materials such as wood, brick, concrete, asphalt,
metal, and plastic, materials resulting from the demolition of any structure or
vehicle, used grease, used oil, used vehicle parts, used appliances or
machinery parts, used tires, discarded household furnishings and equipment,
junked parts or bodies of automobiles and other metallic junk or scrap,
discarded cleaning materials, and any material commonly known as trash or junk.
         (b)   REFUSE does not include:
            1.   Waste from the extraction, beneficiation, and processing of
ores and minerals, including phosphate-rock and overburden from the mining of
uranium, ore, coal, copper, molybdenum,
and other ores and minerals;
            2.   Agricultural waste, including, but not limited to, manure and
other crop residues returned to the soil as fertilizer or soil conditioner;
            3.   Sand and gravel;
            4.   Solid or dissolved material in domestic sewage, or solid or
dissolved materials in irrigation return, flows, or industrial discharges that
are point sources subject to permits under § 402 of the Federal Water Pollution
Control Act, 33 U.S.C. § 1342, or source, special nuclear, or by-produce
material as defined by the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, 42 U.S.C. §§ 2011 et seq.
and subsequent amendments;
            5.   Any material regulated by Subtitle C of the Federal Resource
Conservation and Recovery Act, being 42 U.S.C. §§ 6901 et seq., or substances
regulated by the Federal Toxic Substance Control Act, being 15 U.S.C. §§ 2601
et seq.; and
            6.   Salvage materials, as defined in this chapter, which are
contained within an official. legally established salvage yard.
      REPAIR. The reconstruction, renewal, refinishing, or refurbishing of all
or any part of an existing building or structure, or property, for the purpose
of its maintenance.
      SALVAGE MATERIALS. Any inoperable motor vehicles, inoperable construction
equipment, inoperable agricultural equipment, inoperable machinery, inoperable
major household appliances, any unused or junked manufactured or mobile homes
intended to be dismantled, and accumulations of scrap metal or used building
materials, which are kept together in one location or on any property for the
commercial purpose of selling or bartering same, repairing same, or recycling
parts from same into other like objects. Such SALVAGE MATERIALS are permitted
only in an official, legally established salvage yard.
      SALVAGE YARD. Any property upon which salvage materials may be legally
stored in the quantities described below:
         (a)   Four or more inoperable vehicles;
         (b)   Any unused or junked manufactured or mobile home to be
dismantled;
         (c)   Four or more inoperable major household appliances;
         (d)   Four or more inoperable pieces of construction equipment;
         (e)   Four or more inoperable pieces of agricultural equipment,
brought in from another property; or
         (f)   Scrap metal, used building materials, and used household
furnishings or goods, or other used materials.
      SEWAGE. Residential wastes, commercial wastes, industrial wastes, and any
drainage, but does not include stormwater.
      SEWERAGE SYSTEM. A system for transporting sewage owned and operated by
the county, or a private disposal system approved by the State Environmental
Department.
      SHALL. Construed as mandatory.
      SITE. A parcel of land, or several contiguous parcels of land, used or
occupied, or to be used or occupied, by a building and accessory buildings, and
the area belonging to such buildings, bounded by a property line or a
designated portion of a public street.
      SOLID WASTE. Any garbage, rubbish, refuse, rejected or waste food, offal,
swill, carrion, ashes, dirt, slop, wastewater, trash, weeds, briers, brush,
junk automobiles or automobile parts, waste, or unwholesome material of any
kind, except sewage, and including residential, commercial, institutional,
industrial, and recreational waste.
      STREET or ROAD. All property dedicated or intended for public or private
access to property, or subject to public easements therefor.
      STRUCTURE. That which is built or constructed, an edifice or building of
any kind, or any piece of work artificially built up or composed of parts
joined together in some definite manner. Without limiting the generality of the
foregoing, STRUCTURE shall include a wall, fence, sign, or billboard.
      TOWING SERVICE. The use of specialized equipment, including repossession
services using towing equipment, to transport:
         (a)   A damaged, disabled, or abandoned motor vehicle and its cargo;
         (b)   A motor vehicle to replace a damaged, disabled, or abandoned
motor vehicle;
         (c)   Parts and equipment to repair a damaged, disabled, or abandoned
motor vehicle;
         (d)   A motor vehicle whose driver has been declared unable to drive
by a law enforcement officer;
         (e)   A motor vehicle whose driver has been removed from the scene or
is unable to drive; or
         (f)   A motor vehicle repossessed or seized pursuant to lawful
authority.
      USE. The use for which land or buildings are occupied or maintained,
arranged, designed, or intended.
      USED TIRE. A tire that previously has been on a vehicle but that retains
suitable tread depth and is free of damage or defects so that it may be safely
returned to its original purpose.
      WASTE TIRE or SCRAP TIRE.
         (a)   A tire that is no longer suitable for its originally intended
purpose because of wear, damage, or defect.
         (b)   This definition shall include a tire mounted on a rim but not on
a vehicle.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)

§ 90.20 MANUFACTURED HOME; MOBILE HOME SALVAGE.
   (A)   No manufactured home/mobile home shall be transported or moved into,
or installed on, any site in the county for the purpose of salvaging parts or
components of such homes for private or personal use, or for sale to others,
except that such homes may be transported to a licensed salvage yard.
   (B)   (1)   For the purpose of this chapter, no manufactured home or mobile
home shall be installed, parked, or located on any site, lot, tract, or parcel
of land to be used for any purpose other than that for which the manufactured
home or mobile home was designed or intended.
      (2)   No person shall use any manufactured home or mobile home for the
sole purpose of the storage of any goods or materials, or for any purpose other
than that for which the manufactured home or mobile home was designed or
intended.

§ 90.22 SALVAGE YARDS.
   (A)   Salvage yards must be legally established in compliance with the laws
prevailing in the county, and all applicable state and federal environmental
laws and regulations. The owner/operator is responsible for identifying all
hazardous materials used, processed, stored, or handled at the facility, and
for maintaining updated qualitative and quantitative records of these materials
at the facility.
   (B)   The abandonment or unauthorized release of hazardous materials is
prohibited. No person shall cause, permit, suffer, or allow the usage, storage,
abandonment, or disposal of hazardous materials:
      (1)   In a manner which violates a provision of any federal, state, or
local government regulations; or
      (2)   In a manner which causes, or may cause, an unauthorized release of
hazardous material.
   (C)   All hazardous material shall be properly stored and be accessible to
inspection at anytime.

§ 90.23 UNLAWFUL BURIAL.
   (A)   Application. This section applies only to the burial or disposal of
human remains outside of formally designated cemeteries, either public or
private.
   (B)   Unlawful burial.
      (1)   In accordance with NMSA § 30-12-14, no person shall use any land or
lands as a burial place or a place of interment within 50 yards from either
side of the bank or border of any stream, river, or any body of water.
      (2)   No person shall use any land or lands as a place of burial or a
place of interment within 100 yards of any county or state road, right-of-way,
easement, or other public way, unless such use preceded the effective date of
this section.

§ 90.24 WASTE TIRES; STORAGE, USE.
   (A)   Except for agricultural uses, a person shall not store or use for any
purpose on any site or lot in the county waste or scrap tires, baled or non-
baled, nor any processed tires, nor any used tires, without the owner of such
site or lot, or his or her authorized agent, obtaining a valid permit for such
storage or use from the county. Any use proposed shall be a beneficial use, and
whether such proposed use is judged to be beneficial shall be in the sole
discretion of the county. Excluded from this requirement are: a retail business
premises where new and used tires are normally sold, and a business where a
tire retreading business is carried on, provided no more than 500 waste or
scrap tires are kept on the business premises at any one time.
   (B)   No person shall engage in the open burning of scrap tires.
   (C)   A person shall not engage in, maintain, or allow illegal dumping of
used, waste, or scrap tires.

§ 90.25 NOISE CAUSED BY UN-MUFFLED PIPES.
   (A)   Intent. The intent of this section is to ensure the citizens an
environment free from excessive sound caused by the use of an un-muffled
retarder device, commonly known as a “Jake brake,” or un-muffled straight
pipes, when a driver is attempting to slow a motor vehicle’s rate of speed
without the use of braking power and instead utilizing any exhaust and/or
engine device.
   (B)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      MOTOR VEHICLE. Any vehicle which is self-propelled.
      PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY. Any street, avenue, boulevard, highway, or alley, or
similar place which is under the authority of the county or the state.
      RETARDER. Any exhaust and/or engine device used as braking power to slow
down a truck, automobile, motorcycle, or other motor vehicle’s rate of speed.
   (C)   Use of retarder devices prohibited. No person shall operate or cause
to be operated any motor vehicle in an attempt to slow the speed of the motor
vehicle with the use of an un-muffled retarder device, commonly known as a
“Jake brake,” or un-muffled straight pipes. It shall be an affirmative defense
that an un-muffled retarder and/or compression brakes were applied in an
emergency to protect persons and/or property.
      (1)   A violation of this section shall be cause for issue of a citation
and a complaint to be filed with the Magistrate Court for the county; and
      (2)   Any uniformed Sheriff’s Deputy shall have, in addition to any other
authority vested in him or her, the power to stop a motor-vehicle reasonably
suspected of violation of this section.
   (D)   Applicable rights-of-way exception.
      (1)   This section shall apply to all public rights-of-way (as defined
herein) within the county outside the boundaries of any municipality.
      (2)   Provided, however, that any such right-of-way or portion of right-
of-way within the county that has been designated by the State Department of
Transportation as a particularly hazardous road upon which the Department has
required the use of a “retarder or other exhaust and/or engine device used as
braking power,” to slow down a truck, automobile, motorcycle, or other motor
vehicle’s rate of speed shall not be subject to the prohibition contained in
this section.
(Ord. 57, passed 11-5-2004) Penalty, see §
90.99
DANGEROUS BUILDINGS
§ 90.40 DANGEROUS BUILDINGS.
   (A)   Defined. The term DANGEROUS BUILDING, as used in this section, is
defined to mean and to include:
      (1)   Any dwelling or other building, with the exception of certain
agricultural buildings that still serve the purpose of storage of agricultural
equipment, supplies, tools, or parts, which is ruined, damaged, and dilapidated
and is dangerous or injurious to the public health, comfort, peace, or safety
of the occupants of the dwelling, the occupants of neighboring dwellings, or
other residents of the area because of its condition, or which has a blighting
influence on properties in the area. The conditions may include the following,
without limitations: defects increasing the hazards of fire, accident, or other
calamities; lack of adequate ventilation, light, or sanitary facilities;
dilapidation; disrepair; structural defects; uncleanliness; overcrowding;
inadequate ingress and egress; inadequate drainage; or any violation of health,
fire, building, or any other regulations relating to the use of land and the
use and occupancy of buildings and improvements; and
      (2)   Any such DANGEROUS BUILDING in the county is declared to be a
nuisance.
   (B)   Permiting of dangerous building. It is unlawful to maintain or permit
the existence of any dangerous building in the county or the failure to repair,
remodel, or renovate a building so designated or moved within the county; and
it is unlawful for the owner, occupant, or person in custody of any dangerous
building to permit the same to remain in a dangerous condition, or to occupy
such building or permit it to be occupied while it remains in a dangerous
condition.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.41 REMOVAL OF DANGEROUS BUILDINGS, DEBRIS.
   (A)   In addition to the provisions of §
90.43(B), whenever any building or structure, except for an agricultural
building which is currently used for the purpose of storage of agricultural
equipment, supplies, tools, or parts, is ruined, damaged, and dilapidated, or
any property is covered with ruins, rubbish, refuse, wreckage, or debris, the
Board of County Commissioners may, by resolution, find that the ruined,
damaged, or dilapidated building, structure, or property is a menace to the
public health, safety, peace, or comfort and require the removal of the
building, structure, ruins, rubbish, refuse wreckage, or debris. COVERED, for
purposes of this section, shall mean any part of the subject property.
   (B)   (1)   A copy of the resolution shall be served on the owner, occupant,
or agent in charge of the building, structure, or property.
      (2)   If the owner, as shown by the real estate records of the County
Clerk, occupant, or agent in charge of the building, structure, or property
cannot be served within the county, a copy of the resolution shall be posted on
the building structure or property, and a copy of the resolution shall be
published one time.
   (C)   Within ten days of the receipt of a copy of the resolution or of the
posting and the publishing of a copy of the resolution, the owner, occupant, or
agent in charge of the building, structure, or property shall commence removing
the building, structure, ruin, rubbish, refuse, wreckage, or debris, or file a
written objection with the County Manager asking for a hearing before the Board
of County Commissioners.
   (D)   If a written objection is filed as required by this section, the Board
of County Commissioners shall:
      (1)   Fix a date for a hearing on its resolution and the objection;
      (2)   Consider all evidence for and against the removal resolution at the
hearing; and
      (3)   Determine if its resolution should be enforced or rescinded.
   (E)   Any person aggrieved by the determination of the Board of County
Commissioners may appeal to the district court by:
      (1)   Giving notice of appeal to the Board of County Commissioners within
five days after the determination made by the Board of County Commissioners;
and
      (2)   Filing a petition in District Court within 20 days after the
determination by the Board of County Commissioners. The District Court shall
hear the matter de novo and enter judgment in accordance with its findings.
   (F)   If the owner, occupant, or agent in charge of the building, structure,
or property fails to commence removing the building, structure, ruins, rubbish,
refuse, wreckage, or debris within ten days of being served a copy of the
resolution or of the posting and the publishing of the resolution, or within
five days of the determination by the governing body that the resolution shall
be enforced;
      (2)   After the district court enters a judgment sustaining the
determination of the Board of County Commissioners, the county may remove the
building, structure, ruins, rubbish, refuse, wreckage, or debris at the cost
and expense of the owner.
      (3)   The reasonable cost of the removal shall constitute a lien against
the building, structure, ruins, rubbish, refuse, wreckage, or debris so removed
and against the lot or parcel of land from which it was removed. The lien shall
be foreclosed in the manner provided in NMSA §§ 3-36-1 through 3-36-6.
   (G)   The county may pay for the costs of removal of any condemned building,
structure, ruins, rubbish, refuse, wreckage, or debris by granting to the
person removing such materials the legal right to all salvageable materials in
lieu of all other compensation.
   (H)   Any person or firm removing any condemned building, structure, ruins,
rubbish, refuse, wreckage, or debris shall leave the property from which the
material has been removed in a clean, level, and safe condition for further
occupancy or construction, and with all excavations filled.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 90.42 EMERGENCY MEASURES.
   (A)   For purposes of this section, EMERGENCY or IMMINENT DANGER shall mean
any condition which could cause serious or life-threatening injury or death at
any time.
   (B)   (1)   Where, in the opinion of the Building Official, or the Code
Compliance Officer, there is imminent danger of failure or collapse of a
building or structure which endangers life, or when any structure or part of a
structure has fallen and life is endangered by the occupation of the structure,
or when there is actual or potential danger to the building occupants or those
in the proximity of any structure because of explosives, explosive fumes, or
vapors, or the presence of toxic fumes, gases, or materials, or operation of
defective or dangerous equipment, the Building Official or the Code Compliance
Officer, with the approval of the County Planning Director, or the County
Manager, is hereby authorized and empowered to order and require the occupants
to vacate the premises forthwith.
      (2)   The County Planning Director, or the Building Official or the Code
Compliance Officer shall cause to be posted at the entrance to such structure a
notice reading as follows: “This Structure is Unsafe and Its Occupancy Has Been
Prohibited by the County Code Compliance Officer (or the Building Official).”
      (3)   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to enter such structure
except for the purpose of securing the structure, making the required repairs,
removing the hazardous condition, or of demolishing the structure.
         (b)   In determining the nature and extent of the imminent danger, the
Building Official or the Code Compliance Officer, with the approval of the
County Planning Director or the County Manager, may engage the services of a
professional engineer licensed in the state, or other knowledgeable
professional.
   (C)   Whenever, in the opinion of the Code Compliance Officer or the
Building Official, there is imminent danger due to an unsafe condition, the
Code Compliance Officer, with the approval of the County Planning Director or
the County Manager, may order the boarding up of openings, to render such
structure temporarily safe, or take such other action as the Code Compliance
Officer or the Building Official deems necessary to meet such emergency.
   (D)   When necessary for public safety, the Code Compliance Officer or the
Building Official, with the approval of the County Planning Director or the
County Manager, shall temporarily close structures and/or order the authority
having jurisdiction to close sidewalks, streets, roads, public ways, and places
adjacent to unsafe structures and prohibit the same from being utilized.
   (E)   For the purposes of administering and enforcing §
90.41, the Code Compliance Officer, with the approval of the County Planning
Director or the County Manager, may employ the necessary labor and materials to
perform the required emergency work as expeditiously as possible.
   (F)   (1)   Costs incurred in the performance of emergency work shall be
paid by the county.
      (2)   The County Attorney shall institute all appropriate action against
the owner of the premises where the unsafe structure is, or was, located for
the recovery of such costs.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010) Penalty, see §
90.99

§ 90.58 NOTICE OF NUISANCE OF VIOLATION.
   (A)   Any condition or situation which violates any of the provisions of
this chapter shall be deemed a nuisance, both public and private in nature.
   (B)   In addition to the criminal penalties provided for in this chapter,
any such nuisance, after reasonable efforts to secure voluntary compliance with
this chapter have failed, shall be subject to abatement as follows.
      (1)   Notice of nuisance.
         (a)   If, after inspection, as the result of a complaint by member of
the public, or the observation of any county or state employee, the Officer is
satisfied that a nuisance does exist, the Officer shall serve, or cause to be
served by personal service, or send by prepaid registered mail to the owner of
record of the property, or to the occupant or tenant of the property, or both,
and to all persons shown by the records to have an interest in the property, a
notice of nuisance or violation setting out the particulars of the violation
(s). The notice shall establish that the abatement of the violation(s) by the
owner or occupant, or tenant or both, shall begin in not more than ten days,
and shall be completed in not more than 90 days after service of the notice.
The notice shall be served at the owner’s or occupant’s, or tenant’s, last
known address.
         (b)   In the event a violation of this chapter constitutes an
immediate danger to the public health and safety, the notice provisions of this
division (B)(1) shall not apply, and the violation may be prosecuted and abated
immediately.
      (2)   Placard. If the Code Compliance Officer is unable to achieve
service under division (B)(1)(a) above, he or she may place a placard
containing the terms of the notice in a conspicuous place on the property or
building, and the placing of the placard shall be deemed to be sufficient
service of the notice on the owner or other persons.
      (3)   Extension of timeframe for abatement. Where the Officer is
satisfied that there is good and sufficient reason to extend the timeframe for
abatement of the violation(s), he or she may extend the timeframe set out in
division (B)(1)(a) above for a period of time not to exceed 45 days beyond the
time period set out in the original notice.
      (4)   Failure to abate. In the event the owner, occupant, or tenant of
the property where the nuisance violation exists has failed to abate the
nuisance violation(s) within the prescribed period of time, then the Officer
shall issue a citation or file a complaint charging violation of this chapter
with the Magistrate Court, or other appropriate court of jurisdiction,
demanding that the owner of the property or the occupant, or both, be held to
answer to the court for the violation.
      (5)   Removal of nuisance. In the event that the person is convicted of
violating this chapter and continues to refuse to abate the violations, the
county or aggrieved property owner may enforce this section in any manner
consistent with law.
      (6)   Injunctions.
         (a)   The county or aggrieved property owner, when a nuisance exists
as set forth herein, may institute civil proceedings in Magistrate Court or
District Court to enjoin all persons from maintaining or permitting, the
nuisance and to abate the same, and for civil damages as may be appropriate.
         (b)   Costs and attorneys fees shall be elements of damage in any
proceeding.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)

§ 90.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   (1)   Any person violating or failing, or refusing to comply with the
provisions of this chapter and the codes adopted may be prosecuted in any court
of competent jurisdiction within the county, and shall be punished by:
         (a)   A fine of not more than $300;
         (b)   A fine of not more than $1,000 for discarding or disposing of
refuse, litter, or garbage on public or private property in any manner other
than by disposing it in an authorized landfill; and/or
         (c)   A fine of not more than $5,000 for the improper or illegal
disposal of hazardous materials or waste in any manner other than as provided
for in the Hazardous Waste Act (NMSA Chapter 74, Article 4); and in accordance
with NMSA § 4-37-3.
      (2)   The Board of County Commissioners may apply to the District Court
for appropriate injunctive relief to compel compliance by any person whose
conduct violates any provision of this chapter. The county shall be entitled to
recover a reasonable attorney’s fee if required to enforce this chapter through
the issuance of a demand letter, or in enforcing any portion of this chapter in
any court of competent jurisdiction. After the effective date of this chapter,
all violations are subject to issuance of a citation.
   (B)   Anyone who does not comply with §
90.23 is guilty of a misdemeanor
   (C)   Any person violating §
90.25 shall be punished by a fine of not more than $300 or by imprisonment not
to exceed 90 days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.
(Ord. 57, passed 11-5-2004; Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
CHAPTER 91: FIRE PROTECTION AND PREVENTION
Section

91.02   Authority

91.06   Permitted open burning

OPEN BURNING
§ 91.01 TITLE.
   This subchapter shall be known as the “Luna County Open Burning Regulation
Ordinance” or “this subchapter.”
(Ord. 84, passed 7-11-2013; Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
§ 91.02 AUTHORITY.
   This subchapter is enacted pursuant to the authority granted to counties
under NMSA §§ 4-37-1 through 4-37-3, 68-2-23, and 68-5-1 et seq. (1978), and in
accordance with 20.2.60 NMAC (Open Burning), to protect the health, safety, and
welfare of the public through the responsible regulation of open burning.
(Ord. 84, passed 7-11-2013; Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
§ 91.03 APPLICABILITY.
   This subchapter applies to all open burning conducted within the
unincorporated areas of the county.
(Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
§ 91.04 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   OPEN BURNING. Any fire where the products of combustion are emitted directly
into the ambient air without passing through a chimney or stack.
   PROHIBITED MATERIALS. Includes, but is not limited to:
      (1)   Plastics;
      (2)   Rubber;
      (3)   Tires;
      (4)   Treated or painted wood;
      (5)   Insulation;
      (6)   Construction and demolition debris;
      (7)   Household garbage and refuse;
      (8)   Asbestos-containing materials;
      (9)   Hazardous waste;
      (10)   Petroleum-based products (e.g., roofing tar and the like);
      (11)   Electrical wiring or appliances; and
      (12)   Any material that emits toxic fumes when burned.
(Ord. 84, passed 7-11-2013; Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
§ 91.05 PROHIBITED BURNING.
   (A)   No person shall conduct open burning of any prohibited materials.
   (B)   No burning shall be conducted during:
      (1)   Red flag warnings issued by the National Weather Service;
      (2)   Periods when wind speeds exceed 15 mph; or
      (3)   Active fire bans issued by state or county authorities or draught
emergencies.
   (C)   Burning must not occur within 50 feet of any structure or combustible
fence.
(Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
§ 91.06 PERMITTED OPEN BURNING.
   Open burning may be conducted only under the following conditions:
   (A)   A valid county burn notice has been issued;
   (B)   The burn is attended at all times by an adult;
   (C)   Water, shovel, extinguisher, or other fire suppression tools are
present;
   (D)   Burning occurs between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., weather permitting;
   (E)   Burn area is cleared of flammable vegetation within a 25-foot radius;
   (F)   Only approved ignition methods are used:
      (1)   Auxiliary fuels no heavier than No. 2 diesel may be used, in the
minimum quantity necessary to start the burn; and
      (2)   Approved incendiary devices may be used if compliant with the same
fuel standards.
   (G)   Daily burn limits shall not exceed:
      (1)   Ten acres per day for non-piled vegetative material; and
      (2)   One thousand cubic feet per day for piled vegetative material.
   (H)   Burns exceeding these limits require compliance with 20.2.65 NMAC
(Smoke Management). For these burns, the applicant must:
      (1)   Submit a smoke management burn plan to the New Mexico Environment
Department (NMED);
      (2)   Receive prior approval from NMED before ignition;
      (3)   Implement emission reduction techniques including fuel moisture
monitoring, timing for dispersion, and contingency actions for smoke
intrusions; and
      (4)   Maintain records and report burn outcomes to NMED as required.
   (I)   The applicant follows all permit conditions and public safety
directions.
(Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
§ 91.07 EXEMPTIONS.
   (A)   Agricultural burning exemption. Agricultural burning that is a
standard part of a commercial agricultural operation (e.g., ditch burning,
field clearing, pest/disease control, and the like) is exempt from permit
requirements, provided that:
      (1)   It is conducted in accordance with best management practices
(BMPs);
      (2)   There is no state or local burn ban in effect; and
      (3)   The fire poses no hazard to life or property.
   (B)   Ceremonial and cultural burning. Open fires used for cultural,
religious, or ceremonial purposes (e.g., tribal practices, seasonal ceremonies,
and the like) are exempt, provided that:
      (1)   Reasonable fire safety measures are taken; and
      (2)   Burning of prohibited materials is strictly avoided.
(Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
§ 91.08 BURN NOTICE APPLICATION PROCESS.
   (A)   Applicants must:
      (1)   Submit a completed burn notice application;
      (2)   Provide details including name, contact information, burn location,
material to be burned, date, and time;
      (3)   Signature acknowledging compliance with this ordinance and safety
practices;
      (4)   Notices may be approved, denied, or revoked by the Planning
Department or fire personnel.
   (B)   Notices are valid only for the date(s) indicated and may be revoked
for noncompliance or hazardous conditions.
(Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
§ 91.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Violations of §§ 91.09 throughout
91.08 are subject to the following pursuant to NMSA 1978, § 4-37-3:
      (1)   A fine not to exceed $500;
      (2)   Imprisonment not exceeding 90 days; or
      (3)   Both such fine and imprisonment.
   (B)   Each day of violation shall constitute a separate offense.
   (C)   The county may recover the costs of emergency response or fire
suppression services resulting from illegal or non-compliant burning
activities.
   (D)   Violations may also be referred to the State Environment Department or
other applicable state agencies for further enforcement under 20.2.60 NMAC.
(Ord. 84, passed 7-11-2013; Res. 25-47, passed 7-10-2025)
