BUSINESS REGISTRATION FEE
§ 110.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BOARD. The Board of County Commissioners.
   BUSINESS REGISTRATION FEE. The fees imposed by this subchapter.
   COUNTY. The County of Luna, State of New Mexico.
   ENGAGING IN BUSINESS. Operating, conducting, doing, carrying on, or causing
to be carried on or pursuing any business, including any profession,
occupation, or trade located within the boundaries of the county but outside
the boundaries of an incorporated municipality.
   PERSON. Any person or other legal entity subject to this subchapter.
(Ord. 5, passed 12-14-2023)
§ 110.02 EXEMPTIONS.
   (A)   This subchapter shall not apply to those persons:
      (1)   Engaged solely in farming and ranching;
      (2)   Who have annual gross sales, trades, or exchanges of less than $500
in the county;
      (3)   Engaging in charitable, educational, religious, benevolent, civic,
patriotic, political, social, fraternal, literary, cultural, or athletic fund-
raising purposes; and
      (4)   Who are vendors registered with a duly organized and active club,
society, organization, or association within the county which sponsors annual
community events in the county open to the general public.
   (B)   In such cases, said vendors shall not be required to pay the business
registration fee, but the sponsor shall pay a fixed fee, called a canopy fee,
of $125 annually.
(Ord. 5, passed 12-14-2023)
§ 110.03 IMPOSITION OF FEE.
   (A)   A fee is imposed on all persons engaging in business in the county, as
defined in §
110.01, except for those persons exempt in §
110.02. The fee applies to businesses located within the boundaries of the
county but outside the boundaries of an incorporated municipality.
   (B)   It also applies to businesses located within a municipality who also
conduct business within county jurisdiction.
(Ord. 5, passed 12-14-2023)
§ 110.04 RATE OF FEE.
   All persons engaging in business shall pay an annual license fee of $35 per
business, except as provided in §
110.02.
(Ord. 5, passed 12-14-2023)
§ 110.05 PAYMENT OF FEE.
   Each person having a business subject to the business registration fee shall
pay the business registration fee to the Planning Department by July 1 of each
year for the fiscal year ending June 30 of the following year. Any portion of
the business registration fee that remains unpaid by July 11 is delinquent.
(Ord. 5, passed 12-14-2023)
§ 110.06 ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   If any person engaging in business fails to pay the business
registration fee, as required by §
110.03, they shall be liable for the fee and a penalty of $250, and all costs
incurred by the Planning Department in the enforcement of this subchapter, made
payable to the Planning Department.
   (B)   If a person engaging in business fails to pay the business
registration fee required by this subchapter, the Planning Department shall
mail the person notice of the amount owed by certified mail, return receipt
requested.
   (C)   If the fees, along with penalty payments, are not made by the business
within 15 days of receipt of such notice by the person engaging in business,
the Planning Department may bring an action in law or equity in Magistrate
Court for the collection of any amounts due, including, without limitation, any
penalties thereon, the costs of collection, and reasonable attorney’s fees
incurred in connection therewith.
(Ord. 5, passed 12-14-2023)
CERTIFICATION
§ 110.20 SHORT TITLE.
   This subchapter may be cited as the “Luna County Procurement Preference
Ordinance,” or the “Procurement Preference,” or “this subchapter.”
(Ord. 82, passed 6-14-2012)
§ 110.21 APPLICABILITY.
   This subchapter shall apply to procurement by the county under state law and
the county’s procurement regulations. This subchapter shall not apply to
procurement by the county that is governed pursuant to a grant agreement by the
federal acquisition regulations, 48 C.F.R. part 1 et seq.
(Ord. 82, passed 6-14-2012)
§ 110.22 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COUNTY BUDGET/PROCUREMENT DIRECTOR or PROCUREMENT MANAGER. The person
appointed to serve as the county’s Procurement Manager.
   COUNTY BUSINESS. A business that holds a current county business certificate
at the time of application for a preference certificate pursuant to this
subchapter (or the appropriate municipal business license, if located within a
municipality) that has its primary and permanent office or business location
within the exterior boundaries of the county for at least one year preceding
the submission of an application for a county procurement preference, and
which, if a foreign corporation, has filed a unitary return pursuant to the
Corporate Income and Franchise Tax Act, being NMSA §§ 7-2A-1 et seq., and NMSA
§ 7-2A-8.3, or as amended.
   COUNTY BUSINESS CERTIFICATE or BUSINESS CERTIFICATE. The certificate issued
to a business engaged in business within the unincorporated limits of the
county.
   COUNTY PREFERENCE CERTIFICATE or PREFERENCE CERTIFICATE. The certificate
authorized pursuant to §
110.23(B).
(Ord. 82, passed 6-14-2012)
§ 110.23 PROCUREMENT PREFERENCE.
   (A)   (1)   A county procurement preference is hereby established, as
described in this subchapter.
      (2)   When the county procures services using competitive sealed
proposals pursuant to NMSA § 13-1-111, or as amended, an offer submitted by a
county business shall be deemed to receive 5% of the overall totals points
awarded in connection with the evaluation of the proposals.
      (3)   When the county procures goods or services and pursuant to NMSA §
13-1-21, or as amended, a county business shall be deemed to receive a 5%
preference towards the overall award.
      (4)   In applying the preference provided in this subchapter, the county
procurement preference certificate shall be applied in addition to any other
preference required by law.
   (B)   A county business shall be eligible to utilize the preference
established in this subchapter only when presenting, prior to or at the time
established in the solicitation for receipt of proposals or competitive sealed
bids, a county preference certificate issued by the Procurement Manager.
(Ord. 82, passed 6-14-2012)
§ 110.24 OBTAINING A PREFERENCE CERTIFICATE.
   (A)   A county business may obtain a preference certificate by filing an
application with the Procurement Manager.
   (B)   The application shall be completed on a form provided by the
Procurement Manger that contains a sworn affidavit from the president or owner
of the business setting forth each of the following:
      (1)   The name, address, telephone number, and name of the business and
its registered agent (if applicable);
      (2)   If a corporation, information that the corporation is registered to
do business in the state and is in good standing, and provides a certificate of
good standing from the State Taxation and Revenue Department;
      (3)   If the business is a foreign corporation, information that the
business is registered to do business in the state and is in good standing, and
provides a certificate of good standing from the State Taxation and Revenue
Department;
      (4)   A copy of a valid business registration to do business in the
county (or a copy of the appropriate municipal business license, if located
within a municipality within the county);
      (5)   A statement that the business has maintained its primary and
permanent office or business location within the exterior boundaries of the
county for at least one year preceding the submission of the application; and
      (6)   If a foreign corporation, copies of the most recent state and
federal tax returns applicable to the business.
   (C)   The Procurement Manager shall issue a preference certificate if the
application demonstrates, to the satisfaction of the Procurement Manager, that
the business holds a current business certificate at the time of application
for a preference certificate pursuant to this subchapter (or the appropriate
municipal business license, if located witl1in a municipality), that the
business has its primary and permanent office or business location within the
exterior boundaries of the county, and has maintained its primary and permanent
office or business location within the exterior boundaries of the county for at
least one consecutive year preceding the submission of the application, and if
a foreign corporation, has filed a unitary return pursuant to the Corporate
Income and Franchise Tax Act, being NMSA §§ 7-2A-1 et seq., and NMSA § 7-2A-
8.3, or as amended.
(Ord. 82, passed 6-14-2012)
§ 110.25 DENIAL OF CERTIFICATE; PROTEST, REVOCATION.
   (A)   If the Purchasing Manager determines that an applicant is not eligible
for certification, the Purchasing Manager shall deny the application and shall
issue a notice of denial.
   (B)   A business whose application for a preference certificate is denied
may protest the denial to the Procurement Manager in conformity with the
protest procedures of the purchasing regulations.
   (C)   If facts are developed by the Procurement Manager that information
provided by an applicant seeking a preference certificate has provided
inaccurate or misleading information that resulted in the issuance of a
certificate, the Procurement Manager shall revoke the certificate and notify
the applicant.
(Ord. 82, passed 6-14-2012)
§ 110.26 EXPIRATION OF PERMIT.
   The preference certificate shall be valid for two years from date of its
issuance. A new application will be required every two years to determine
eligibility for the procurement preference.
(Ord. 82, passed 6-14-2012)
§ 110.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   Any business violating the provisions of §§
110.01 through
110.06. shall be subject to penalties of not to exceed 90 days in jail or $300
fine for each violation.
      (2)   Knowingly providing false or misleading information on an
application for a procurement preference shall constitute a violation of §§
110.20 through
110.26, and shall be punished as set forth in NMSA § 4-37-3, or as amended;
knowingly providing false or misleading information on an application for a
procurement preference may also expose the person providing such information to
additional criminal penalties as provided by state law.
(Ord. 82, passed 6-14-2012; Ord. 5, passed 12-14-2023)
CHAPTER 111: SOLICITORS AND PEDDLERS
Section

§ 111.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   PEDDLER. Any person, whether a resident of the county or not, traveling by
foot, automobiles, motor truck, or any other type of conveyance, from place to
place, from house to house, or from street to street, carrying, conveying, or
transporting unsolicited goods, wares, merchandise, meat, fish, vegetables,
fruits, or truck garden or farm products or provisions, offering and exposing
them for sale, or making sales and delivering articles to purchasers.
   SOLICITOR. Any person, whether a resident of the county or not, traveling
either by foot, automobile, motor truck, or any other type of conveyance, from
place to place, from house to house, or from street to street, taking or
attempting to take orders for sale of goods, wares, and merchandise, personal
property, of any nature whatsoever, for future delivery, or for services,
whether or not such individual has, carries, or exposes for sale a sample of
the subject of such sale, or whether he or she is collecting advance payment on
such sales or not.
(Ord. 11, passed 3-19-1986)
§ 111.02 APPLICATION.
   (A)   Applications for licenses by solicitors and peddlers shall by made to
the County Clerk, shall be sworn and in writing, and shall contain the
following information:
      (1)   Name and physical description of the applicant;
      (2)   Address;
      (3)   A brief description of the nature of the business to be conducted
and the goods to be sold, and, if the goods are farm or orchard products, a
statement whether they are produced or grown by the applicant;
      (4)   If the applicant is employed, the name and address of the employer,
together with credentials establishing the exact relationship;
      (5)   The length of time for which the right to do business is desired;
      (6)   If a vehicle is to be used, a description of the same, together
with the state vehicle license number or other means of identification; and
      (7)   A statement as to whether or not the applicant has been convicted
of any crime, misdemeanor, or violation of any municipal ordinance, and if so,
the nature of the offense, and the punishment or penalty assessed therefor.
   (B)   An applicant for a solicitor’s or peddler’s permit shall supply the
County Clerk with one photograph at the time of the application, which
photograph shall show the head and shoulders of the applicant in a clear and
distinguishing manner.
(Ord. 11, passed 3-19-1986)
§ 111.03 LICENSE FEES FOR SOLICITORS, PEDDLERS.
   The fee for solicitors and peddlers shall be:
   (A)   Twenty-five dollars per year for all peddlers and solicitors having an
established place of business within the county; and
   (B)   One hundred dollars per day.
(Ord. 11, passed 3-19-1986)
§ 111.04 REGULATIONS.
   (A)   A peddler or solicitors, or any person on his or her behalf, shall
not:
      (1)   Shout, make any outcry, blow a horn, ring a bell, or use any sound
device or musical instrument, including any loud speaking radio or sound
amplifying system, on any of the streets or other public places of the county
or on any private premises in the county where sound of sufficient volume is
emitted or produced therefrom to be capable of being plainly heard on such
public places, for the purpose of attracting attention to any goods, wares, or
merchandise which such licensee proposes to sell;
      (2)   (a)   Have any exclusive right to any location in the public
streets, shall not be permitted a stationary location, and shall not be
permitted to operate in any congested area where his or her operations might
impede or inconvenience the public; and
         (b)   For the purpose of this chapter, the judgment of a law
enforcement officer, exercised in good faith, shall be deemed conclusive as to
whether the area is congested or the public impeded or inconvenienced.
      (3)   Sell or offer for sale goods, wares, or merchandise from vehicles
on any of the public streets of the county, provided however, that the
prohibition herein contained shall not include the peddling from door to door
or from vehicles of fresh food products of farm or garden, nor bona fide
deliveries of goods, wares, merchandise, or food made on a regular route to
regular customers;
      (4)   Solicit or peddle from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 a.m., or any time when a
sign has been posted on a building stating “No solicitors or peddlers,” or
words to that effect, except that a licensed solicitor or peddler may call upon
the occupant of a residence at other times when he or she has received express
prior permission from such occupant to do so; and/or
      (5)   Cast, throw, distribute, deposit, scatter, pass out, give away,
circulate, or deliver any commercial or business handbill, dodger, circular, or
other advertising material or device to any residence or business, or leave the
same on any porch, doorstep, or vestibule thereof, or in any yard or public
hallway thereof, or on any vacant lot or other private property in the county,
without first having obtained the express consent or without the express
request of an adult resident or occupant thereof.
   (B)   This chapter shall not prohibit solicitations for a charitable,
religious, education, community, recreational, or similar non-profit purpose by
means of calling upon places of residences or by means of direct personal
contact in public places or upon public property.
(Ord. 11, passed 3-19-1986) Penalty, see §
111.99

CHAPTER 112: SALVAGE YARDS
Section
   
112.01   Regulations
   
112.02   Screening
   
112.03   Unlicensed salvage yards
   
112.04   Agricultural equipment salvage materials
   
112.05   Violations
§ 112.01 REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Only salvage yards licensed by the State Department of Motor Vehicles
may carry on or conduct the active trade or business of dismantling any vehicle
for the resale of parts. Any person possessing more than three wrecked,
dismantled, or partially wrecked or dismantled vehicles, and selling or
offering for sale a used part, and who regularly sells or offers for sale used
vehicles or used vehicle parts, shall be presumed to be conducting the business
of wrecking or dismantling a vehicle for the resale of the parts.
   (B)   All legally established salvage yard shall be adequately screened as
defined in §
112.02.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010) Penalty, see §
10.99
Cross-reference:
   Dealers, wreckers, and dismantlers, see
Chapter 113
§ 112.02 SCREENING.
   (A)   Any salvage yard existing on the effective date of this chapter shall
be adequately screened from any public right-of-way or from any residential
property within 200 yards of the salvage yard.
   (B)   ADEQUATELY SCREENED, for purposes of this section, shall mean solid or
opaque fencing, or trees, shrubs, or other vegetation that is of sufficient
height and density to fully obscure the view of the salvage materials from a
point eight feet above the ground on any public right-of-way, or any
residential property within 200 yards of the salvage yard. Construction
materials, such as lumber, brick, or stone, used for fencing and screening
shall be durable and in good condition, securely anchored, and fastened to
protect it from damage sustained by wind. Use of old metals, poor quality
building materials, and materials such as wood boxes, crates or pallets, and
used tires is prohibited, unless previously approved by the LCBO or the Code
Compliance Officer. Building permits are required for fences six feet or more
in height.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 112.03 UNLICENSED SALVAGE YARDS.
   Any unlicensed salvage yard existing on any site in the county on the
effective date of this chapter shall discontinue all operation on the effective
date of this chapter. All salvage materials, and any and all items intended for
salvage, and all equipment and machinery associated with the salvage operation,
shall be removed from the site to either a licensed salvage yard or to a
location outside of the county. The site shall be left in a clean and tidy
condition to the satisfaction of the County Code Compliance Officer. Failure to
comply may result in the county invoking abatement measures as set out in §§
90.55 through
90.59. Any owner of such site that does not comply with this section shall be
subject to the penalties set out in §§
90.55 through
90.59.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 112.04 AGRICULTURAL EQUIPMENT SALVAGE MATERIALS.
   Any persons in the county engaged in agricultural operations shall be
permitted to maintain agricultural equipment salvage materials on their
property for parts, repair, and replacement purposes.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 112.05 VIOLATIONS.
   Any person, property owner, or property occupant that commits or knowingly
allows the commission of any act in violation of this chapter, shall, upon
conviction, be subject to the same penalties as set forth in §§
90.55 through
90.59.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
CHAPTER 113: DEALERS, WRECKERS, DISMANTLERS; TOWING OPERATIONS
Section
Towing Operations
   
113.01   Screening
Dealers, Wreckers, Dismantlers
   
113.15   Licensing

TOWING OPERATIONS
§ 113.01 SCREENING.
   All towing services operating in the county shall be legally established and
shall abide by the following regulations: All vehicles, including trailers and
mobile homes, towed by a towing service shall be stored in a yard that is
adequately screened. For purposes of this section, ADEQUATELY SCREENED shall
have the same meaning as is set out in §
112.02(B).
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
DEALERS, WRECKERS, DISMANTLERS
§ 113.15 LICENSING.
   All dealers, wreckers, wholesalers, and distributors of any vehicle, and
title service companies and any towing operation engaged in the business of
selling, wrecking, wholesaling, or distributing vehicles, shall be legally
established, meaning licensed by the Motor Vehicle Division of the Department
of Taxation and Revenue as set out in NMSA § 66-4-1.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 113.16 REGULATIONS.
   Any dealer or wrecker, or any towing service engaged in the business of the
dealing or the wrecking of vehicles, shall comply with the following
regulations and criteria: An established place of business must be maintained.
An ESTABLISHED PLACE OF BUSINESS shall be as defined in the State Motor Vehicle
Code, and for purposes of this subchapter shall mean a place:
   (A)   Devoted exclusively to the business for which the dealer or wrecker is
licensed and the business incidental thereto;
   (B)   Identified by a prominently displayed sign giving the dealer’s or
wrecker’s trade name used by the business;
   (C)   Of sufficient size or space to permit the display of one or more
vehicles or to permit the parking or storing of vehicles to be dismantled or
wrecked;
   (D)   On which there is located an enclosed building on a permanent
foundation, which building meets the building requirements of the county and is
large enough to accommodate the office or offices of the dealer or the wrecker,
and large enough to provide a safe place to keep the books and records of the
dealer or wrecker;
   (E)   Where the principal portion of the business of the dealer or wrecker
is conducted and where the books and records of the business are kept and
maintained; and
   (F)   (1)   Where vehicle sales are of new vehicles only, such as a
department store or a franchise of a department store, as long as the
department store or franchise keeps the books and records of its vehicle
business in a general office location at its place of business.
      (2)   As used in this section, DEPARTMENT STORE means a business that
offers a variety of merchandise other than vehicles, and sales of the
merchandise other than vehicles constitutes at least 80% of the gross sales of
the business.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
§ 113.17 PHYSICAL PLACE OF BUSINESS.
   Any title service company must maintain a physical place of business
accessible to the public. Each such place of business shall be open to
inspection by a law enforcement officer or the Department of Taxation and
Revenue during reasonable business hours.
(Ord. 74, passed 4-8-2010)
CHAPTER 114: SEXUALLY-ORIENTED BUSINESSES
Section
   
114.01   Purpose; policy; authority; exclusion

114.03   Obscene display or distribution
   
114.04   Destruction of materials seized

§ 114.01 PURPOSE; POLICY; AUTHORITY; EXCLUSION.
   (A)   The Board of County Commissioners, hereinafter “the Board,” hereby
declares the promotion, commercial exhibition, or sale or possession for such
purposes of obscene material as defined herein to be public nuisances per se.
   (B)   Nothing herein is intended to cover, affect, include, or proscribe the
specific conduct, matters, or material which are prohibited or regulated as to
minors by, or to apply to minors who are protected by NMSA §§ 30-37-1 through
30-37-8. Neither is this chapter intended to apply to any matter used in a bona
fide program of medical or psychological treatment, or a distributed or
displayed non-profit program by a publicly owned or other non-profit library or
educational institution, or used in a bona fide educational program of a bona
fide for-profit educational institution; or while used, distributed, displayed,
or sold or held for use, distribution, display, or sale exclusively under these
conditions. Nor is this chapter intended to apply to possession of obscene
material in a private home for exclusively private use.
(Ord. 14, passed 6-8-1990)
§ 114.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COMMUNITY. The geographical area of the county.
   MATERIAL. Anything tangible that is capable of being used or adapted to
arouse interest, whether through the medium of reading, observation, sound, or
in any other manner, which includes, but is not limited to, magazines, books,
leaflets, pamphlets, booklets, pictures, photographs, drawings, films,
negatives, videos, slides, or motion pictures, but does not include an actual
three-dimensional obscene device.
   OBSCENE. Material or performance that:
      (1)   The average person, applying contemporary community standards,
would find that, taken as a whole, appeals to the prurient interest in sex.
      (2)   The average person, applying contemporary community standards,
would find that it depicts or describes:
         (a)   Patently offensive representations or descriptions of ultimate
sexual acts, normal or perverted, actual or simulated, including sexual
intercourse, sodomy, and sexual bestiality; or
         (b)   Patently offensive representations or descriptions of
masturbation, excretory functions, sadism, masochism, lewd exhibition of the
genitals, the male or female genitals in a state of sexual stimulation or
arousal, covered male genitals in a discernibly turgid state, or a device
designed and marketed as useful primarily for stimulation of the human genital
organs.
      (3)   Reasonable person would find, taken as a whole, lacks serious
literary, artistic, political, or scientific value.
   OBSCENE DEVICE. A device including a dildo, or artificial vagina designed or
marketed as useful primarily for the stimulation of human genital organs.
   PERFORMANCE. A play, motion picture, dance, or other exhibition performed
before an audience.
   PROMOTE. To manufacture, issue, sell, give, provide, lease, rent, deliver,
transfer, transmit, publish, distribute, circulate, disseminate, present,
exhibit, or advertise, or to offer or agree to do the same. Nothing herein
shall be construed so as to restrict or prohibit the use of material or devices
by adults in the privacy of personal residences not for monetary gain or
valuable consideration.
   PRURIENT INTEREST. A lascivious, shameful, or morbid interest in sex.
(Ord. 14, passed 6-8-1990)
§ 114.03 OBSCENE DISPLAY OR DISTRIBUTION.
   A person commits an offense if he or she, knowing its contents and
character:
   (A)   Promotes or possesses with intent to promote any obscene material or
obscene device; or
   (B)   Produces, presents, or directs an obscene performance.
(Ord. 14, passed 6-8-1990)
§ 114.04 DESTRUCTION OF MATERIALS SEIZED.
   Any material or device, as previously defined in this chapter, seized
pursuant to this chapter is contraband and shall be destroyed after obtaining
an order for its destruction from the court.
(Ord. 14, passed 6-8-1990)
§ 114.99 PENALTY.
   An offense under this chapter is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to
exceed $300 or imprisonment for 90 days, or both.
(Ord. 14, passed 6-8-1990)

CURFEW FOR MINORS
§ 130.01 SHORT TITLE.
   The subchapter shall be known as the “Daytime Curfew Ordinance” and shall be
referred to herein as “the ordinance” or “this subchapter.”
(Ord. 31, passed 8-14-1997)
§ 130.02 AUTHORITY.
   This subchapter is enacted as an exercise of the county’s inherent police
power to protect the citizenry and peace within the county.
(Ord. 31, passed 8-14-1997)
§ 130.03 GENERAL PROHIBITION.
   (A)   No person under the age of 18 years and subject to the compulsory
school attendance law shall be upon or about public streets, public places, or
public places of amusement and entertainment within the county during the hours
when said person is required, by state law, to be in attendance at either a
public or private school, a home school, or a state institution.
   (B)   It is an exemption to a violation under this section that the person
engaged in the prohibited conduct while:
      (1)   Accompanied by the minor’s parent or guardian;
      (2)   On an errand at the direction of the minor’s parent or guardian,
without any detour or stop;
      (3)   In a motor vehicle involved in interstate travel;
      (4)   Engaged in an employment activity, or going to or returning home
from an employment activity, without any detour or stop;
      (5)   Involved in an emergency;
      (6)   On the sidewalk abutting the minor’s residence or abutting the
residence of a next-door neighbor if the neighbor did not complain to the
Police Department about the minor’s presence;
      (7)   Attending an official school, religious, or other recreational
activity supervised by adults and sponsored by the city or county civic
organization, or another similar entity that takes responsibility for the
minor, or going to or returning home from, without any detour or stop, an
official school, religious, or other recreational activity supervised by adults
and sponsored by the city, a civic organization, or another similar entity that
takes responsibility for the minor;
      (8)   Exercising First Amendment rights protected by the United States
Constitution, such as the free exercise of religion, freedom of speech, and the
right of assembly; or
      (9) Married or has been married been married or had disabilities of
minority removed in accordance with state law.
(Ord. 31, passed 8-14-1997) Penalty, see §
130.99
§ 130.04 ACCESSORY.
   It shall be unlawful for a person to encourage or assist any person subject
to the compulsory school attendance law to fail or refuse to attend or return
to school unless said absence is excused by an appropriate school official, or
such absence is excused herein or otherwise recognized by state law.
(Ord. 31, passed 8-14-1997) Penalty, see §
130.99
§ 130.05 PARENTAL RESPONSIBILITY
   When a person subject to the compulsory school attendance law is found to be
in violation of this section, the parent or legal guardian shall be cited and
fined in accordance with the penalties herein. It is the intention of this
section to hold the parents or legal guardian vicariously and strictly liable.
(Ord. 31, passed 8-14-1997)
CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOL
§ 130.20 FINDINGS.
   (A)   Minors often obtain, possess, or consume alcoholic beverages at
underage or unruly gatherings held at private residences or at rented
residential and commercial premises under the control of a person who knows, or
should know, of such conduct but fails to stop it.
   (B)   Underage consumption of alcoholic beverages poses an immediate threat
to the public health, safety, and welfare in that it increases alcohol abuse by
minors, physical altercations, violent crimes, including rape and other sexual
offenses, accidental injury, neighborhood vandalism, and excessive noise
disturbance, all of which may require intervention by local law enforcement.
Underage or unruly gatherings with large numbers of underage drinkers and
inadequate or no adult supervision are particularly high risk settings for
these adverse consequences.
   (C)   The State Department of Health conducts a youth risk and resiliency
survey every two years in middle and high schools across the state, including
Deming Public Schools. The survey asks students to report on a variety of
behavior indicators, including underage alcohol consumption. In 2013, the most
recent year for which data is available, youth in the county surpassed the
state averages in most indicators measuring alcohol consumption, including the
most dangerous categories of binge drinking (four or more drinks for a female
in one session, and five or more drinks for a male in one session) and extreme
binge drinking (ten or more drinks in a session). Thirty percent of high school
students reported binge drinking. See Attachment A and Attachment B of the
survey attached to the ordinance codified in this subchapter for study
methodology and full breakdown of alcohol-related statistics from middle and
high school students in Deming Public Schools.
   (D)   Eighty percent of the high school students who admitted to drinking
alcohol indicated they had consumed it in a social setting, either at their own
home or another person’s home. See Attachment B, page 38 of the survey attached
to the ordinance codified in this subchapter.
   (E)   Owners of private property who have been notified, in writing, in
accordance with this subchapter that their tenants are hosting or otherwise
permitting underage or unruly gatherings where alcoholic beverages are served
to or consumed by underage persons have a responsibility to ensure that such
activities do not recur on their property. The failure to take action after
such notice causes serious disruption to the quiet enjoyment of neighboring
residents and impacts to the health and well-being of underage persons and the
community at large.
   (F)   Law enforcement responses to disturbances involving underage
consumption of alcoholic beverages at underage or unruly gatherings frequently
require the use of extensive resources. Further, when law enforcement personnel
respond to disturbances at underage or unruly gatherings it limits their
ability to respond to other service calls in the community, thereby placing the
community at increased risk. Law enforcement is not currently reimbursed for
their expenses when called to an underage or unruly gathering. Providing law
enforcement the authority to direct the host to disperse the gathering and to
cite the responsible persons will ease the burden on law enforcement personnel
to control and deter such gatherings.
   (G)   Law enforcement, fire, and other emergency response services personnel
are required to respond, sometimes on multiple occasions, to underage or unruly
gatherings at private residences and other private property at which alcoholic
beverages are served to or consumed by underage persons, and responses to such
gatherings result in a disproportionate expenditure of public safety resources
of the county, which are underwritten by gross receipts and property taxes paid
to the county by its taxpayers and residents, and delaying police responses to
regular and emergency calls to the rest of the county.
   (H)   In 2013, underage drinking cost the state approximately $478 million
in costs related to youth violence, youth traffic crashes, high-risk sex, youth
injury, and other factors. See Attachment C of the survey attached to the
ordinance codified in this subchapter for fact sheet and sources.
   (I)   The prohibitions found in this subchapter are reasonable and expected
to deter minors from obtaining, possessing, and consuming alcoholic beverages
by holding responsible persons who encourage, are aware of, or should be aware
of, the illegal conduct yet fail to prevent it.
   (J)   For these reasons, the county declares that underage drinking or
unruly gatherings at private residences or other private property are a threat
to the public peace, health, safety, and general welfare, and a public
nuisance.
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)
§ 130.21 PURPOSE.
   The purposes of this subchapter are:
   (A)   To protect the public health, safety, general welfare, and quiet
enjoyment of residential property; and
   (B)   To facilitate the enforcement of laws prohibiting the service of
alcoholic beverages to underage persons, and the consumption or possession of
alcoholic beverages by underage persons.
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)
§ 130.22 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE. Any liquid or solid material intended to be ingested by
a person which contains ethanol, also known as ethyl alcohol, drinking alcohol,
or alcohol, including, but not limited to, alcoholic beverages as defined in
NMSA § 60-3A-3, intoxicating liquor, malt beverage, beer, wine, spirits,
liqueur, whiskey, rum, vodka, cordials, gin, and brandy, and any mixture
containing one or more alcoholic beverages. ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE includes a
mixture of one or more alcoholic beverages whether found or ingested separately
or as a mixture.
   CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE. A drug or substance, the possession and use of which
is regulated under the federal Controlled Substances Act, being 21 U.S.C. §§
801 et seq. Such term does not include any drug or substance for which the
individual found to have consumed such substance has a valid prescription
issued by a licensed medical practitioner authorized to issue such a
prescription.
   LEGAL GUARDIAN. A person who is lawfully vested with the power and charged
with the duty of taking care of a minor.
   MINOR or UNDERAGE PERSON. Any person under the age of 21 years.
   PARENT. Any person who is a natural parent, an adoptive parent, a foster
parent, or a step-parent.
   PRIVATE RESIDENCE or OTHER PRIVATE PROPERTY. A home, yard, apartment,
condominium, or hotel or motel room, or other dwelling unit, or a hall or
meeting room, whether occupied on a temporary or permanent basis, whether
occupied as a dwelling, party, or other social function, and whether owned,
leased, rented, or used with or without compensation, including contiguous
properties, and/or any buildings, structures, or other improvements situated
thereon or affixed thereto.
   PROPERTY OWNER. The owner of a private residence or other private property
as determined by the records of the County Assessor’s office.
   RESPONSE COSTS. The costs associated with responses by law enforcement,
fire, and other emergency response providers to loud or unruly gatherings
including, but not limited to:
      (1)   Salaries and benefits of law enforcement, fire, or other emergency
response personnel for the amount of time spent responding to, remaining at, or
otherwise dealing with loud or unruly gatherings, and the administrative costs
attributable to such response(s);
      (2)   The cost of any medical treatment to or for any law enforcement,
fire, or other emergency response personnel injured responding to, remaining
at, or leaving the scene of a loud or unruly gathering; or
      (3)   The cost of repairing any county equipment or property damaged, and
the cost of the use of any such equipment, in responding to, remaining at, or
leaving the scene of a loud or unruly gathering.
   RESPONSIBLE PERSON. A person or persons with a right of possession in the
private residence or other private property on which an underage or unruly
gathering is conducted, including, but is not limited to:
      (1)   The person who owns, rents, leases, or otherwise has control of the
premises where the gathering occurs;
      (2)   A tenant or lessee of the residence or other private property;
      (3)   Any other person in charge of the private residence or other
private property;
      (4)   The person who organizes or supervises, or conducts, the event or
any other person(s) accepting responsibility for such a gathering; and
      (5)   A property owner that has been sent three notifications within a
12-month period of citations for underage drinking or unruly gatherings having
been issued on property owned by a property owner.
   UNDERAGE GATHERING. A party or gathering of two or more persons at a private
residence or other private property at which alcoholic beverages are being
furnished to, consumed by, or in possession of any underage person.
   UNRULY GATHERING.
      (1)   A party or gathering of two or more persons at a private residence
or other private property where conduct is occurring that constitutes a
substantial disturbance of the quiet enjoyment of private or public property,
as determined by law enforcement.
      (2)   Such conduct includes, but is not limited to:
         (a)   Excessive noise;
         (b)   Excessive traffic that is an impediment to the normal amount of
pedestrian and vehicle traffic;
         (c)   Use of a controlled substance by any person at the gathering;
         (d)   Obstruction of public streets and/or the presence of unruly
crowds that have spilled into public streets;
         (e)   Public drunkenness or unlawful consumption, possession, or
furnishing of alcohol or alcoholic beverages;
         (f)   Assaults, batteries, fights, domestic violence, or other
disturbances of the peace;
         (g)   Vandalism;
         (h)   Litter; or
         (i)   Any other conduct which constitutes a threat to the public
health, safety, quiet enjoyment of residential property, or the general
welfare.
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)
§ 130.23 RESPONSIBILITY FOR PROPER PROPERTY OWNERSHIP.
   Every owner, occupant, lessee, or holder of any possessory interest of a
private residence or other private property within the county is required to
maintain, manage, and supervise the property and all persons thereon in a
manner so as not to violate the provisions of this subchapter.
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)
§ 130.24 PROHIBITED ACTS.
   (A)   It is unlawful for any responsible person to host, conduct, aid,
allow, permit, or condone an underage gathering or unruly gathering at any
private residence or other private property.
   (B)   A responsible person who hosts an event or gathering as described in
division (A) above does not have to be present at the event or gathering to be
held responsible for civil penalties and/or response costs.
   (C)   This subchapter does not apply to conduct solely between an underage
person and his or her parents while present in a private residence or other
private property.
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015) Penalty, see §
130.99
§ 130.25 DEDICATION OF FUNDS.
   (A)   All revenue collected from penalties for violation of this subchapter
shall be deposited in an account dedicated to funding activities associated
with this subchapter.
   (B)   Funding shall be placed toward enforcement and administration through
the County Sheriff’s office.
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)
§ 130.26 ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   This subchapter can be enforced by any commissioned law enforcement
officer in the county.
   (B)   When a law enforcement officer makes an initial response to an
underage gathering or unruly gathering at a residence or other private property
within the county, the officer may issue a citation for violation of this
subchapter to all identified responsible persons.
   (C)   If the responsible person present at the time of the violation is
underage then the officer may subsequently return to the residence or other
private property and issue a citation to a then-present responsible person(s)
and warning to the property owner.
   (D)   If the resident of the private property is a renter, then within 30
calendar days of initial citation of the renter for violation of this
subchapter, a copy of the written warning shall be transmitted to the property
owner of record. If the renter of said rental property violates this subchapter
three times or more within a 12-month period and written notification has been
provided the property owner, the property owner shall be subject to fines
following the fine schedule. It is the responsibility of property owners to
ensure their tenants are not reoccurring hazards to public safety.
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)
§ 130.27 RECOVERY OF RESPONSE COSTS.
   When a law enforcement officer issues a second or subsequent citation within
12-months of an earlier citation given to responsible person(s) at the same
residence or private property, all responsible persons who received a previous
warning may be held jointly and severally liable for the county’s response
costs concerning such second or subsequent underage gathering or unruly
gathering. Only those who were responsible person(s) at both the first and
subsequent underage gathering or unruly gathering shall be subject to response
costs. In the event the responsible person is a tenant, the property owner
shall not be responsible for response costs until after the property owner or
landlord has received three written notifications that the tenant at issue has
been cited in accordance with this subchapter. Response costs shall be included
with the fine set forth in §
130.99(C).
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)
§ 130.28 APPEALS AND HEARINGS.
   (A)   Any person upon whom a fine is imposed pursuant to §
130.99(C) or recovery cost pursuant to §
130.27 shall have the right to appeal the imposition of such fine or response
cost pursuant to the procedures established by this code for appealing.
   (B)   Upon receipt of a notice of a fine or recovery cost, the person may
request a hearing before the hearing officer to show cause as to why the person
should not be liable for the violation of this subchapter. Such requests must
be filed in writing with the County Manager within ten calendar days of the
date of written notice of the fine or response cost. The person shall be given
written notice by personal delivery or certified or registered mail of the
hearing at least ten calendar days before the hearing.
   (C)   All hearings shall be open to the public and shall be held only after
notice is given to the person appealing the fine.
   (D)   (1)   The hearing shall be conducted by the hearing officer.
      (2)   The hearing officer shall be appointed by the County Manager.
      (3)   Formal rules of evidence shall not apply to the conduct of the
hearing.
      (4)   Cross-questioning is neither prohibited nor encouraged. The hearing
officer has full discretion whether to allow it.
      (5)   The hearing officer may hear testimony from any witness.
      (6)   After calling the meeting to order, the hearing officer shall
outline the procedure to be followed in the conduct of the hearing.
      (7)   The hearing may be recessed or adjourned to another time and/or
place upon the discretion of the hearing officer.
   (E)   The decision of the hearing officer may be appealed to the District
Court.
(Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)
§ 130.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   The first violation of §§
130.01 through
130.05 shall result in a written warning being issued to the parent or legal
guardian of the person in violation. The Board of County Commissioners strongly
recommends that five hours of community service be included for the first
violation.
      (2)   The second violation of §§
130.01 through
130.05 by the same person within 12 months of the first violation shall result
in a fine of $50. The Board of County Commissioners strongly recommends that
ten hours of community service be included for the second violation.
      (3)   The third violation of §§
130.01 through
130.05 by the same person within 12 months of the first violation shall result
in a fine of $100. Each subsequent violation of §§
130.01 through
130.05 by the same person within 12 months of the third violation shall result
in a fine of $150.
   (C)   (1)   Responsible persons violating §§
130.20 through
130.28 shall be fined as follows:
         (a)   First violation: Citation with an administrative penalty of $250
fine;
         (b)   A second violation within a 12-month period: Citation with an
administrative penalty of $500 fine;
         (c)   A third or subsequent violation within a 12-month period:
Citation with an administrative penalty of $1,000 fine; and
         (d)   If the person responsible for the event is underage, the parents
or legal guardians of the person may be jointly and severally liable for the
civil penalties pursuant to §§
130.20 through
130.28. A parent or legal guardian shall not be liable for the fine amount for
a first violation if the parent can demonstrate he or she did not have prior
knowledge of the underage gathering or unruly gathering. In the event the
parent or legal guardian learns of the underage or unruly gathering while such
gathering is occurring, the parent or legal guardian must additionally
demonstrate that he or she contacted law enforcement immediately upon learning
of the underage or unruly gathering, and took steps to stop the underage
gathering or unruly gathering. All other responsible persons shall remain
liable for this fine.
      (2)   In the event a tenant is the responsible person, upon the third
notification to the property owner of underage and/or unruly gatherings on the
property within a 12-month period, the property owner shall be fined as set
forth in divisions (C)(1)(a), (C)(1)(b), and (C)(1)(c) above. Notwithstanding
the foregoing, an owner shall not be fined if he or she can demonstrate that he
or she has taken or is in the process of taking all action legally required to
remove the tenant from the property.
      (3)   The fines set forth in divisions (C)(1)(a), (C)(1)(b), and (C)(1)
(c) above may be appealed pursuant to §
130.28. The payment of any such fines shall be stayed upon any timely appeal.
(Ord. 31, passed 8-14-1997; Ord. 95, passed 12-10-2015)

USE, POSSESSION, SALE OF SYNTHETIC CANNABINOIDS
§ 131.01 SHORT TITLE.
   This subchapter shall be known as the “Synthetic Cannabinoid Ordinance,” and
shall be referred to herein as “this subchapter.”
(Ord. 80, passed 1-13-2011)
§ 131.02 JURISDICTION.
   This subchapter shall provide for the regulation of the possession, use, and
sale of synthetic cannabinoids, by whatever slang term such products are known,
and salvia divinorum within the county but not within the boundaries of
municipalities.
(Ord. 80, passed 1-13-2011)
§ 131.03 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of this subchapter is to promote the general health and welfare
of the people of the county through the regulation of the possession, use, and
sale of synthetic cannabinoids and salvia divinorum to protect the essential
conditions of health and safety in the county.
(Ord. 80, passed 1-13-2011)
§ 131.04 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   K-2 or SPICE, GENIE, OASCENTS, ZOHAI, SAGE. Is defined as slang terms that
refer to any substance, whether described as tobacco, herbs, incense, spice, or
any blend thereof, regardless of whether the substance is marketed for the
purpose of being smoked, which includes any one or more of the following
chemicals:
      (1)   Salvia divinorum or salvinorin A. All parts of the plant presently
classified botanically as salvla divinorum, whether growing or not, the seeds
thereof, any extract from any part of such plant, and every compound,
manufacture, salts, derivative, mixture, or preparation of such plant, its
seeds, or extracts;
      (2)   2-[(1R, 3S)-hydroxycyclohexyl]-5-(2-methylocatan-2-yl) phenol (also
known as CP47, 497) and homologues;
      (3)   (6aS, 10aS)-9-(hydroxmethyl)-6, 6-dimethyl-3-(2-methyloctan-2-yl)-
6a, 7, 10, 10a- tetrahydrobenzo [c] chormen-1-ol) (also known as HU-211 or
dexanabinol);
      (4)   1-pentyl-3-(1-naphthoyl) indole (also known as JWH-018); or
      (5)   Butyl-3-(1-naphthoyl) indole (also known as JWH-073).
   SYNTHETIC CANNABINOID. Manufactured chemical compounds identified in the
definition for K-2 above, which mimic the effects of THC, the active principle
in cannabis, and are found in “herbal” smoking mixtures commonly sold as
“spice” or any of the other slang terms for these products. SYNTHETIC
CANNABINOID compounds are sprayed onto a mix of inert plant ingredients,
usually free of tobacco or cannabis, to produce these smoking mixtures.
(Ord. 80, passed 1-13-2011)
§ 131.05 POSSESSION, USE, SALE.
   The possession, sale, and use of K-2, spice, genie, dascents, zohai, sage,
or salvia oivinorum, or any other synthetic cannabinoid with any of the
chemicals identified in §
131.04 as a compound, is prohibited.
(Ord. 80, passed 1-13-2011) Penalty, see §
131.99
§ 131.06 DRUG PARAPHERNALIA PROHIBITED.
   It shalt be unlawful for any person to use or possess with intent to use an
ingestion device to inject, ingest, inhale, or otherwise introduce a synthetic
cannabinoid into a person’s system. An ingestive device shall be considered
drug paraphernalia according to the definition section found in NMSA § 30-31-2.
(Ord. 80, passed 1-13-2011) Penalty, see §
131.99
§ 131.07 ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT.
   The County Sheriff, and any other official designated by the Board of County
Commissioners, shall be responsible for the administration and enforcement of
this subchapter.
(Ord. 80, passed 1-13-2011)
§ 131.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Any person violating or failing, or refusing to comply with, the
provisions of §§
131.01 through
131.07 and the codes adopted shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and may be
prosecuted in any court of competent jurisdiction within the county, and shall
be punished by a fine of not more than $300, or imprisonment for not more than
90 days, or both,
(Ord. 80, passed 1-13-2011)
