GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 150.01 SHORT TITLE.
   This chapter shall be known as the “Building Code Ordinance,” and shall be
referred to herein as “this ordinance” or “this chapter.”
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.02 PURPOSE.
   This chapter shall provide for the regulation of all construction, whether
residential or commercial, or other use, including any additions, expansions,
repairs, remodel, or renovation to any building or structures in the county;
provide for the issuance of permits for such work; establish minimum standards
of workmanship and materials to be used in such work; and provide for the
inspection, administration, penalties, and enforcement of the regulation.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.03 JURISDICTION.
   This chapter shall provide for the regulation of construction activities
within the county, but not within the boundaries of municipalities.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.04 DEFINITIONS; MEANING OF TERMS.
   (A)   Meaning of terms. Whenever the terms COUNTY PLANNING DIRECTOR or
COUNTY PLANNER appear in this chapter, they shall be read and understood as
including any other person or position authorized by the County Manager or the
Board of County Commissioners to administer or otherwise carry out the
requirements of this chapter.
   (B)   Words not defined. Any word or term not defined in this chapter shall
have the meaning ascribed to it in the county subdivision ordinance, or they
shall have their ordinary accepted meaning within the context with which they
are used.
   (C)   Definitions. For the purpose of this chapter, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      AGRICULTURE. An agricultural use or activity requires a tract containing
five or more contiguous acres in active, current use for the production of farm
crops for sale and profit, including vegetables, fruit, cotton, grain, and
other crops, and the processing of crops to the generally recognizable minimum
level of marketability and storage thereof on the premises; the open range
grazing of livestock or irrigated pasture for grazing livestock; animal and
poultry husbandry, dairy operations, floriculture, and horticulture; and
accessory uses customarily incidental to agricultural activities. Provided
further, that AGRICULTURE does not include commercial slaughter houses, meat
packing plants, fertilizer yards, or other similar animal related uses.
      BUILDING. Any structure used or intended for supporting or sheltering any
use or occupancy.
      BUILDING OFFICIAL. The officer or official, or inspector or other
designated authority, charged with the administration and enforcement of any
code, or the BUILDING OFFICIAL’S duly authorized representative.
      CERTIFICATE OF COMPLIANCE. A certificate issued to the property owner by
the County Code Compliance Officer, or other designated county official, or a
State Building Official evidencing the fact that the requirements of this
chapter, as set forth in this chapter, have been met.
      CID. The State Construction Industries Division.
      CODE. A standard that is an extensive compilation of provisions covering
broad subject matter, or that is suitable for adoption into law, any adopted
uniform code pertaining to construction activities.
      CODE COMPLIANCE OFFICER. The person designated by the county to enforce
various county codes or ordinances.
      COMMUNITY LIQUID WASTE SYSTEM. A liquid waste system or sewerage system,
publicly or privately owned and operated, including collection and treatment
facilities constructed to serve one or more lots.
      COMMUNITY WATER SYSTEM. A water system or utility, publicly or privately
owned, that relies on surface and/or groundwater diversions, other than wells
permitted by the State Engineer under NMSA § 72-12-1, and that consists of
common storage and/or distribution facilities operated for the delivery of
water to multiple service connections. A COMMUNITY WATER SUPPLY SYSTEM shall
have sufficient water rights to serve all lots within the community. A
COMMUNITY WATER SYSTEM shall include mutual domestic water associations
established in accordance with state law.
      CONTIGUOUS. Adjacent lots or parcels of land sharing a boundary line.
      COUNTY. Luna County, New Mexico.
      COUNTY BOARD. The Board of County Commissioners.
      DEVELOPMENT. The use of any land; the carrying out of any building
activity, including construction, reconstruction, conversion, or enlargement of
any building or structure; the making of any material change in the use, or
intensity of use, or appearance of any building, structure, or land; and the
establishment of a commercial parking lot or the dividing of land into lots,
blocks, or parcels, including the construction of roads, the installation of
water, sanitary sewer, and stormwater management facilities, or other
utilities.
      DWELLING. Any building or portion thereof, which is designed or used
exclusively for residential purposes.
      DWELLING UNIT, ACCESSORY.
         (a)   A self-contained living quarter attached to, or detached from,
or under the same roof as, the main or principal dwelling, located on the same
site as the main or principal dwelling created by:
            1.   The conversion of an existing single-family dwelling;
            2.   The construction of an addition to an existing single-family
dwelling; or
            3.   The construction of a detached structure which is subordinate
to the main of principal dwelling.
         (b)   The gross floor area of any such ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT shall
be no larger than 50% of the gross floor area of the original main or principal
dwelling.
      DWELLING, APARTMENT or DWELLING MULTIPLE. A building or portion thereof
that contains three or more dwelling units, and for purposes of this chapter,
includes residential condominiums.
      FAMILY. One or more persons occupying a dwelling unit and living as a
single housekeeping unit as distinguished from a group occupying a boarding
house, dormitory, lodging house, or hotel, as herein defined.
      FIRE MARSHAL. The County Fire Marshal, or a person discharging the duties
of FIRE MARSHAL.
      FPC. The Fire Prevention Code.
      FLOOD HAZARD BOUNDARY MAP. An official map issued by the Federal
Emergency Management Agency, where the areas within special flood hazards are
designated.
      FLOOD PRONE AREA. An area where a temporary condition of partial or
complete inundation of normally dry land results from the unusual and rapid
accumulation or runoff of surface waters.
      FOOTING. The portion of the foundation of a structure that spreads and
transmits loads directly to the soil or piles.
      GRADE LEVEL. The lowest point of elevation of the finished surface of the
ground, paving, or sidewalk within the area between the building and the
property line or, when the property line is more than five feet from the
building, between the building and a line five feet from the building.
      HABITABLE. As applied to any form of housing, such as manufactured homes,
site built homes, or mobile homes, means that there are no known defects,
damage, or deterioration to the home which creates a dangerous or unsafe
situation or condition. All plumbing, heating, and electrical systems are in
safe working order and must meet all applicable codes.
      IBC. The International Building Code.
      INSPECTOR. The County Building Inspector or the Code Compliance Officer,
or a person duly delegated by the County Building Inspector or the Code
Compliance Officer, or a person instructed or requested by the County Building
Inspector or the Code Compliance Officer, to provide a written report with
respect to any matter set out in this chapter.
      IRC. The International Residential Code.
      LCBO. The County Building Official; see also INSPECTOR and BUILDING
OFFICIAL.
      LOT. A parcel of land occupied or intended for occupancy by one main
building, together with its accessory buildings and uses customarily incidental
to it.
      LOT OF RECORD. A lot which is part of a subdivision, the map or plat of
which has been recorded in the office of the County Clerk, or a lot described
by metes and bounds or by survey plat prepared by a land surveyor licensed in
the state, which bas been recorded in the office of the County Clerk.
      MODULAR HOME. A standardized factory fabricated transportable building
module not having a chassis or wheels of its own, designed and constructed in
accordance with the International Building Code and intended to be placed on a
permanent foundation, and requires a building permit for installation.
      NFPA. The National Fire Protection Association.
      NMBC. The New Mexico Building Code.
      NON-RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY. A building or structure, or parts thereof, not
occupied in whole or in part for the purposes of human habitation, including
the land and premises appurtenant thereto.
      OCCUPANCY. The purpose that a building, or part thereof, is used or
intended to be used.
      OFFICER. The Code Compliance Officer of the county; the person designated
by the county to administer and enforce various codes and ordinances.
      OWNER. Any person, agent, firm, or corporation having a legal or
equitable interest in the property.
      PARCEL. A unit of land capable of being described by location and
boundaries, and not dedicated for public or common use.
      PERMIT. An official document or certificate issued by the Building
Official, the County Planner, or other authorized authority, as appropriate,
authorizing performance of a specified activity.
      PERSON. A natural person including any individual, partnership, company,
corporation, firm, association, trust, estate, foundation, state and federal
agency, institution, county, city, town, village, or municipality or other
legal entity, however organized.
      PROPERTY. Any area, plot, or parcel of land in the county, which is under
a common ownership or is separately identified for assessment by the County
Assessor’s office. PROPERTY shall include land under the ownership of the
United States, the state, or any local government or school district entity.
This definition is intended to be inclusive and not limiting, and shall
therefore include all land within the boundaries of the county, except that the
definition of property, and therefore this chapter, shall exclude property
within the boundaries of the City of Deming and the Village of Columbus, and
any hereafter incorporated municipality.
      PROPERTY OCCUPANT. Any person who is occupying any property, whether by
legal right or without legal right.
      PROPERTY OWNER. The person who is the recorded owner of any property
according to the records contained in the County Clerk’s office.
      REPAIR. The reconstruction, renewal, refinishing, or refurbishing of all
or any part of an existing building or structure, or property for the purpose
of its maintenance.
      RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY. Any property or building that is used, designed, or
intended for use as a dwelling unit, dwelling, or apartment dwelling, and
includes the yards, accessory buildings, and vacant property belonging to such
property.
      SEWAGE. Residential liquid wastes, commercial liquid wastes, industrial
liquid wastes, and any drainage, but does not include stormwater.
      SEWERAGE SYSTEM. A system for transporting sewage owned and operated by
the county, a municipality, or a private disposal system approved by the State
Environmental Department.
      SHALL. Shall be construed as mandatory.
      SITE BUILT RESIDENCES. Residences constructed at the permanent building
site, but which may incorporate the use of some prefabricated building
components.
      SMOKE DETECTOR. An approved device that senses visible or invisible
particles of combustion.
      SPECIAL FLOOD HAZARD AREA. Land in the floodplain subject to a 1% or
greater chance of flooding in any given year.
      STANDARDS. The provisions and measures of physical conditions and
occupancy set out in this chapter.
      STREET or ROAD. All property dedicated or intended for public or private
access to property, or subject to public easements therefor.
      STRUCTURE. That which is built or constructed, an edifice or building of
any kind, or any piece of work artificially built up or composed of parts
joined together in some definite manner. Without limiting the generality of the
foregoing, STRUCTURE shall include a wall, fence, sign, or billboard.
      TEMPORARY. Applies to facilities or structures that are not of permanent
construction, and are not intended to be permanent erected and maintained on a
site. Tents and air supported structures are considered TEMPORARY for purposes
of this chapter.
      TERRAIN MANAGEMENT. The control of floods, drainage, and erosion, and
measures required for adapting proposed development to existing soil
characteristics and topography.
      UMC. The Uniform Mechanical Code.
      UPC. The Uniform Plumbing Code.
      UTILITY SERVICE. Connection to an electrical service pole or other
approved receptacle, or gas and water meter installation, but does not include
electrical mainline extension or gas and water mainline extension, or water
main tap or meter box and setter installation.
      USE. The use for which land or buildings are occupied or maintained,
arranged, designed, or intended.
      VARIANCE. Any deviation from the regulations of this chapter, as approved
by the Board of County Commissioners, where such variance will not be contrary
to the public interest; however, the allowable use of the premises is not
subject to change by VARIANCE.
      WASTEWATER. The liquid- or water-carried wastes removed from residential
properties, businesses, institutions, and other uses, including bath and toilet
wastes, laundry waste, and kitchen waste, but not including toxic, hazardous,
or industrial waste.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
BUILDING STANDARDS
§ 150.15 ADOPTION OF BUILDING CODE; OTHER CODES.
   Each and all of the regulations, provisions, penalties, conditions, terms,
and all appendices of the latest editions of the following are hereby referred
to, adopted, and incorporated as fully as if set out verbatim herein and any
amendments thereto, including the most recent additions, updates, revisions, or
editions thereof:
   (A)   International Building Code;
   (B)   International Residential Code;
   (C)   State Commercial Building Code;
   (D)   State Residential Code;
   (E)   National Electric Code;
   (F)   State Non-Load Bearing Straw Construction Building Code (Phase III);
   (G)   State Plumbing Code;
   (H)   Uniform Plumbing and Mechanical Code;
   (I)   State Mechanical Code;
   (J)   State Electrical Code;
   (K)   State Electrical Safety Code (Phase III);
   (L)   National Fire Protection Association, Fire Prevention Code; and
   (M)   NFIP Regulations, 44 C.F.R. § 60.3, flood insurance study, and flood
insurance rate map, effective October 19, 2010.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.16 COPIES OF CODES AVAILABLE FOR INSPECTION.
   One or more copies of applicable codes adopted in §
150.15 shall be available for review and inspection during regular business
hours in the office of designated official.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.17 FEE SCHEDULE.
   The fee schedule for building permits shall be established. No permit shall
be issued nor shall an application be considered complete prior to the receipt
of said fee.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.18 BUILDING PERMITS REQUIRED.
   Any construction, residential, or commercial or other use, any additions,
expansions, repairs, remodel, or renovation to any building or structure, to
include site built and modular buildings or structures, shall have a building
permit issued by the LCBO or a State Building Official, and follow procedures
required by the codes adopted in this chapter. The building permit must be
displayed in a conspicuous place at the building site. If the LCBO, or State
Building Official or the County Code Compliance Officer, determines that the
property for which a permit has been requested is in violation, has outstanding
violations, or may be in non-compliance with any part of this chapter, or the
county subdivision ordinance, or any other applicable county, state, or federal
regulation, the LCBO, State Building Official, or the County Code Compliance
Officer may deny issuance of the permit until such time as the property has
been deemed compliant.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.19 EXCEPTIONS.
   (A)   One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage
sheds, playhouses, and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed
120 square feet (11.15 m2).
   (B)   Fences not over six feet high.
   (C)   Retaining walls that are not laterally supported at the top and that
retain in excess of 36 inches (915 mm) of unbalanced fill, unless supporting a
surcharge or impounding Class I, II, or III-A liquids.
   (D)   Water tanks supported directly upon grade if the capacity does not
exceed 5,000 gallons (18,927 L) and the ratio of height to diameter or width
does not exceed two to one.
   (E)   Sidewalks and driveways not more than 30 inches (762 mm) above grade
and not over any basement or story below, and which are not part of an
accessible route.
   (F)   Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops, and
similar finish work.
   (G)   Temporary motion picture, television, and theater stage sets and
scenery.
   (H)   Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a group R-3 occupancy, as
applicable in the NMRBC, which are less than 24 inches (610 mm) deep, do not
exceed 5,000 gallons (19,000 L), and are installed entirely aboveground.
   (I)   Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural
purposes, and not including services systems.
   (J)   Swings and other playground equipment accessory to one- and two-family
dwellings.
   (K)   Window awnings supported by an exterior wall of group R-3, as
applicable in the NMRBC, and group U occupancies.
   (L)   Movable cases, counters, and partitions not over five feet, nine
inches (1,753 mm) in height.
   (M)   Any work not otherwise regulated by the state construction codes and
the CID rules.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.20 ALTERNATE MATERIALS, DESIGN, METHODS OF CONSTRUCTION.
   (A)   Pursuant to the International Building Code and the International
Residential Code, as amended from time to time, where materials, design, and
construction methods are specified in any of the codes or rules and regulations
adopted in §§
150.15 through
150.28, alternate materials, design, and methods of construction may be
allowed, provided any alternate has been approved and is authorized by the
County Building Official (LCBO), or other authorized official.
   (B)   The LCBO, or other authorized official, may approve any such
alternate, provided the LCBO, or other authorized official, is satisfied the
proposed design is satisfactory and complies with the provisions of those codes
and rules and regulations set out in §§
150.15 through
150.28, and that the material and method of work proposed is at least the
equivalent of that prescribed in any of the codes and rules and regulations set
out in §§
150.15 through
150.28.
   (C)   (1)   The LCBO, or other authorized official, shall require that
sufficient evidence or proof to substantiate any claims made about alternate
material, design, or methods of construction.
      (2)   Without limiting the generality of the foregoing sentence, the LCBO
may require a study and/or certificate of code compliance from a qualified
engineer or architect as evidence or proof of claims made about alternate
material, design, or methods of construction.
   (D)   Whenever there is insufficient evidence of compliance with any of the
provisions of this code or evidence that any material or construction does not
conform to the requirements of this code, the LCBO, or other authorized
official, may require tests by an approved agency as proof of compliance to be
made at no expense to the county.
   (E)   The details of any action by the LCBO, or other authorized official,
granting approval of an alternate shall be recorded and retained in the files
of the County Building Official’s office or the County Planner’s office.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.21 USE OF WASTE TIRES FOR CONSTRUCTION.
   (A)   No use of waste or scrap tires, baled or non-baled, or processed
tires, or used tires, for the construction of any building or structure is
permitted on any site or lot in the county unless all of the following
conditions are met to the satisfaction of the county:
      (1)   (a)   Such proposed use constitutes no environmental hazard and
that it will not endanger the health or safety of the residents of the county;
and
         (b)   To this end, the county may require the owner, or his or her
authorized agent, to produce and submit to the county an environmental impact
assessment prepared by a qualified environmental consultant showing no adverse
environmental impact. Prior to taking any decision, the county may consult with
any state agency or it may engage its own consultant to wider take an oversight
review of the environmental impact assessment prepared by the owner’s, or his
or her authorized agent’s, consultant.
      (2)   A building permit is obtained from the Construction Industries
Division of the state;
      (3)   Written approval is obtained from the Fire Marshal, or other
authorized official, which written approval shall state clearly that there is
sufficient fire suppression measures in place on the lot or site; and that, in
his or her opinion, the county has the capability to effectively deal with any
building or structure fire that may occur. The Fire Marshal may also prescribe
specific fire prevention measures that shall be taken by the owner, or his or
her authorized agent;
      (4)   The owner, or his or her authorized agent, shall submit design and
construction plans to the County Planner and to the Construction Industries
Division showing clearly the use of waste or scrap tires, or processed tires,
and that such design complies with all requirements of the International
Building Code. These drawings shall be stamped and signed by a professional
engineer licensed in the state, or by an architect licensed in the state;
      (5)   A financial guarantee in favor of the county, in the form of a
bond, cashier’s check, or other form satisfactory to the County Attorney, and
in an amount satisfactory to the county shall be posted with the County Clerk.
The amount of the financial guarantee shall be sufficient to cover the full
cost of any clean-up, disposal of materials, and the removal of all buildings
and structures on the site or lot. The amount of the financial guarantee shall
be in the sole discretion of the county. The owner, or his or her authorized
agent, shall keep the financial guarantee current. The county shall retain the
right to request an increase in the financial guarantee as circumstances
warrant. The financial guarantee shall be released at the time the project is
completed to the satisfaction of the Building Official; and
      (6)   A permit for the proposed use is obtained from the County Planning
Department. The county shall not issue any permit unless and until it is fully
satisfied that conditions set out in divisions (A)(1) through (A)(5) above have
been fulfilled.
   (B)   If the owner, or his or her authorized agent, or any successor, fails
to maintain full compliance with the condition upon which approval of a
proposed use is given, the county, after giving notice to comply, may revoke
the permit. Upon revocation, all operations shall cease and site clean-up shall
commence immediately.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.22 ON-SITE UTILITY, DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS.
   Approved on-site utilities, to include water, sewer, and electricity, are
prerequisite to the issuance of a building permit. All housing units shall be
connected to a waste disposal system permitted and approved by the State
Environment Department, a domestic water well permitted by the State Engineer,
or be connected to an approved potable water utility, whether private or
municipal. For purposes of this section:
   (A)   There shall be no multiple users connected to a domestic water well
nor to any on-site liquid waste disposal system, except for properly permitted
community water systems and properly permitted cluster wastewater systems, or
as otherwise provided herein;
   (B)   All electrical, plumbing, and gas hookups shall be inspected and
approved by an inspector of CID, as the case may be, prior to occupancy and
before a certificate of occupancy will be issued by the LCBO, or other
authorized official;
   (C)   Any water/well, sewer/septic, electric, or natural gas/LP utility
provider that connects service to individual parcels before the land owner
holds a valid building permit is in violation of this chapter, and the service
shall be disconnected;
   (D)   Any waste disposal system must be approved by the State Environment
Department; and
   (E)   No building permit or other permit shall be issued until and unless
the applicant for such permit can show, to the satisfaction of the County
Planner, that the applicant has legal access to a lot or parcel of land, either
by means of a public road or by means of a properly recorded easement, and such
access shall provide reasonable physical ingress and egress to and from the
parcel of land.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.23 SMOKE DETECTORS.
   Smoke detectors shall be required in all dwelling units to include site
built and modular, occupied or installed after the effective date of this
chapter.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.24 FLOOD HAZARD REGULATIONS.
   (A)   The County Floodplain Manager is hereby appointed the Floodplain
Administrator to administer and implement the flood hazard installation
provisions of this section and other appropriate sections of 44 C.F.R.
pertaining to floodplain management. No residential, commercial, or other use
or development shall be located or installed in a flood-prone area, such as a
flood hazard area as designated by the National Flood Insurance Rate Map for
the county, or in, on, or over the path of an arroyo, or floodway without the
prior approval of the County Floodplain Manager and the issuance of a
floodplain development permit. All development and all construction related to
such development shall comply with the minimum standards as adopted by, or may
be amended by, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). A new or
replacement water supply system or sanitary sewage system may be required
within a designated flood hazard area, which shall be designed to minimize or
eliminate infiltration of floodwaters into the system as well as discharges
from the system into floodwaters, and the on-site waste disposal system must be
located so as to avoid impairment of them or contamination from them during
flooding.
   (B)   All new construction and substantial improvements of structures
designed for human occupancy being built in a special flood hazard area shall
be constructed such that all electrical, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and
other service facilities are located so as to prevent water from entering or
accumulating within the components during conditions of flooding and must meet
one of the following conditions:
      (1)   The lowest floor level elevated at least one foot above the base
flood elevation where base flood elevations are determined; and/or
      (2)   The lowest floor level, with respect to site built structures,
elevated two feet above the highest adjacent grade in areas where no base flood
elevations are determined.
   (C)   Any building or structure to be constructed in “A” Zones, as
designated by the National Flood Insurance Rate Map for the county, where no
base flood elevations are determined, must have its lowest floor level
constructed a minimum of two feet above the highest adjacent grade. The
material used to raise the lowest floor above the highest adjacent grade must
be compacted to the satisfaction of the LCBO, the County Planner, or other
authorized official, who may require that the landowner provide a report from a
qualified geo-technical consultant that the soil is sufficiently compacted to
accommodate the intended development. This section shall apply only to
dwellings or structures erected or installed after the date of this chapter, as
amended.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010) Penalty, see §
150.99
Cross-reference:
   Flood damage prevention, see
Chapter 153
§ 150.25 STORMWATER, GRADING, DRAINAGE, DUST CONTROL.
   (A)   No property owner shall alter the natural flow of stormwater across
his, her, or their property in such a manner as to increase the flood hazard on
other properties.
   (B)   Except for agricultural operations, no person shall clear any land of
its natural vegetation without having in place and implementing a plan,
approved by the Code Compliance Officer, to prevent soil, sand, dust, and
building materials, construction waste, or other materials from being blown by
the wind from the said land. In the event the owner, lessee, occupant, or any
agent or representative thereof having charge or control of such land fails or
refuses to prevent such materials from being blown from the land by the wind,
the county may take such corrective action as it deems advisable, and the cost
of doing so shall constitute a lien on the subject land.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010) Penalty, see §
150.99
§ 150.26 LIGHTING.
   (A)   Lighting fixtures, lamps, and their supports and connections shall be
maintained in a safe and complete condition, without visible deterioration.
   (B)   All properties that are being developed, remodeled, refurbished, or
rehabilitated shall comply with the Night Sky Protection Act, NMSA §§ 74-12-
1 through 74-12-11.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.27 ROOFS.
   All roofs shall be kept clear of debris such as tires, concrete blocks,
rocks, and other objects, materials, and structures not approved by the
builder, manufacturer, or installer, or for which a permit has not been issued.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.28 SETBACK.
   All permitted structures shall have a 25-foot setback from the front
property line, a five-foot setback from the side property line, and a five-foot
setback from the rear property line.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.29 CONFORMANCE MANDATORY; ONE MAIN DWELLING PER LOT.
   (A)   Conformance mandatory. Except as otherwise provided by this chapter,
no building shall hereafter be used, erected, constructed, reconstructed,
moved, or altered, nor shall any land be used or developed, except in
conformity with the regulations, herein set out in applicable parts of this
chapter.
   (B)   One main dwelling unit per lot.
      (1)   Every dwelling unit hereafter erected, enlarged, or structurally
altered shall be located on a lot as defined in §
150.04, and in no case shall there be more than one main dwelling unit on one
lot.
      (2)   Land that is part of one lot and that is not in excess of the area
requirements for that lot shall not be used to satisfy the area requirements of
any other lot.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010) Penalty, see §
150.99
ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT
§ 150.40 ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   This chapter and all codes, rules, regulations, and other provisions
set out in said chapter shall be enforced by the County Building Official
(LCBO), who is certified by the State Construction Industries Division, and has
such powers and duties as are enumerated in, and set forth in, the current
provisions of the codes adopted in §
150.15, or by a County Code Compliance Officer. Sections
150.15 through
150.28 may be enforced by an inspector employed by the State Construction
Industries Division. The LCBO shall not enforce any code provisions pertaining
to gas service installations or related matters.
   (B)   Any Building Inspector of the County Planning Office, and the County
Fire Marshal, and any electrical inspector of the state, and any plumbing
inspector of the state, and any environmentalist of the State Environment
Department, and any engineer, or technician or technologist, or water resource
specialist, of the State Engineer’s office of the state, and any other
qualified person, may be authorized by the Code Compliance Officer to help
enforce the standards set out in this chapter, or may be requested by the Code
Compliance Officer to give a written report, or other advice to aid in the
administration and enforcement of this chapter.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.41 NOTICE OF VIOLATION.
   In addition to the criminal penalties provided for in this chapter, any such
violation, after reasonable efforts to secure voluntary compliance with this
chapter, have failed, shall be subject to abatement as follows.
   (A)   Notice of violation.
      (1)   If, after inspection, or the observation of any county or state
employee, the Officer is satisfied that a violation does exist, the Officer
shall serve, or cause to be served by personal service, or send by prepaid
registered mail to the owner of record of the property, or to the occupant or
tenant of the property, or both, and to all persons shown by the records to
have an interest in the property, a notice of violation setting out the
particulars of the violation(s). The notice shall establish that the abatement
of the violation(s) by the owner, or occupant or tenant, or both, shall begin
in not more than ten days and shall be completed in not more than 90 days after
service of the notice. The notice shall be served at the owner’s, or occupant’s
or tenant’s, last known address.
      (2)   In the event a violation of this chapter constitutes an immediate
danger to the public health and safety, the notice provisions of this division
(A) shall not apply, and the violation may be prosecuted and abated
immediately.
   (B)   Placard. If the Officer is unable to achieve service under division
(A) above, he or she may place a placard containing the terms of the notice in
a conspicuous place on the property or building, and the placing of the placard
shall be deemed to be sufficient service of the notice on the owner or other
persons.
   (C)   Extension of timeframe for abatement. Where the Officer is satisfied
that there is good and sufficient reason to extend the timeframe for abatement
of the violation(s), he or she may extend the timeframe set out in division (A)
above for a period of time not to exceed 45 days beyond the time period set out
in the original notice.
   (D)   Failure to correct. In the event the owner, occupant, or tenant of the
property where the violation exists has failed to correct the violation(s)
within the prescribed period of time, then the Officer shall issue a citation
or file a complaint charging violation of this chapter with the Magistrate
Court, or other appropriate court of jurisdiction, demanding that the owner of
the property or the occupant, or both, be held to answer to the court for the
violation.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.42 CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY.
   (A)   All buildings or structures, to include site built and modular,
whether titled or untitled, are subject to this chapter and shall, prior to
use, be inspected by the LCBO, or other authorized official.
   (B)   Following the final inspection of a building or structure, the Officer
will issue a certificate of occupancy/compliance when the building or structure
is in compliance with the standards of this chapter.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.43 PROHIBITION.
   The Code Compliance Officer may issue a notice prohibiting the occupancy of
any unsafe or uninhabitable building.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.44 CITATION; UNIFORM NON-TRAFFIC.
   The use of uniform non-traffic citation forms is authorized for use in
enforcement of this chapter, except as otherwise provided.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.45 VARIANCE.
   (A)   It is the intention of the Board of County Commissioners that all
variances be temporary in duration. The Board of County Commissioners may grant
a variance to the regulations set out in §
150.29 for the sole purpose of permitting one accessory dwelling unit on any
property in the county on the following grounds only to provide living
accommodation to an immediate member of the family of the owner-occupant of the
principal dwelling unit which family member requires immediate and urgent care
because he or she is disabled, physically or mentally infirm, has a disease
which is or will become debilitating, or is incapable of being gainfully
employed because of his, her, or their condition. A certificate or letter
signed by a physician licensed in the state attesting to the medical condition
and the need for care of the family member who will occupy the accessory
dwelling unit shall be required by the Board of County Commissioners as proof
of the medical condition.
   (B)   The Board of County Commissioners shall not grant any variance which
will cause the county to incur or absorb any costs. In granting any variance,
the Board of County Commissioners may impose such conditions as will:
      (1)   Substantially secure the objectives of the standards set out in
this chapter;
      (2)   Not adversely affect the health safety and general welfare of the
general public and the immediate property owners;
      (3)   Impose whatever time limits may be reasonable and appropriate in
the circumstances. Any variance granted shall be for a period of time not to
exceed three years from the date of granting such variance. If necessary, the
variance may be renewed prior to the expiration of the term of the variance
upon written application by the owner-occupant. Such renewal shall be for a
period of time not to exceed three years. All variances granted by the Board of
County Commissioners must be renewed prior to the expiration of either the
initial time limit imposed by the Board of County Commissioners or any renewal
period granted by the Board of County Commissioners. There shall be no limits
on the number of renewals, provided the reason for the initial variance remains
valid;
      (4)   Impose conditions on the type, quality, and design of any proposed
construction;
      (5)   Impose height limits;
      (6)   Require buffering in the form of fencing and/or vegetation to
protect and shield adjacent land uses;
      (7)   Ensure compatibility with other development in the adjacent area.
COMPATIBILITY, as used here, shall include, but is not limited to, the
following: land use, height, scale, density, water supply, and liquid waste
disposal facilities; and
      (8)   Accomplish any other purpose and effect deemed advisable and
appropriate by the Board of County Commissioners.
   (C)   The following procedure shall apply to all requests for a variance.
      (1)   All requests for a variance shall be in writing and submitted to
the County Planner. The written request shall set out the following
information:
         (a)   A description of the specific variance requested;
         (b)   The reasons for the request;
         (c)   The supporting information, such as medical certificates, for
such request;
         (d)   The period of time for which the variance is necessary (initial
variance may be for a maximum three-year period, subject to renewal); and
         (e)   A description of the action the owner-occupant will take to
discontinue the use of, and remove, the additional accessory dwelling when the
reason for the variance no longer exists.
      (2)   The County Planner shall review the written request for variance
for completeness and shall, within ten days of receipt of the request, inform
the applicant either that the request is complete or the nature of any
additional information that is required. Until the request is complete, no
further action shall be taken by the County Planner or the Board of County
Commissioners.
      (3)   The County Planner shall confer with, and seek the advice of, the
Code Compliance Officer and the County Attorney, as appropriate, with respect
to the request for variance.
      (4)   The County Planner shall notify all property owners within 500 feet
of the subject property by first class regular mail at least ten days prior to
the Board of County Commissioners meeting at which the variance application
will be heard. Such notice shall briefly describe the nature of the variance
and the date, time, and location of the hearing.
      (5)   The County Planner shall submit a written report, together with his
or her recommendation to the Board of County Commissioners, five days prior to
the hearing date.
      (6)   The Board of County Commissioners shall hold a public hearing on
all requests for a variance, or a renewal of a variance, under this section.
The public hearing shall be held at a regularly scheduled County Commissioners’
meeting. The public hearing shall be considered a quasi-judicial proceeding to
be conducted in accordance with quasi-judicial procedures adopted by the Board
of County Commissioners. The Board of County Commissioners will then decide the
matter during its regular business meeting.
      (7)   The written decision and order of the Board of County
Commissioners, together with any conditions, shall be prepared, signed, and
filed with the County Clerk within ten working days after the date the Board of
County Commissioners made its decision. The County Planner shall keep a written
record of the variance granted and shall show the location and nature of the
variance on a county map specifically designated for that purpose.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
§ 150.99 PENALTY.
   Any person violating or failing, or refusing, to comply with the provisions
of this chapter and the codes adopted may be prosecuted in any court of
competent jurisdiction within the county, and shall be punished by a fine of
not more than $300. The Board of County Commissioners may apply to the District
Court for appropriate injunctive relief to compel compliance by any person
whose conduct violates any provision of this chapter. The county shall be
entitled to recover a reasonable attorney’s fee if required to enforce this
chapter through the issuance of a demand letter, or in enforcing any portion of
this chapter in any court of competent jurisdiction. After the effective date
of this chapter, all violations are subject to issuance of a citation.
(Ord. 75, passed 8-12-2010)
