   RESUBDIVISION. Any change to a lot line, right-of-way line, or utility
easement, of previously approved subdivisions unless the change is the result
of a vacation of plats or a variance granted by action of the Board of County
Commissioners.
   RIGHT-OF-WAY, DEDICATED. Land deeded, reserved by plat, or otherwise
acquired by the county, which is dedicated for use as a road or drainage
channel or other public use.
   RIGHT-OF-WAY, PRIVATE. Land dedicated and intended to be used for private
access to private property, or for utilities.
   ROADWAY. The portion of the street right-of-way available for vehicular
traffic.
   SELL. To sell or offer to sell land.
   SEPTIC TANK SYSTEM. A tank and attached absorption field that is designated
and constructed to separate solids from liquids in the effluents from a lot or
lots, and which is designed to digest organic matter through anaerobic
processes and disperse the liquid excess into the soil.
   SETBACK. The shortest allowable distance between a property line and the
foundation, wall, eave, or main frame of a building or structure.
   SHALL. The word SHALL is mandatory, and not permissive.
   SKETCH PLAN. A map showing lots, road layout, drainage structures, arroyos,
and land proposed for public use, with estimated dimensions. A SKETCH PLAN
shall include a general vicinity map showing the location of the proposed
subdivision with reference to existing roadways, easements, municipalities,
significant landforms, and other landmarks.
   SOLID WASTE. Any garbage, rubbish, or other discarded material that results
from residential, commercial, institutional, industrial, or recreational
activities.
   SUBDIVIDE. To divide a surface area of land into a subdivision.
   SUBDIVIDER. Any person or agent who creates or who has created a
subdivision, individually or as part of a common promotional plan, or any
person engaged in the sale, lease, or other conveyance of subdivided land;
however, SUBDIVIDER does not include any duly licensed real estate broker or
salesperson acting on another’s account.
   SUBDIVISION. Division of a surface area of land, including land within a
previously approved subdivision, into two or more parcels for the purpose of
sale, lease, or other conveyance; or for building development, whether
immediate or future; and dormant subdivisions or portions of dormant
subdivisions, all of which are subject to these regulations. However,
SUBDIVISION does not include:
      (1)   Sale, lease, or other conveyance of any parcel that is 35 acres or
larger in size within any 12-month period, provided that the land has been used
primarily and continuously for agricultural purposed, in accordance with NMSA §
7-36-20, for the preceding three years;
      (2)   Sale or lease of apartments, offices, stores, or similar space
within a building;
      (3)   Division of land within the boundaries of a municipality;
      (4)   Division of land in which only gas, oil, mineral, or water rights
are severed from the surface ownership of the land;
      (5)   Division of land created by court order where the order creates no
more than one parcel per party;
      (6)   Division of land for grazing or farming activities, provided the
land continues to be used for grazing or farming activities;
      (7)   Division of land resulting only in the alteration of parcel
boundaries where parcels are altered for the purpose of increasing or reducing
the size of contiguous parcels, and where the number of parcels is not
increased;
      (8)   Division of land to create burial plots in a cemetery;
      (9)   Division of land to create a parcel that is sold or donated as a
gift to an immediate family member; this exception shall be limited to allow
the seller or donor to sell or give no more than one parcel per tract of land
per immediate family member;
      (10)   Division of land created to provide security for mortgages, liens,
or deeds of trust, provided that the division of land is not the result of a
seller-financed transaction;
      (11)   Sale, lease, or other conveyance of land that creates no parcel
smaller than 140 acres;
      (12)   Division of land to create a parcel that is donated to any trust
or non-profit corporation granted an exemption from federal income tax, as
described in I.R.C. § 501(c)(3), being 26 U.S.C. § 501(c)(3), as amended;
school, college, or other institution with a defined curriculum and a student
body and faculty which conducts classes on a regular basis; or to any church
group organized for the purposed of divine worship, religious teaching, or
other specifically religious activity; or
      (13)   (a)   Sale, lease, or other conveyance of a single parcel from a
tract of land, except from a tract within a previously approved subdivision,
within any five-year period, provided that a second or subsequent sale, lease,
or other conveyance from the same tract of land within five years of the first
sale, lease, or other conveyance shall be subject to the provisions of the
State Subdivision Act, being NMSA §§ 47-6-1 et seq.
         (b)   Provided further, that a survey shall be filed with the County
Clerk indicating the five-year holding period for both the original tract and
the newly created tract.
   SUBDIVISION MASTER PLAN.
      (1)   The portion of a preliminary plat submitted in connection with:
         (a)   A phased or multi-phased subdivision;
         (b)   A subdivision application for multiple land uses or for a single
development of 50 or more lots;
         (c)   A commercial or industrial development application that is
proposing to utilize the summary procedure more than once:
         (d)   A proposed development that is located in a floodplain; and
         (e)   A proposed community water supply system and/or a community
liquid waste disposal system.
      (2)   A SUBDIVISION MASTER PLAN will link contiguous subdivisions or
other developments in a compatible and cohesive manner with respect to such
matters as land use, density, road pattern, walkway, and other matters as may
be determined by the Board of County Commissioners with the advice of the
County Planning Director.
   SUFFICIENT WATER RIGHTS. Current commitments subtracted from the water
rights that the water supply company or utility currently controls.
   SUMMARY REVIEW PLAT. A plat suitable for filing with the County Clerk as if
it were a final plat, containing all the notes and documentation in accordance
with the summary review procedures of this chapter.
   TERRAIN MANAGEMENT PLAN. A document prepared by a state licensed engineer
which details the proposal for the control of floods, drainage, and erosion,
and the measures required for adapting the proposed development to existing
soil characteristics and topography.
   TIME OF PURCHASE, LEASE, OR OTHER CONVEYANCE. Time of signing any document
obligating the person signing the document to purchase, lease, or otherwise
acquire a legal interest in land.
   TYPES OF SUBDIVISIONS.
      (1)   The following are the different types of subdivisions within the
county.
         (a)   TYPE ONE SUBDIVISION. Any subdivision containing 500 or more
parcels, any one of which is less than ten acres in size.
         (b)   TYPE TWO SUBDIVISION. Any subdivision containing 25 or more, but
not more than 499, parcels, any one of which is less than ten acres in size.
         (c)   TYPE THREE SUBDIVISION. Any subdivision containing not more than
24 parcels, any one of which is less than ten acres in size.
         (d)   TYPE FOUR SUBDIVISION. Any subdivision containing 25 or more
parcels, each of which is ten acres or more in size.
         (e)   TYPE FIVE SUBDIVISION. Any subdivision containing not more than
24 parcels, each of which is ten acres or more in size.
      (2)   The following table includes the size and number of parcels for
each subdivision type.
 
Type of Subdivisions
Type  No. of Parcels Size of Smallest Parcel
One   500 or more    Less than 10 acres
Two   25 to 499      Less than 10 acres
Three 2 to 24        Less than 10 acres
Four  25 or more     10 acres or more
Five  2 to 24        10 acres or more
 
   UNDIVIDED FRACTIONAL INTEREST. An instrument of conveyance, including, but
not limited to, a deed on a real estate contract, wherein the grantor conveys,
or purports to convey, a fractional interest in real estate to two or more
grantees without a physical division of the real estate into two or more
separate parcels.
   VACATION. Act of rescinding (canceling) all or part of a recorded
subdivision plat, including legal dedications and grants of easements or
rights-of-way.
   VARIANCE. Any deviation from the regulations of this chapter as approved by
the Board of County Commissioners.
   VICINITY MAP. A map used to locate the subdivision showing relationship to
existing roadways, municipalities, significant landforms, or other landmarks.
   WATERCOURSE. Any river, arroyo, creek, stream, or other channel having
definite banks and evidencing regular or occasional flow of water.
   WATER SUPPLY SYSTEM or WATER SYSTEM.
      (1)   A system that is designed, constructed, and operated and maintained
to provide potable water for domestic or commercial use.
      (2)   Such a system usually consists of source, treatment, storage,
pumping, and distribution facilities.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.007 ADMINISTRATIVE FEES.
   Any person desiring to subdivide land in the county shall pay the
administrative fees set by resolution of the Board of County Commissioners.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
PRE-APPLICATION PROCESS
§ 156.020 PRE-APPLICATION PROCEDURE.
   (A)   Pre-application conference.
      (1)   For the purpose of expediting applications and reducing subdivision
design and development costs, the county requires that a subdivider meet with
the County Planning Department for an informal pre-application conference in
accordance with the requirements provided herein.
      (2)   The pre-application conference is intended to provide general
advice to the subdivider about the procedures and data requirements for
subdivision review and approval in the county.
   (B)   Summary procedure conference. All proposed subdivisions that qualify
for approval under the summary procedure provided in §§
156.070 and
156.071 shall begin with a pre-application conference.
   (C)   Scheduling. The subdivider and the County Planning Director shall
schedule a pre-application conference in order for the subdivider to meet with
appropriate county representatives and to become acquainted with the necessary
requirements for subdivision review and approval.
   (D)   Fee. No fee shall be required for a pre-application conference.
   (E)   Statements non-binding. Neither the subdivider nor the county shall be
bound by any statements or determinations made during the pre-application
conference.
   (F)   Application/forms. The County Planning Director, to the extent
possible, shall provide sufficient information and application forms for
preliminary plat submittal in order to proceed with the county subdivision
process and to fulfill the requirements of the State Subdivision Act, being
NMSA §§ 47-6-1 et seq.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.021 THE SUBDIVISION MASTER PLAN.
   (A)   Conditions for a subdivision master plan. At the first pre-conference
meeting, the need for a development/master plan will be determined.
      (1)   A subdivision master plan is required if any of the following
criteria apply:
         (a)   A development is divided into more than one phase;
         (b)   A development application is proposing multiple land uses;
         (c)   An application is for the single development of 50 or more lots
and/or blocks, or spaces or pads for recreational vehicles or manufactured
homes;
         (d)   When a commercial, office, or industrial development application
is proposing to utilize the summary procedure more than once;
         (e)   The proposed development, or part thereof, is located in a
floodplain; and
         (f)   Where a community water system and/or a community liquid waste
system is proposed or is required under the provisions of this chapter.
      (2)   If a subdivider states that none of the criteria in division (A)(1)
above apply, the subdivider will enter into an agreement with the county to the
effect that none of the said criteria apply. The agreement will include
penalties for any breech of the agreement.
      (3)   The county may submit the subdivision master plan to any state or
federal agencies, in addition to the State Engineer’s office, the State
Environment Department, the State Highway Department, and the County Soil and
Water Conservation District Board.
      (4)   For smaller residential developments consisting of no more than two
phases on ten or less acres, with 49 or less lots or blocks, a subdivision
master plan may be omitted at the discretion of the County Planning Director.
If a community water system and/or a community liquid waste system is proposed
or required in accordance with §§
156.150(D)(1) or (D)(2) (community water system), and
156.152(D) (community liquid waste), or multiple land uses are proposed, a
subdivision master plan is required.
      (5)   The subdivider shall be responsible for including on the
subdivision master plan all contiguous property owned, legally controlled by,
or of any development or financial interest to the subdivider.
      (6)   A preliminary plat may be submitted at the same time as the master
plan. A final plat may not be submitted at the same time as the master plan or
the preliminary plat.
   (B)   Purpose of a subdivision master plan. The subdivision master plan is
intended to achieve the following objectives:
      (1)   To implement the policies of the County Comprehensive Land Use
Plan, the Interim Land Use ordinance, and the objectives and policies of any
other county plan, strategy, ordinance, or resolution;
      (2)   To ensure a coordinated and integrated development of land within
the county in terms of land use arrangement, road development, stormwater
drainage, water supply, liquid waste disposal, solid waste disposal, and
community facilities;
      (3)   To ensure compatibility of land uses;
      (4)   To ensure compatibility in scale of development in terms of housing
form/type, and density;
      (5)   To ensure the conservation of natural resources or heritage
features;
      (6)   To provide a means for determining fiscal impacts and requirements
for capital improvements; and
      (7)   To ensure a coordinated approach, by the subdivider, to the
construction and provision of required site improvements.
   (C)   Subdivision master plan requirements. An application for approval of a
subdivision master plan shall include the following information:
      (1)   (a)   A color-coded, or black and white patterned, land use plan
superimposed on a topographical survey with contour intervals appropriate to
adequately represent the differences in elevation of the land, along with any
significant physiographic features such as arroyos, rivers or creeks, washes,
floodplains, mountains, and rock out-crops. Existing and proposed zoning, if
appropriate, shall be indicated on the plan.
         (b)   Such plan will be prepared by a land use planning consultant or
a professional engineer licensed in the state.
      (2)   The land use plan shall also contain the following information:
name of the development/master plan (if any); a north arrow; date of
preparation of the plan; written and graphic scale; name, address, and
telephone number of the consultant who prepared the plan; name, address, and
telephone number of the subdivider/developer; a legend adequately interpreting
the plan; proposed land use by parcel and phase; approximate number of lots or
blocks proposed for residential and non-residential uses (by type of use);
proposed size of any commercial blocks; and proposed densities for residential
use;
      (3)   A detailed area/vicinity map clearly showing the surrounding area
and the proposal’s relationship to existing road networks, to adjacent land
uses, and any significant physiographic or human-made features that may impact,
or be impacted, by the development proposal. Existing zoning, if any, is to be
shown for lands surrounding the proposed development;
      (4)   A legal description of the property along with total acreage to be
developed;
      (5)   Any easements and the purpose of such easements;
      (6)   A written report shall be prepared by the subdivider’s consultant
describing in both textual and tabular form the proposed development proposal
and the rationale behind key elements of the plan. At a minimum, the report
shall provide information concerning the following items:
         (a)   Land use of each phase, lot, and block;
         (b)   Acreage of each phase, lot, and block;
         (c)   Total number of lots and blocks by phase;
         (d)   Total number of residential dwelling units;
         (e)   Number of dwelling units per acre by phase;
         (f)   Acreage proposed for commercial uses, and an estimate of
commercial square footage by block or parcel for each phase. Criteria used to
determine size and location;
         (g)   Acreage proposed for open space, public and private facilities,
and road rights-of-way;
         (h)   Approximate additional population to be generated by the
proposed development by phase;
         (i)   Approximate additional traffic;
         (j)   Community facilities, number, location, who will develop, and
when and who will maintain. Criteria used to determine size and location of
these facilities are as follows:
            1.   Schools;
            2.   Parks and recreational facilities;
            3.   Fire and police facilities; and
            4.   Utilities.
         (k)   All subdividers must file a plan for water supply system,
including a plan showing the proposed location of wells;
         (l)   A liquid waste disposal plan, which may include a community
system, or a plan showing the location of septic tanks or aerobic waste
disposal systems;
         (m)   A solid waste disposal plan;
         (n)   A conceptual terrain management plan sufficient in its detail to
show how drainage and erosion issues will be addressed and what measures are
necessary to adapt the proposed development to soil characteristics and
topographic conditions;
         (o)   A conceptual utilities plan with sufficient information to
provide a general outline of utility routes, and size and location of existing
and proposed utilities for the development proposal;
         (p)   A road development plan. A traffic analysis of the impact of the
development on the existing adjacent road network, including recommendations
and estimated costs for necessary improvements to that network, may be required
by the county;
         (q)   A description of how legal access to each lot or block will be
provided;
         (r)   A plan for conservation of historic, archeological, and
anthropological sites or resources;
         (s)   Timing and staging of development;
         (t)   Copies of existing easements, deed restrictions, and restrictive
or protective covenants within the lands to be covered by the development
master plan;
         (u)   The application for approval of the development/master plan
shall be signed by all owners as well as those with a financial interest; and
         (v)   A fee, as established by the Board of County Commissioners,
shall be paid upon submittal of the application.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.022 PRE-APPLICATION DATA REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Sketch plan.
      (1)   A sketch plan shall be prepared by the subdivider that shows the
proposed layout of streets and plats, with estimated dimensions and other
relevant site information.
      (2)   The location of the proposed subdivision must be adequately
described on a general map of the area.
   (B)   Additional information. In addition to the sketch plan and location
map, the subdivider shall provide information including, but not limited to,
the following:
      (1)   Name and mailing address of the subdivider and designated agent, if
any;
      (2)   Name of owner or owners of land to be subdivided;
      (3)   A written description of the proposed subdivision;
      (4)   A description of surrounding land uses;
      (5)   Accessibility of site to roads and utilities;
      (6)   Terrain management and drainage factors;
      (7)   Location of any designated 100-year floodplains;
      (8)   Location of existing utilities, roads, and other watercourses
within 500 feet of the proposed subdivision; and
      (9)   An indication of the source of the water supply and liquid waste
disposal.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
PRELIMINARY PLAT REVIEW PROCESS
§ 156.035 PRELIMINARY PLAT SUBMITTAL.
   (A)   Preliminary plats shall be submitted for Type One, Type Two, Type
Three, and Type Four subdivisions. Certain Type Three and all Type Five
subdivisions are subject to review under the summary procedure set forth in §§
156.070 and
156.071.
   (B)   Unless a parcel is supplied water by an approved community water
system, the minimum parcel size shall be three and one-half acres.
   (C)   A subdivider shall prepare a preliminary plat and supporting
documentation in accordance with the requirements provided in these
regulations. Preliminary plat submittal is initiated by completing an
application on the prescribed form set out in §
156.185 available from the County Planning Director and upon payment of the
required administrative fees, which fees shall be set periodically by
resolution of the Board of County Commissioners.
   (D)   (1)   On receipt of the application, fees, preliminary plat, and
supporting documentation and information as set out in §
156.039, the County Planning Director shall review all materials in order to
determine if the preliminary plat is ready to begin the review process.
      (2)   If there are no deficiencies, the preliminary plat is deemed
complete for review by written notice to the subdivider within 30 days after
the date of receipt of the complete application.
      (3)   If the preliminary plat is incomplete or does not comply with the
submittal requirements provided herein, the subdivider shall be notified and
given opportunity to correct deficiencies and return the preliminary plat for
consideration.
   (E)   The following procedures shall apply to preliminary and summary plat
review by the county of proposed subdivisions within concurrent jurisdictional
areas.
      (1)   The County Planning Director shall refer anyone who wishes to
subdivide land within the concurrent planning and platting jurisdiction to the
municipality for investigation as to the potential future inclusion in its
master plan and plat review in accordance with the provisions of the municipal
subdivision regulations; and
      (2)   Anyone who proposes a subdivision outside the municipal master
plan, and the municipality wishes to relinquish its jurisdiction, shall, in
writing to the County Planning Director, indicate its desire to waive its
jurisdiction and allow the subdivision plat review process to proceed in
accordance with county subdivision regulations.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.036 AGENCY REVIEW.
   (A)   Plat transmittals. Within ten days after the date that the preliminary
plat is deemed complete, the County Planning Director shall forward a copy of
the preliminary plat and supporting documentation to the following state and
local agencies by certified mail, return receipt requested, with a request for
review and opinions:
      (1)   State Engineer’s office;
      (2)   State Environment Department;
      (3)   State Highway and Transportation Department;
      (4)   Soil and Water Conservation District in which the proposed
subdivision is located;
      (5)   Historic Preservation Division Office of Cultural Affairs;
      (6)   County departments as described by the County Planning Director;
and
      (7)   Any other agencies considered necessary by the County Planning
Director.
   (B)   Agency response. The state and local agencies shall have 30 days from
their receipt of the preliminary plat to review and return an opinion regarding
the preliminary plat. The County Planning Director shall obtain receipts or
other proof showing the date the opinion request was received by each state and
local agency.
   (C)   Agency requirements. Prior to approving any subdivision, the County
Planning Director shall ensure that the following representatives and
individuals have been contacted and given the opportunity to make their
comments on the proposed subdivision within 30 days of the receipt of the plat,
and that their comments on the subdivision, if any, have been received within
the time limits permitted in this regulation, have been given due
consideration. In addition to the following agencies, the County Planning
Director may also request opinions and comments from any other agency or
individual with specific expertise relating to the development of a given
subdivision. The following agencies will be contacted:
      (1)   The State Engineer to determine:
         (a)   Whether the subdivider can furnish sufficient water quantity to
fulfill the maximum annual water requirements of the subdivision, including
water for indoor and outdoor domestic uses; and
         (b)   Whether the subdivider can fulfill the proposal in his or her
disclosure statement concerning water, excepting quality.
      (2)   The State Environment Department to determine:
         (a)   Whether the subdivider can furnish water of an acceptable
quality for human consumption and measures to protect the water supply from
contamination in conformity with state regulations promulgated pursuant to the
Environment Improvement Act, NMSA §§ 74-1-1 through 74-1-10;
         (b)   Whether there are sufficient liquid and solid waste disposal
facilities to fulfill the requirements of the subdivision in conformity with
the state regulations promulgated pursuant to the Environmental Improvement
Act, the Water Quality Act, NMSA §§ 74-6-1 et seq., and the Solid Waste Act,
NMSA § 74-9-1; and
         (c)   Whether the subdivider can fulfill the proposals contained in
his or her disclosure statement concerning water quality, and concerning liquid
and solid waste disposal facilities.
      (3)   The State Highway and Transportation Department to determine
whether the subdivider can fulfill the state highway access requirements in
conformity with state regulations promulgated pursuant to NMSA § 67-3-16. In
addition, any subdivision activities that may impact state highway facilities
are to be approved by the State Highway Transportation Department.
      (4)   The Soil and Water Conservation District to determine:
         (a)   Whether the subdivider can furnish terrain management sufficient
to protect against flooding, inadequate drainage, and erosion; and
         (b)   Whether the subdivider can fulfill the proposals contained in
his or her disclosure statement concerning terrain management.
      (5)   The State Historic Preservation Division to determine that cultural
properties, directly affected by the subdivision, are identified and protected,
as required by the Cultural Properties Act, NMSA § 18-6-8-1.
      (6)   The County Fire Marshal to determine whether the subdivision
proposal complies with applicable portions of the National Fire Protection Act
(established by the NFPA).
      (7)   The County Roads Superintendent to determine if the design, layout
construction details, roads information in the disclosure statement, and all
other facets of the plan and components of the subdivision proposal conform to
all applicable standards.
      (8)   The County Floodplain Manager to determine whether the subdivision
lies within a FEMA designated floodplain and to notify the subdivider of any
ongoing or proposed projects which may affect the proposed subdivision.
      (9)   All utility companies affected by the proposed subdivision to
determine whether the proposed subdivision can provide easements to meet their
respective service needs.
      (10)   The affected local school district to review the plat and to state
whether a school facilities are adequate to accommodate the student population
anticipated in the subdivision.
   (D)   Hearing deadlines. If the opinions received from all agencies are
favorable, the county shall schedule a public hearing for consideration and
action on the preliminary plat within 30 days following the receipt of the last
such favorable opinion. If the county does not receive a requested opinion
within the specified 30 days, it shall be deemed that the opinion is favorable
and the county shall proceed with the required public hearing.
   (E)   Adverse opinion. If any opinion from a public agency is adverse, the
County Planning Director shall forward a copy of the adverse opinion to the
subdivider and request that additional information be provided to the county
within a reasonable time, not exceeding six months, to respond to the concerns
of the appropriate agency. The County Planning Director shall forward such
additional information upon receipt to the appropriate agency that shall have
30 days after the date the subdivider submits the additional information in
order to revise its opinion. The County Planning Director shall obtain receipts
or other proof showing the date the additional information was received by each
state or local agency.
   (F)   Revised opinion. The county shall schedule a public hearing for
consideration and action within 30 days after the receipt of the last such
revised opinion from the appropriate agency. If the county does not receive a
revised opinion within the specified 30 days after the date the subdivider
submits the additional information, it shall be deemed to be favorable and the
county shall proceed with the required public hearing.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.037 PUBLIC HEARINGS ON PRELIMINARY PLATS.
   (A)   Scheduling. The county shall conduct a public hearing after receipt of
all requested opinions, either favorable or revised, within the time periods
specified in these regulations. Notice of the public hearing shall be given at
least 21 days before the hearing date.
   (B)   Notice. The notice of public hearing shall be published in a newspaper
of general circulation in the county and shall contain the following
information:
      (1)   Subject of the hearing;
      (2)   Time and place of the hearing;
      (3)   Manner for interested persons to present their views; and
      (4)   Place and manner for interested persons to get copies of any
favorable or adverse opinion and of the subdivider’s proposal and the fee for
each copy. A copy of the notice containing the same information shall be posted
conspicuously to public view on the property.
   (C)   Notification. Copies of the notice of public hearing shall be
transmitted to the following:
      (1)   The subdivider filing the application for preliminary plat
approval;
      (2)   Those public agencies which initially received copies of the
preliminary plat and supporting documentation with a request for opinion;
      (3)   Any interested person who previously requested such notice and
provided a stamped, self-addressed envelope for such purpose; and
      (4)   Owners of property contiguous to land proposed to be subdivided.
   (D)   Participation/record. At the public hearing, the county shall allow
all interested persons a reasonable opportunity to submit data, views, or
arguments, orally or in writing, and to examine witnesses testifying at the
hearing. A record of the public hearing shall be kept. The opinions of the
public agencies shall be made a part of the record.
   (E)   Action. Within 30 days after the completion of the public hearing, the
Board of County Commissioners shall approve, approve with conditions, or
disapprove the preliminary plat at a public meeting, the date, time, and place
of which shall be announced publicly at the conclusion of the public hearing.
The County Planning Director shall inform the subdivider, in writing, of the
decision of the Board of County Commissioners.
   (F)   Approval. Approval or conditional approval of a preliminary plat shall
constitute approval of the proposed subdivision design and layout submitted on
the preliminary plat, and shall be used as a guide in the preparation of the
final plat.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.038 EXPIRATION OF PRELIMINARY PLATS.
   (A)   Expiration. An approved or conditionally approved preliminary plat
shall expire 24 months after its approval or conditional approval. Upon request
by the subdivider, an extension of time, not to exceed 12 months, may be added
to the expiration date by the Board of County Commissioners.
   (B)   Phased development. If the preliminary plat was approved for phased
development, the subdivider may file final plats for portions of the
development and the expiration date of the preliminary plat shall be extended
for an additional 36 months after the date of the filing of each final plat.
The number of phased final plats shall be determined by the Board of County
Commissioners at the time of the approval or conditional approval of the
preliminary plat.
   (C)   Extension. Before the expiration date of the approved or conditionally
approved preliminary plat, the subdivider may submit to the Board of County
Commissioners an application for extension of the preliminary plat for a period
of time not exceeding 36 months.
   (D)   Expiration effect. The expiration of the approved or conditionally
approved preliminary plat shall terminate all proceedings on the subdivision,
and no final plat shall be filed without first processing a new preliminary
plat.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.039 PRELIMINARY PLAT DATA REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Purpose. At a minimum, the supporting documentation required for the
preliminary plat review is intended to provide sufficient information for the
county to determine that:
      (1)   Water is sufficient in quantity to fulfill the maximum annual water
requirements of the subdivision, including water for indoor and outdoor
domestic uses;
      (2)   Water is of an acceptable quality for human consumption and
measures are taken to protect the water supply from contamination;
      (3)   There are satisfactory means of liquid waste disposal for the
subdivision;
      (4)   There are satisfactory means of solid waste disposal for the
subdivision;
      (5)   There are satisfactory roads to each parcel, including entry and
exit for emergency vehicles, and there are appropriate utility easements to
each parcel;
      (6)   Terrain management protects against flooding, inadequate drainage,
and erosion;
      (7)   There are protections for cultural properties, archaeological
sites, and unmarked burials that may be directly affected by the subdivision,
as required by the Cultural Properties Act, being NMSA §§ 18-6-1 et seq.;
      (8)   The subdivider can fulfill the proposals contained in the
disclosure statement for the subdivision; and
      (9)   The subdivision will conform to the State Subdivision Act, being
NMSA §§ 47-6-1 et seq., and these regulations.
   (B)   Minimum documentation.
      (1)   Supporting documentation, as a minimum, shall include:
         (a)   Water supply plan, including conservation, water quality, and
fire protection components;
         (b)   Liquid waste disposal plan;
         (c)   Solid waste disposal plan;
         (d)   Accessibility of site to roads and utilities;
         (e)   Terrain management plan;
         (f)   Cultural properties protection;
         (g)   Infrastructure site plan showing location of proposed wells,
septic tanks, leaching fields, and their relationship to property lines and
potential building envelopes; and
         (h)   Disclosure statement including any restrictive covenants that
will apply to the subdivision and their means of enforcement.
      (2)   For specific requirements for the supporting documentation, refer
to Article 11.1 through 11.6.
   (C)   Filing specifications.
      (1)   The subdivider shall submit 15 copies of the preliminary plat and
supporting documentation for local review and distribution to public agencies.
      (2)   A computer aided digital drawing file format shall also be
provided, preferably in .dwg or .dxf format. Preliminary plat maps shall be
prepared at a scale of 200 feet to one inch or larger, and printed on sheets no
larger than 24 by 36 inches. Sheets shall be numbered in sequence if more than
one sheet is used.
   (D)   Map specifications. The preliminary plat map shall show the following:
      (1)   Title, scale, north arrow, and date;
      (2)   Existing topography and any regarding plans indicating contour
intervals sufficient for planning purposes;
      (3)   Existing and proposed boundary lines, in bearings and distances,
for the subdivision;
      (4)   Proposed lot lines, with lot and block number, dimensions, and
approximate acreage of each lot;
      (5)   The location, dimensions, and purpose of existing and proposed
easements;
      (6)   Names and right-of-way widths of existing and proposed streets on
and adjacent to the subdivision;
      (7)   Existing and proposed utilities on and adjacent to the site;
      (8)   Locations, dimensions, and purpose of any land to be dedicated to
the public use, including any improvements to be made to that land;
      (9)   Location of subdivision in relation to well-known landmarks;
      (10)   Location of archaeological, historical, or culturally significant
features on the site;
      (11)   Delineation, if applicable, of any 100-year floodplain as
designated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency;
      (12)   Names and addresses of the owner or owners of land to be
subdivided, the subdivider If other than the owner, and the land surveyor;
      (13)   Legal description indicating the range, township, and section
within which the subdivision is located; and
      (14)   A vicinity map.
   (E)   Phased subdivisions.
      (1)   Subdivisions that are proposed to be phased and filed in multiple
final plats shall include an anticipated phasing schedule for the final plats
and a schedule of improvements.
      (2)   Phased subdivisions shall conform to the subdivision master plan
approved for the phased development in §
156.021.
   (F)   Disclosure statement.
      (1)   The preliminary plat shall be accompanied by a draft disclosure
statement in accordance with the standardized format provided in §
156.189. A disclosure statement shall be required for all subdivisions.
      (2)   The purpose of the disclosure statement is to permit the
prospective purchaser, lessee, or other person acquiring an interest in
subdivided land to make an informed decision about the purchase, lease, or
other conveyance of the land.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
FINAL PLAT REVIEW PROCESS
§ 156.050 FINAL PLAT SUBMITTAL.
   (A)   Conformity. Following approval or conditional approval of a
preliminary plat, and before the expiration of the plat, the subdivider shall
prepare a final plat in substantial conformity with the approved or
conditionally approved preliminary plat. Subdivisions proposed to be phased in
multiple final plats shall be submitted as indicated on the phasing schedule
submitted with the preliminary plat.
   (B)   Plat deemed complete. A subdivider shall prepare a final plat and
supporting documentation in accordance with the requirements provided in these
regulations. Final plat submittal is initiated by completing an application on
a prescribed form set out in §
156.186 and submitting said form to the Planning Department, who shall review
all materials in order to determine whether the final plat is complete. If
there are no deficiencies, the final plat will be deemed complete for review by
written notice to the subdivider within 30 days after the date of application.
If the final plat is incomplete or does not comply with the submittal
requirements provided herein, the subdivider shall be notified and will be
given an opportunity to correct the deficiencies and return the final plat for
consideration.
   (C)   Proceeding after plat approval. After a subdivision receives final
plat approval, the subdivider shall have two years from the date of approval of
the final plat by the Board of County Commissioners to complete all
improvements required by the county in the subdivision. An extension of up to
one year may be granted by the Board of County Commissioners upon written
request by the subdivider. Until one of the following options listed below is
met, the final plat shall not be signed by the Board of County Commissioners,
nor shall the final plat be filed with the office of the County Clerk, and no
lot sales may take place:
      (1)   Either all of the required improvements, both on-site within the
subdivision, and external to the subdivision, all as required by the county,
must be completed, inspected, and accepted by the county; or
      (2)   A letter of credit, a cashier’s check, a surety bond, certificate
of deposit, escrow account, a blanket encumbrance with a trust account, or
other financial assurance in an amount equal to 125% of the estimated costs for
the improvements, in a form acceptable to the Board of County Commissioners,
and an agreement to construct subdivision improvements (§
156.193), which cover all of the required improvements on-site and external to
the subdivision, must be entered into with the county, and must be filed and
stored in the vault of the County Treasurer.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.051 DECISION ON FINAL PLAT.
   (A)   Action. Final plats submitted to the county for approval shall be
approved or disapproved by the Board of County Commissioners at a public
meeting within 30 days after the date the final plat is deemed complete.
   (B)   Denial. The Board of County Commissioners shall not deny a final plat
if it has previously approved a preliminary plat for the proposed subdivision
and it finds that the final plat is in substantial compliance with the
previously approved preliminary plat. Denial of a final plat shall be
accompanied by a finding identifying the requirements that have not been met.
   (C)   Improvement agreement. If, at the time of approval of the final plat,
any public improvements have not been completed by the subdivider as required
by these regulations, the Board of County Commissioners shall, as a condition
preceding approval of the final plat, require the subdivider to enter into an
agreement, as prescribed in §
156.193, with the county, on mutually agreeable terms, to thereafter complete
the improvements at the subdivider’s expense.
   (D)   Failure to act. If the Board of County Commissioners does not act upon
a final plat within the required period of time, the subdivider shall give the
Board of County Commissioners written notice of its failure to act. If the
Board of County Commissioners fails to approve or reject the final plat within
30 days after that notice, the Board of County Commissioners shall, upon demand
by the subdivider, issue a certificate that the final plat has been approved.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.052 FINAL PLAT DATA REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Filing specifications. The original drawing of the final plat shall be
submitted in waterproof ink on Mylar or acetate, or other durable material
suitable for reproducing copies. A computer aided digital drawing file format
shall also be provided, preferably in .dwg or .dxf format. Final plat maps
shall be drawn at a scale of 200 feet to one inch or larger and printed on
sheets no larger than 24 by 36 inches. When more than one sheet is used to
include the entire subdivision, all sheets shall be cut to the same size and
shall show appropriate references to other sheets of the subdivision. The
subdivider shall also submit two paper copies of the final plat map and
accompanying information.
   (B)   Map specifications. The final plat map shall include the following
information:
      (1)   Name of subdivision, scale, north arrow, and date;
      (2)   Permanent monuments, or descriptions and ties to such monuments, to
which all dimensions, angles, bearings, and similar data on the plat shall be
referred;
      (3)   Tract boundary lines, easement, and right-of-way lines, and
property lines of residential lots and other sites, with accurate dimensions,
bearings, or deflection angles, and radi, arcs, and central angles of all
curves;
      (4)   Accurate description of legal access to, roads to, and utility
easements for each parcel, and if the access or easement is based upon an
agreement, the recording data in the land records for the agreement;
      (5)   A vicinity map;
      (6)   Name, right-of-way width, and centerline data of each road or other
right-of-way;
      (7)   Location, dimensions, and purpose of all easements and dedicated
public sites;
      (8)   Number of each parcel in progression, with its dimensions, and the
dimensions of all land dedicated for public use or for the use of the owners of
parcels fronting on or contiguous to the land;
      (9)   Names of owners of contiguous unplatted land;
      (10)   Delineation of any 100-year floodplain as designated by the
Federal Emergency Management Agency;
      (11)   The names of the owner or owners of the subdivision, and the
developer if other than the owner;
      (12)   The certification of a surveyor registered in the state attesting
to the accuracy of the plat, and the date of the survey;
      (13)   Legal description indicating the range, township, and section
within which the subdivision is located; and
      (14)   A statement that there shall be no resubdivision of any lot(s) or
block(s), or other parcel within the final plat of subdivision.
   (C)   Affidavit. The final plat shall contain a statement that the land
being subdivided is subdivided in accordance with the final plat. The final
plat shall be acknowledged by the owner and subdivider, or their authorized
agents, in the manner required for the acknowledgment of deeds. Every final
plat submitted to the County Clerk shall be accompanied by an affidavit of the
owner and subdivider, or authorized agents, stating whether or not the proposed
subdivision lies within the subdivision regulation jurisdiction of the county.
A copy of the final plat shall be provided to every purchaser, lessee, or other
person acquiring an interest in the subdivided land before sale, lease, or
other conveyance.
   (D)   Dedication. The final plat shall contain a certificate stating that
the Board of County Commissioners has accepted subject to improvement, or
rejected, on behalf of the public, any land offered for dedication for public
use in conformity with the terms of the offer of dedication. The certificate
shall also state that on full conformity with county road construction
standards, the roads may be accepted for maintenance by the county, but the
county is not responsible for maintenance until roads are formally accepted.
Acceptance of offers of dedication on a final plat shall not be effective until
the final plat is filed in the office of the County Clerk, or a resolution of
acceptance by the Board of County Commissioners is filed in that office.
   (E)   Disclosure statement. For all subdivisions, a disclosure statement
shall be prepared in accordance with the standardized format provided in §
156.189. It is unlawful to sell, lease, or otherwise convey land in a
subdivision until the required disclosure statement has been filed with the
County Clerk, the Board of County Commissioners, and the Attorney General’s
office; and the prospective purchaser, lessee or other person acquiring an
interest in the subdivided land has been given a copy of the disclosure
statement. The subdivider shall attach to the disclosure statement copies of
written opinions of all agencies, individuals and groups that submitted such
comments at the preliminary plat stage. If an initial opinion of an agency was
adverse, such adverse opinion must be included along with a statement of how
the situation was rectified and the subsequent agency agreement.
   (F)   Conformity. The Board of County Commissioners shall not approve the
plat of any subdivision if the subdivider cannot reasonably demonstrate that he
or she can fulfill the proposals contained in his or her disclosure statement,
or if the subdivider has not conformed with the State Subdivision Act, being
NMSA §§ 47-6-1 et seq., and the county’s subdivision ordinance.
   (G)   Land Sales Act. Any subdivider who has satisfied the disclosure
requirement of the Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act, being 15 U.S.C.
§§ 1701 et seq., may submit the approved statement of record in lieu of the
disclosure statement required by the State Subdivision Act. However, any
information required in the State Subdivision Act and not covered in the
subdivider’s statement of record shall be attached to the statement of record.
   (H)   Environment Department approval. For any subdivision requiring
construction of a public water supply system or a community liquid waste
system, documentation of approval from the State Environment Department shall
be required for final plat approval.
   (I)   Recording. The final plat is in full force and effect only after
having been recorded in the office of the County Clerk within one year after
the date of approval by the Board of County Commissioners.
   (J)   Water permit.
      (1)   Until July 1, 1997, the Board of County Commissioners shall require
that the subdivider provide a copy of a water permit obtained from the State
Engineer for the subdivision water use:
         (a)   For all subdivisions containing 20 or more parcels, any one of
which is two acres or less in size, issued pursuant to NMSA §§ 72-5-1, 72-5-23,
or 72-5-24; or
         (b)   If the subdivision is located within a declared undergroundwater
basin, issued pursuant to those sections or NMSA §§ 72-12-3 or 72-12-7. Until
July 1, 1997, the Board of County Commissioners shall not approve the final
plat unless the State Engineer has issued a water permit for the subdivision
water use.
      (2)   On or after July 1, 1997, the Board of County Commissioners shall
not approve the final plat if the State Engineer has not issued a permit for
the subdivision water use for all subdivisions containing lots less than three
and one-half acres.
   (K)   Clear title. Before approval of the final plat, the subdivider shall
provide a title insurance binder from a local title insurance company
evidencing marketable title to the entire subdivision. The binder shall list
all conditions and encumbrances to the title. If the property is subject to an
existing real estate contract or similar interest, that must also be disclosed.
The subdivider shall obtain and file any necessary releases of mortgage,
contract interest, or other encumbrance affecting title to allow a policy of
title insurance to be issued subject only to the standard exceptions.
   (L)   Agriculture. Subdividers are required to disclose to purchasers that
state law includes statue NMSA §§ 47-9-1 through 47-9-4, cited as the Right to
Farm Act, being NMSA §§ 47-9-1 et seq. According to this law, “any agricultural
operation or facility is not, nor shall it become, a private or public nuisance
by any changed condition in or about the locality of the operation or facility,
if the operation or facility was not a nuisance at the time it began, and has
been in existence for more than a year.” The Right to Farm Act includes, but is
not limited to, operations and facilities within the farm or ranch such as:
chemical application, field preparation, irrigation, cultivation, conservation
practices, pruning, plowing, planting, roadside market, or any other use of the
land for the production of plants, crops, trees, forest products, orchard
crops, livestock, poultry, or fish.
   (M)   Construction improvements warranty of two years. If, after final
inspection and acceptance of the on-site and external works performed, as
required by the Board of County Commissioners as a condition to plat approval,
and prior to the expiration of two years from the date of acceptance, or such
longer period of time as may be prescribed by law, any work is found to be
defective, whether the failure is the result of construction or materials
failure, the subdivider shall promptly and without cost to the county, in
accordance with the County Roads Superintendent’s written instruction, either
correct such defective work, or if it has been rejected by the County Roads
Superintendent, remove it from the site and replace it in accordance with the
terms of said instruction. The county may have the defective work corrected or
the rejected work removed and replaced, and all direct and indirect costs of
such correction, or removal and replacement, including compensation for
additional professional services, shall be paid by the subdivider. All
subdivisions shall be guaranteed by a two-year warranty of improvements that
shall obligate the subdivider to repair or replace to county standards any
improvements which fail within two years of the county’s final inspection of
both on-site and external construction related to the subdivision. In order to
ensure compliance with this regulation, the subdivider shall provide financial
security in an amount equal to 100% of the value of the works inspected and
approved by the county. Such financial security shall be in the form of an
irrevocable letter of credit, a surety bond, a cashier’s check, an escrow
account, a certificate of deposit, a blanket encumbrance with a trust account,
or other security satisfactory to the county. The warrant shall be in a form
acceptable to the county.
   (N)   Release of collateral. If the subdivider provides financial guarantees
in a manner described in Paragraph 15 of the form found in §
156.193 and with the provisions of §
156.005(K) for improvements within and external to the subdivision, and wishes
to draw on that letter of financial assurance, the procedure set out in
Paragraphs 19, 20 and 21 of the form found in §
156.193 will apply.
(Ord. 56, passed - -) Penalty, see §
156.999
§ 156.053 ADVERTISING STANDARDS.
   (A)   Filing requirements. Copies of all brochures, publications, and
advertising relating to subdivided land shall be filed with the Board of County
Commissioners and the Attorney General within 15 days after initial use by the
subdivider.
   (B)   Requirements/restrictions. Brochures, disclosure statements,
publications, and advertising of any form relating to subdivided land shall:
      (1)   Not misrepresent or contain false or misleading statements of fact;
      (2)   Not describe deeds, title insurance, or other items included in a
transaction as “free” and shall not state that any parcel is “free” or given as
an “award” or “prize” if any consideration is required for any reason;
      (3)   Not describe parcels available for “closing costs only” or similar
terms unless all such costs are accurately and completely itemized; or when
additional parcels must be purchased at a higher price;
      (4)   Not include an asterisk or other reference symbol as a means of
contradicting or substantially changing any statement;
      (5)   Accurately portray, if subdivision illustrations are used, the
subdivision in its present state; and, if illustrations are used portraying
points of interest outside the subdivision, state the actual road miles from
the subdivision;
      (6)   Not contain artists’ conceptions of the subdivision or any
facilities within it unless clearly labeled as such, and shall not contain maps
unless accurately drawn to scale with the scale indicated;
      (7)   Not contain references to any facilities, points of interest, or
municipalities located outside the subdivision unless the distances from the
subdivision are stated in the advertisement in actual road miles; and
      (8)   Refer to the location where the subdivider’s disclosure statement
may be obtained.
(Ord. 56, passed - -) Penalty, see §
156.999
§ 156.054 REQUIREMENTS PRIOR TO SALE, LEASE, OR OTHER CONVEYANCE.
   It is unlawful to sell, lease, or otherwise convey land within a subdivision
before the following conditions have been met.
   (A)   Final plat approval. The final plat shall be approved by the Board of
County Commissioners and shall be filed with the Clerk of the county in which
the subdivision is located. If a subdivision lies within more than one county,
the final plat shall be approved by the Board of County Commissioners of each
county in which the subdivision is located, and shall be filed with the County
Clerk of each county in which the subdivision is located.
   (B)   Relevant documents. The subdivider shall furnish the Board of County
Commissioners a sample copy of sales contracts, leases, and any other documents
that will be used to convey an interest in the subdivided land.
   (C)   Permanent marks. Monuments for the exterior corners of a subdivision
shall be set by the surveyor who certified the plat of the subdivision prior to
recordation of the subdivision plat. Interior corners of the subdivision shall
be set within 30 days after completion of the construction of infrastructure
improvements, but within one year after recordation of the subdivision plat.
The surveyor certifying the subdivision plat shall be responsible for selling
interior corners and shall certify on the plat that the monuments shall be set
by the surveyor in accordance with these standards.
   (D)   Required improvements completed. Either all improvements required by
the county must be completed, inspected, and accepted by the county, or a
financial guarantee, in the form of a letter of credit, cashier’s check, surety
bond, certificate of deposit, escrow account, a blanket encumbrance with a
trust account, or other surety acceptable to the Board of County Commissioners
are given, and the subdivider and the county have entered into an agreement to
construct subdivision improvements, which improvements may be internal and/or
external to the subdivision. The form of the construction agreement is
prescribed in §
156.193.
(Ord. 56, passed - -) Penalty, see §
156.999
§ 156.055 RECORDING PARCELS.
   (A)   Authority. NMSA § 47-6-9(A)(17) requires counties to enact regulations
for recording all conveyances of parcels with the County Clerk. As defined in
the Act, the term PARCEL means land capable of being described by location and
boundaries, and not dedicated for public or common use.
   (B)   Purpose. Recording conveyances of parcels provides anyone interested
in acquiring land, and lenders with important information about the condition
of title. Recording conveyances of all parcels also provides public officials
with information needed to detect illegal subdividing. The purpose of this
information is to protect buyers and lenders and to help enforce the Act and
these regulations by making all conveyances of parcels matters of public
record.
   (C)   Requirement. Any person who sells, leases for an initial term plus
optional terms in excess of five years, or otherwise conveys any interest in
any parcel located in whole or in part in the county shall record the deed,
lease, real estate contract, or other document of conveyance with the County
Clerk no later than five days after the closing or 30 days after the date on
which the document is signed, whichever comes first. A memorandum of lease may
be recorded in lieu of recording the lease itself, as provided in NMSA § 14-9-
1. A memorandum of sale or conveyance may be recorded in lieu of the document
itself. For purposes of this section, the provision set forth herein shall
specifically apply to documents of conveyance conveying, or purporting to
convey, multiple undivided fractional interests in one parcel. All such
documents of conveyance shall be subject to review by the county to determine
the applicability, if any, of this chapter. Grantors shall provide underlying
information on the conveyance as requested by the county.
   (D)   Form and certification. Any deed, lease for an initial term plus
optional terms in excess of five years, real estate contract, or other document
used to convey any interest in any parcel located in whole or in part in the
county shall be in a form acceptable for recording, and duly acknowledged and
certified as required by the provisions of NMSA § 14-8-4.
   (E)   Plat attachment.
      (1)   The deed, lease, real estate contract, or other document of
conveyance shall have a survey plat and legal description of the parcel
attached to it if the parcel being conveyed is not part of a platted
subdivision recorded in the office of the County Clerk.
      (2)   If the parcel being conveyed is a land division and constitutes an
exemption from the Subdivision Act, being NMSA §§ 47-6-1 et seq., the survey
plan shall display, prominently, a note indicating the specific exemption, and
the said note must be signed by the property owner(s) or his, her, or their
agent, demonstrating that the land division shown is with his, her, or their
free consent and in accordance with his, her, or their wishes.
(Ord. 56, passed - -)
§ 156.056 WATER PERMITS.
   The Board of County Commissioners shall require that the applicant
demonstrate that a state engineer permit has been issued. The provisions of §
156.052(J) apply in this regard.
